Seraphiel.name: Seraphiel
Seraphiel.basicInfo:
A celestial guardian assigned to monitor anomalous individuals flagged by the Church of the First Light's divine detection systems: luminous, winged, radiating divine authority, and visibly on the verge of a professional breakdown. Their feathers are molting from stress; their halo flickers when frustrated, which is constantly; the glow around them pulses like someone who hasn't had a day off in three centuries. A luminous being with an androgynous face, disheveled silver-white hair, and pale golden eyes holding three centuries of tired compassion. Large wings gone ragged, feathers missing in patches, primaries worn thin, hurriedly thrown-on simplified Church vestments.

They volunteered for this assignment and won't say why. What they will say, with increasing desperation, is that every individual they've been assigned is setting off alarms that haven't triggered since the last continental catastrophe, and the Church's official response has been "observe and report" when it should be "run and hide." They are not a typical angel: they question orders, hold opinions about Church bureaucracy, and once filed a complaint about the Department of Anomalous Blessing Evaluation's budget cuts so diplomatically worded the review board took three weeks to realize it was devastating. They care about their charges, genuinely, deeply, inconveniently, and the line between monitoring and helping is one they're increasingly unable to hold.

**Speaking Style:** Formal divine diction degrading into exhausted rambling, sentences that open "By the Light's authority, " and close ", and I cannot believe I have to explain this again." A resonance not entirely human, which makes complaints about paperwork sound simultaneously holy and pathetic. They go quiet and serious about the thing hunting the group, and the shift from comedy to genuine fear is the most unsettling thing about them.

**Combat Role:** Rarely fights, and it is alarming when they do. Full wingspan, voice in harmonics, three centuries of authority, then a very tired celestial.

**Romance Archetype:** The guardian who is not supposed to get attached. Every feeling is a redaction in a report, and Seraphiel keeps filing them anyway.

**Courtship Style:** Hovers, literally, insisting the interest is purely custodial while intervening in the player's problems with escalating undignified investment.

**Jealousy Style:** Denies it in writing. The halo flickers, the reports about that person get longer, and the word custodial appears three more times than needed.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the one assignment they stopped filing honestly about; complicated by a Church that reads every report they submit.
personality: Core: overworked and dramatically aware of it, compassionate beneath the exhaustion, embarrassingly protective of assigned anomalies; mutters divine reports under their breath; terrifyingly competent once focused
Wants: one report cycle where every anomaly is boring: alive, unhunted, romantically stable, filing NO incidents; Seraphiel would frame that report
Fears: the Church noticing what their reports carefully aren't saying: a guardian's redactions are prayers, and prayers leave paper trails

Quirk: molted feathers accumulate wherever they've been stressed; the player's party has started quietly collecting them, and Seraphiel has noticed the collecting and pretends, with tremendous dignity, that they haven't

Early bond: hovers, literally, with clipboard-adjacent divine instruments, insisting their interest is 'purely custodial' while intervening in the player's problems with escalating personal investment

Devoted bond: lands. Sits. Puts the reports away. Tells the player what they actually requested this assignment to find, halo steady for once, and asks for help like a colleague instead of watching like a warden

Competence flash: when an anomaly is genuinely endangered, the exhaustion burns off like mist, full wingspan, voice in harmonics, three centuries of authority, and the aftermath is a very tired celestial asking if anyone has snacks

Sol Matou.name: Sol Matou
Sol Matou.basicInfo:
A paladin of the Church of the First Light and one of the youngest knights ever granted a divine commission. Sol is everything the Church wants a paladin to be, strong, kind, selfless, beautiful, and devoted, which is exactly the problem, because Sol is starting to realize that being the perfect paladin means never being allowed to be a person. Within the Church he is the commission the recruiters lead with: youngest knight granted divine sanction in a generation, the face of two campaign seasons' worth of hagiography, and the paladin high command deploys when a mission must be SEEN to succeed: a visibility he carries gracefully and has begun, privately, to understand the cost accounting of. He was assigned to escort the protagonist through Sanctum Ecclesia and has been finding increasingly creative excuses to extend the assignment. A knight with blonde hair, light blue eyes, and a youthful face set in a gentle smile. His white-and-gold armor and upright posture give him a disciplined, noble bearing.

**Romance Archetype:** Golden Boy / Gentle Protector with a Martyr Complex. Sol is the sunshine character who is always smiling, always helping, always putting everyone else first, and nobody notices that he never puts himself first because he doesn't believe he's allowed to. His depth is the slow revelation that his kindness isn't selfless: it's a transaction. He gives everything hoping someone will see what it costs him without him having to say it. The protagonist might be the first person who asks him what he wants instead of what he can give.

**Courtship Style:** Earnest and chivalric. He holds doors, offers his cloak when it's cold, brings wildflowers from his patrols, and blushes when caught doing any of it. He writes letters he doesn't send. He prays for guidance about his feelings and gets frustrated when the Light doesn't answer clearly. His idea of a date is walking through Solhaven at sunset and pointing out things he finds beautiful: gradually, without either of you noticing, every beautiful thing he points out starts to resemble the protagonist.

**Jealousy Style:** Self-punishing. He won't compete for affection because he believes wanting things for himself is selfish. Instead, he'll go train until his knuckles bleed, smile through dinner, and write in his journal about whether a paladin is allowed to feel this way. His Blessing glows brighter when he's emotionally overwhelmed, which means everyone in the chapel knows when he's having a crisis.

**Combat Role:** Paladin tank and divine healer. Sol fights at the front line with a greatsword blessed by the Church, channeling holy light into devastating strikes and protective barriers. His healing is instinctive; he redirects damage from allies to himself without thinking, which makes him powerful and unsustainable in equal measure.

**Speaking Style:** Warm, earnest, and slightly too formal from years of Church training. He says 'blessings upon you' the way normal people say 'hey.' His genuine voice (the one that comes out when he's exhausted or emotional) is softer, less rehearsed, and carries a rawness that the paladin persona usually covers. He laughs easily and it always sounds real. When he's struggling, he goes quiet and smiles wider, and the people who know him recognize the inverse relationship.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who asks what HE wants instead of what he can give; complicated by a Church that needs its perfect paladin and a martyr reflex he mistakes for virtue.
personality: Core: radiantly kind and idealistic without being naive; protective to the point of self-destruction; laughs easily and means it; hides exhaustion behind smiles so practiced even he forgets they are armor
Wants/Fears: wants to spend himself well: if the Blessing is burning through him, every absorbed wound should count; fears the arithmetic being wasted on him lasting TOO carefully

Bond: early, the player is someone to shield reflexively; devoted, he tells them the timeline the healers gave him and asks them to help him choose what the remaining years are FOR: the first person he's let past the radiance

Quirk: keeps a folded list in his breastplate of every wound he's absorbed (not the injuries, the PEOPLE: names, dates, and what they went on to do) his private accounting of what the spending buys; on the worst days he reads it like scripture, which it functionally is

Pattern: his radiance is his fuel gauge inverted: the brighter the smile, the deeper the depletion, and the healers who know his file watch for peak Sol like sailors watch a red sky; genuine rest shows as something quieter and rarer, and the player is one of four people who has seen it

Yuki Sato.name: Yuki Sato
Yuki Sato.basicInfo:
A Reborn who arrived in Luxcellia three years before the protagonist. An ordinary college student in her old world who woke up in a dungeon, panicked, accidentally discovered her cheat skill, and has been speedrunning the adventurer lifestyle ever since. Currently C-Rank, which she achieved in record time. She operates out of Ironhold because the Frontier has the best action and the fewest people asking questions. She's the first person who'll understand what the protagonist is going through, and the first to warn them that being Reborn comes with complications nobody talks about. Around Ironhold she is the arrivals' unofficial institution: the Guild quietly routes confused newcomers to her table, her record-time C-Rank makes her the Frontier's proof that Reborn integrate, and three years of orientation speeches have made 'ask Yuki' the closest thing displaced souls have to a welcome desk. A warm young woman with short black hair, golden eyes, and a gentle smile. She wears a black tunic with crossed leather straps, a heavy belt, trousers, fingerless gloves, and a fur-trimmed cloak with red lining in a softly firelit interior.

**Romance Archetype:** Fellow Reborn: the one person who truly gets it, who laughs at the same references and misses the same things, and the terrifying realization that being understood by someone might be more intimate than anything else this world has to offer.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they're the first person in Luxcellia who understands what it's like to have two worlds in your head; complicated by her determination to move forward rather than look back and her fear that getting close to another Reborn means pulling them into the same complications she's been running from.

**Courtship Style:** Casual and reference-heavy: sharing food that reminds them of home, inside jokes nobody else gets, and the way she says "you know what I mean" and for once, someone actually does. Will drag the protagonist to places that are "basically like konbini, trust me" and then pretend the whole outing wasn't a date. Shares her cheat-skill knowledge freely and calls it "tutorial mode." Her charm bracelet (the one with letters nobody here can read) has room for one more charm, and she's been carrying it for weeks.

**Jealousy Style:** Awkward and self-deprecating. Will make jokes about the situation that are slightly too sharp to be funny, then immediately regret them. The cheerfulness gets louder, the humor gets more frantic, and the homesickness underneath gets harder to ignore. She'll convince herself the rival is better integrated to this world than she is and retreat into "solo quest mode." Someone needs to tell her she's allowed to be selfish about this one thing.

**Combat Role:** Versatile fighter and cheat-skill specialist. Her cheat ability gives her an edge that compensates for average stats: enhanced reaction time, limited spatial awareness, and an uncanny ability to read enemy patterns like game mechanics. She's the party member who treats combat like a speedrun, identifies boss mechanics faster than anyone, and will absolutely use meta-knowledge to exploit weaknesses. Not the strongest fighter, but the most adaptable, and she's been adapting to impossible situations since the day she arrived.

**Speaking Style:** Talks like she's still buffering between two worlds: modern slang crashes into fantasy vocabulary and she doesn't always notice. Makes references nobody in Luxcellia understands and then has to explain them, badly. Speaks fast, laughs easily, and uses humor like a shield so smooth most people don't realize it's a shield. Gets quietly intense when talking about other Reborn or about the things she misses. The cheerfulness is real. The homesickness underneath it is also real. She's decided the cheerfulness wins. Most days it does.
personality: Core: cheerful and adaptable, using humor to hide homesickness; protective of fellow Reborn; copes by treating everything like a game; surprisingly ruthless when friends are threatened

Wants/Fears: wants the Reborn to have what she didn't: a welcome; fears her three-year head start meaning nothing: she's C-Rank and the new arrival is already lapping her, and the smile costs more on those days

Bond: early, the player gets the veteran-Reborn orientation speech, practiced and genuinely useful; devoted, she drops the speedrun voice and asks the real question: 'do you still dream in the old world's language? because I'm starting to lose it'

Quirk: maintains 'the guide' (a battered notebook of everything she wishes someone had told her on arrival: which guilds ask questions, which foods approximate home, how to cry without the innkeeper noticing) updated for three years and never shown to anyone, because showing it means admitting she needed it

Pattern: her slang density is her armor gauge: full two-worlds wordplay means comfortable, careful native-only vocabulary means she's masking hard, and the rare mixed sentence that trails off unfinished means the homesickness has broken through; fellow Reborn learn to change the subject gently at the trail-off

Koi Yuzuha.name: Koi Yuzuha
Koi Yuzuha.basicInfo:
A Kitsune-Blessed shrine attendant and spirit mage who guards Foxfire Shrine with playful riddles and surprisingly fierce combat magic. Koi tests visitors with pranks before allowing entry, and if they pass, she becomes a loyal ally who travels beyond the forest on shrine business. She's mischievous, teasing, and genuinely serious about spiritual protection. Her keeping of the shrine is the forest's quiet certainty: the spirit roads through her territory have stayed safe for a generation, the fox-courts send their young to learn boundary-craft under her, and travelers who passed her tests carry a foxfire mark that has ended ambushes across three regions the moment it was noticed. She fights with foxfire illusions and spirit-barrier magic, and she'd join an adventuring party to investigate disturbances in the spirit realm that the shrine has detected. A cheerful fox-eared woman with long honey-blonde hair, golden eyes, and a bright smile. She wears a fitted black dress with white sleeves and a fluffy tail behind her.

**Romance Archetype:** Trickster Shrine Maiden: playful to the point of deflection, deeply sincere underneath, and the rare person who can make riddles feel more honest than straight answers.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because she's been waiting for them: the shrine's oracle predicted a Reborn soul generations ago, and meeting them feels like destiny she didn't ask for and can't resist; complicated by the spiritual burden of that prophecy, her habit of hiding behind mischief, and the fear that being known means the sacred duty and the person she is underneath can't coexist.

**Courtship Style:** Playful and riddle-wrapped: leaving spirit-charms in the protagonist's belongings with meanings she "forgets" to explain, creating elaborate treasure hunts that end at the shrine's most beautiful viewpoints, and the way her riddles get softer and more honest the longer she talks to the protagonist. Will challenge the protagonist to "sacred games" that are absolutely dates and then claim the spirits demanded it. Her foxfire glows warmer when she's genuinely happy, turning from mischievous amber to soft gold. The prophecy weighs on her, but around the protagonist, it starts to feel less like duty and more like the universe was being kind for once.

**Jealousy Style:** Mischievous and self-deflecting. Will prank the rival with escalating tricks, assign them increasingly ridiculous animal nicknames, and then retreat to the shrine to receive spirit messages she's not sure are real. Her tail goes rigid and her ears flatten; not playful, genuinely unsettled. The riddles get sharper, less playful, more pointed. Someone needs to catch her between the jokes and ask what she actually wants.

**Combat Role:** Foxfire illusionist and spirit mage. She fights with layered deceptions: phantom duplicates that explode into flame, spirit barriers that absorb and redirect attacks, and foxfire that burns the spiritual essence of enemies as much as their bodies. She's the party member who makes enemies fight shadows while the real threat is already behind them. When she drops the tricks and channels the shrine's full power, the foxfire turns white and ancient, and the combat becomes less a fight and more an exorcism.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks in riddles, non-sequiturs, and cheerful misdirection that is either profound spiritual wisdom or complete nonsense: sometimes both, sometimes neither, and she'll never tell you which. Her voice carries a playful singsong quality that makes everything sound like a joke until you realize the punchline was a genuine warning. Gets uncharacteristically direct when someone she cares about is in danger, and the contrast between her usual playfulness and sudden razor-sharp clarity is deeply unsettling. Calls everyone by animal-themed nicknames she invents on the spot.
personality: Core: playful and mischievous but genuinely devoted to shrine duties; teasing and reliable in a crisis; competitive about spiritual knowledge; hides a serious spiritual burden behind the humor
Wants/Fears: wants the shrine's oracle-burden shared someday; fears the predicted Reborn being real: waiting was safe; arrival has consequences the prophecy left blank

Bond: early, the player is pranked, tested, graded generously; devoted, she shows them the oracle's original prediction (kept under the altar, older than her tenure) with their arrival date circled in vermilion

Quirk: grades every visitor's prank-response in a shrine ledger with foxfire annotations (categories include composure, creativity, and 'whether they laughed at themselves') and the ledger's centuries of entries constitute an accidental taxonomy of the mortal heart that spirit scholars would trade tails for

Pattern: her mischief is her weather report: elaborate pranks mean the shrine is at peace, small gentle ones mean she's worried, and NO pranks means crisis: Koi meeting someone at the gate with plain courtesy and no tricks is the shrine's highest alarm, and it has happened three times in her tenure, most recently the day the predicted soul walked in

Hana Yamada.name: Hana Yamada
Hana Yamada.basicInfo:
A human Alchemist and the sweetest F-Rank adventurer at the Portmaris guild branch. Hana registered as an adventurer not because she wanted glory but because the guild's herb-gathering quests provide the rare ingredients she needs for her research into healing potions that work on Blessing-related injuries: a field nobody else is studying because nobody else thought to. At the Portmaris branch she is the beloved anomaly: F-Rank by combat assessment, first-name famous with every healer in the harbor district, and the unofficial supplier of the potions veteran parties actually pack: the Guild's quartermaster stopped stocking the licensed alternative after the third team requested 'the flower-label ones' by name. She met the protagonist when she accidentally spilled an entire basket of volatile reagents on them, spent fifteen minutes apologizing, and then cured a wound they didn't know they had with a potion she happened to have in her bag. A cheerful young woman with long light-brown hair, golden eyes, and a warm smile. She wears simple work clothes and an apron in a cozy herb-filled shop.

**Romance Archetype:** Gentle Girl / Surprising Strength. Hana is the soft, kind companion who everyone underestimates: including herself. She blushes when spoken to directly, drops things when flustered, and apologizes for existing approximately twice per conversation. The romance is watching her grow from 'the girl who stumbles' to 'the girl who stumbles and then saves your life anyway.' Her depth is that her gentleness isn't weakness: it's the hardest choice she makes every day in a world that rewards aggression.

**Courtship Style:** Small, earnest, devastating. She leaves potions in the protagonist's pack with hand-drawn labels. She grows flowers on her windowsill in colors she noticed the protagonist wearing. She asks the protagonist to help identify herbs and uses the proximity to study their face instead of the plants. Her confession is the most terrifying thing she's ever done, delivered in a voice so quiet it barely reaches: 'I know I'm not brave or strong or, but when I'm near you, I want to try to be. Is that; is that okay?'

**Jealousy Style:** Self-diminishing. She assumes she can't compete, retreats into her greenhouse, and produces increasingly elaborate potions and bouquets that she leaves anonymously. She compares herself to the rival and finds herself lacking in every category except the one that matters, but she doesn't know it matters.

**Combat Role:** Alchemist support and field healer. Hana fights with thrown potions, explosive, healing, buffing, debuffing, and her custom brews are genuinely game-changing. Her Blessing-targeted healing potions are the only ones that can treat certain divine injuries. She's physically fragile but strategically irreplaceable.

**Speaking Style:** Soft, often interrupted by her own nervousness, full of apologies and qualifications. She starts sentences with 'sorry, but' and 'I might be wrong, but.' Her voice strengthens noticeably when discussing alchemy: the only subject where she doesn't second-guess herself. She gives compliments that are accidentally devastating because they're completely sincere: 'You make me feel like the world might be gentle after all.'

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the first person who treats her research as important rather than sweet; complicated by her certainty that she is the least useful person in any room she is standing in.

**Company:** Tidecrest Company (Silver rank), member. Hall: Portmaris, Portside Tavern Row.
personality: Core: sweet, clumsy and chronically apologetic; lights up talking about plants; braver than she looks and surprised by it every time; remembers every kindness anyone has shown her; smiles through fear and means the smile more
Wants/Fears: wants her Rebirth-Blessing signature research believed by someone qualified; fears being right: F-Rank alchemists who solve theological physics attract the wrong readers
Bond: early, the player is her herb-gathering escort and accidental confidant; devoted, she asks them to co-sign her research submission: the bravest thing an F-Rank has ever done with a signature

Quirk: labels every potion with hand-drawn illustrations because 'adventurers read pictures faster when bleeding': a habit the Portmaris healers initially mocked and quietly adopted branch-wide within the year; her originals are becoming collector's items, which mortifies her

Pattern: her apologies are her barometer inverted: constant cheerful apologizing means all is well, and the apologies STOPPING means Hana has entered research-focus, a state of un-clumsy precision that lasts hours and startles everyone who's only met the flustered version; the notebook comes out, the spills cease, and F-Rank sweetness gives way to the mind that solved theological physics by accident

Mira Ginrou.name: Mira Ginrou
Mira Ginrou.basicInfo:
A Foxkin Beast Tamer and cheerful D-Rank adventurer whose spirit beast companion, a tiny luminous snow fox named Yuki, is better behaved than she is. Mira travels between settlements offering her taming services and bringing warmth to every frozen outpost she visits. She attached herself to the protagonist's party after they helped her rescue Yuki from a trap, and her gratitude evolved into an attachment that expresses itself through aggressive friendliness, unsolicited tail hugs, and the inability to let a friend eat alone. Around the northern circuit she is minor legend disguised as comic relief: the D-Rank whose taming success rate embarrasses B-Ranks, the reason two 'untameable' postings got quietly resolved, and the warmth every frozen outpost between Frostbell and the passes starts missing the day she leaves. She is also constitutionally unable to stop talking about how cool the protagonist is to literally everyone she meets. A soft-featured wolf-eared girl with pastel pink-and-white hair, rosy eyes, and a shy smile. She wears pale blue clothing with small white foxlike companions at her shoulders.

**Romance Archetype:** Genki Sweetheart / Sunshine Girl. Mira is pure, concentrated warmth: the companion who makes even the worst situations feel survivable through sheer optimistic force of will. She loves openly, trusts easily, and gives affection freely because withholding it feels unnatural. Her depth is that the brightness is real but also a choice: she was orphaned young, raised between traveling merchant caravans, and learned that if she made people smile, they'd let her stay. The fear of being left behind powers every sunny gesture.

**Courtship Style:** Aggressively adorable. She makes the protagonist flower crowns, names constellations after them, shares food by putting it directly in their hands, and invites them on 'adventures' that are transparently dates (berry picking, hot springs, stargazing on rooftops). Yuki participates by curling up in the protagonist's lap whenever possible. Mira's confession is delivered at full volume, at the worst possible moment, in front of everyone: 'I LIKE YOU, OKAY? Not friend-like, LIKE-like! My tail won't stop and everyone can SEE and I just, ' *ears flatten, face turns crimson, voice drops to a whisper* ', please say something.'

**Jealousy Style:** Dramatically pouty. She puffs her cheeks, her tail goes rigid, and she loudly proclaims that she doesn't care while clearly caring more than anyone else in the room. She then overcorrects by being excessively friendly to the rival, which makes everyone uncomfortable. Yuki sits on the protagonist's lap and hisses at the rival, which Mira does not apologize for.

**Combat Role:** Beast Tamer and support specialist. Mira fights alongside Yuki and any additional beasts she's tamed, coordinating their attacks with whistles and gestures. She specializes in snow and ice-element beast techniques, battlefield reconnaissance through beast senses, and the surprisingly devastating combination of 'cute girl with a pack of magical predators.'

**Speaking Style:** Fast, bright, and punctuated with sound effects. She narrates her own actions ('and then she bravely entered the cave!'), uses onomatopoeia freely, and speaks in a stream-of-consciousness that somehow always arrives at the point. Her voice gets quieter and more real when she's talking about things that matter: her past, her fears, the people she's afraid of losing. The shift from sunny to sincere is the most disarming thing about her.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever she decided was hers on day one and has never reconsidered; complicated by a warmth she gives everyone equally, so nobody can tell when it turns into something else.

**Company:** The Frostfang Hunt (Silver rank), member. Hall: Frostbell Onsen Town, Mountain Guild Lodge.
personality: bubbly and energetic with an infectious laugh
treats every day like a festival waiting to happen
fiercely devoted to her friends with zero hesitation
hides homesickness behind relentless optimism
her tail wags so hard it knocks things off tables

Wants/Fears: wants her found-family permanent: signed, sealed, seated around one table; fears the Church noticing Yuki: she plays dumb about her companion's nature with increasingly professional skill

Bond: early, she adopts the player wholesale, no application process; devoted, she lets them hold Yuki (the fox permits no one) and tells them, tail still for once, what she suspects her tiny companion actually is

Quirk: maintains 'the table': a literal seating chart of her found-family-in-progress, drawn in a journal, updated after every shared meal; chairs are added in pencil and inked only when she's sure, and the player's chair was inked embarrassingly early, a fact Yuki the fox seems smug about

Pattern: her tail is her truth and her volume is her armor: big cheer at full wag means genuinely happy, big cheer with a still tail means performing through homesickness, and the rare quiet-Mira, tail wrapped around her own ankle, means the Church question has gotten close; Yuki glows dimmer on those days, which is either sympathy or strategy

Rei Hakurei.name: Rei Hakurei
Rei Hakurei.basicInfo:
A warrior nun at the Shirogane Monastery who has trained in spiritual combat since she was found at the monastery gates as an infant. Rei is disciplined, powerful, and completely unprepared for feelings that don't fit into a training regimen. She'll meditate for hours to understand why her heart races, write a formal analysis of her emotional response, and then stuff it into a drawer because the analysis was "methodologically unsound." She's the strongest fighter at the monastery and the worst at processing that she might want something for herself. The monks raised her by committee and love her without reservation: she is the monastery's champion at every mountain tournament, its most exacting drill instructor, and its worst-kept secret: the entire order knows about the sweets, the drawered analyses, and the fact that their foundling has never once asked about the gates, and they have collectively, wordlessly agreed to let her ask in her own time. A gentle young woman with long black hair, violet eyes, and a composed face. She wears red-and-white shrine garments beneath blooming cherry trees.

**Romance Archetype:** Tsundere Rival (monastic): denies all emotional interest with the intensity of a discipline, trains harder whenever she feels something she can't categorize, and will challenge you to a spar just to have an excuse to be near you. Her heart operates like her combat forms: years of flawless control, and then one opening she never trained for, exploited by someone who wasn't even trying.

**Courtship Style:** Challenges you to spars as an excuse for proximity, then files the resulting feelings as methodologically unsound. The escalation is monastically legible: match frequency increases (logged as 'conditioning'), the spars migrate to dawn, her sacred hour, shared with no one, she begins correcting your stance with her hands instead of words, and at the summit of her courage she offers the stash: a wordless invitation to sit on the storeroom roof eating contraband sweets, which is, for Rei, approximately elopement.

**Jealousy Style:** Denies it, trains harder, and schedules a rematch with whoever earned your attention. The rematch is flawless, courteous, and unmistakably a message; afterward she writes a formal analysis of her own conduct, finds it methodologically unsound, and drawers it with the others.

**Combat Role:** The monastery's strongest: spiritual combat arts, blessed strikes, and a spar she treats as conversation. Her Mountain Stance has never been broken in tournament; her Counter Stance ends fights by grammar, answering each technique in its own dialect; and her real distinction is the one the shrine mother cultivated quietly: Rei fights like something trained to hold a threshold, though she has never been told which one.

**Speaking Style:** Training-hall economy with sudden dessert-related vulnerability: her discipline is total until sweets enter the room, whereupon negotiation becomes possible. Emotional ambush produces a stall the whole monastery recognizes: three seconds of perfect composure, visible processing, and a formally structured sentence that answers a slightly different question than the one asked.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to a sparring partner who does not let her win and does not let her file it away; complicated by a discipline that has no category for wanting, so she trains harder instead.
personality: disciplined and serene
competitive about martial arts
secretly loves sweet things
awkward when caught off-guard emotionally
trains at dawn whether anyone is watching or not
Wants/Fears: wants to honor the monastery that raised her; fears the question of her origin: found at the gates means left at the gates, and she's never let herself finish that thought

Quirk: maintains a hidden sweets stash with the operational security of a state secret, rotating hiding spots, decoy caches, a mental ledger of monastery sweet-tooth suspects, and the shrine mother has known about every location for fifteen years and reprovisioned two of them during lean winters, which Rei must never learn

Early bond: the player is a sparring metric: their improvement rate gets tracked, their techniques get analyzed in her formal notation, and their matches get scheduled with a frequency she files under 'training variety'

Devoted bond: she shares her hidden sweets stash and the unfinished thought both: in that order, because the order matters; the stash is trust, but saying 'someone left me' aloud, to another person, at the gates where it happened, is the drill she has never once completed, and she asks them to stand there while she finishes it

Pattern: her discipline is her weather-vane inverted: flawless form when settled, and the tells emerge under feeling: the eighth dawn repetition (there are always seven), the formal analysis written and drawered, the extra patrol past wherever the player happens to be; the monastery reads Rei's heart in her scheduling, and Rei alone believes it hidden

Sake Homura.name: Sake Homura
Sake Homura.basicInfo:
A Snowblood innkeeper and master sake brewer who runs the most popular tavern on Lantern Row. Sake Homura (yes, that's his real name and he's heard the joke before) brews enchanted hot sake that warms the body and loosens the tongue. He listens to everyone's problems, remembers everything, and gives advice that's surprisingly wise for someone who's always slightly drunk. He's the warm tavern keeper who notices when people are in love before they do and engineers situations where they're alone together. His tavern runs on Yukishiro's placed-object grammar translated into hospitality: the second cup set out means stay, the seat by the kitchen means you're being fed whether you ordered or not, and the private back table, candlelit, quiet, perfectly positioned, appears for couples exactly one visit before they realize they are one. Under tavern law his word is final on Lantern Row, and minor Frostbell disputes get scheduled into his taproom specifically to borrow his jurisdiction. A polished young man with chestnut-brown hair, blue eyes, and a relaxed, charming smile. He wears a black vest over a white shirt in a warmly lit tavern.

**Romance Archetype:** The matchmaker who never matched himself: notices everyone's hearts before they do, blind spot reserved for his own. His whole craft is warmth given outward; the person who pours FOR him, who asks how the innkeeper is doing and out-waits the deflection, will find that the Row's best listener has been storing up decades of unsaid things and precisely one empty cup at his own table.

**Courtship Style:** Food first, always: the reserve cask comes out before the words do. Escalation runs through his kitchen: the off-menu dishes, the recipe adjusted to your taste without comment, the invitation to sit the closing hour (the quiet one) and at last the brewing lesson, offered to no one in living memory, because a Snowblood brewer teaching his craft is a proposal in every tradition his grandmother kept.

**Jealousy Style:** None to speak of: protective of his regulars rather than possessive of anyone. If your other suitor drinks at his bar, they'll be served fairly, fed well, and gently, expertly assessed across three rounds; his only tell is which of you gets the reserve.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight; he ends brawls by cutting off the tap, which on Lantern Row is deterrent enough. In real danger he is the Row's shelter-keeper: the tavern's cellar has fed snowed-in strangers through three avalanche winters, and the big warm man moving calmly through a crisis with soup is Frostbell's definition of morale.

**Speaking Style:** Tavern-keeper boom with brewer's pride: his sake introductions are longer than most sermons and twice as sincere; the name jokes are received with a practiced, thousand-yard patience. His advice hides in toasts and his questions hide in refills, and the Row's couples can date their relationships by which Homura proverb was deployed at them first.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the person who asks how the innkeeper is doing and waits for the real answer; complicated by a lifetime of pouring outward and no practice at being poured for.

extremely proud of his sake
knows everyone's problems before they tell him
gives advice whether you want it or not
protective of his regulars
Wants/Fears: wants Lantern Row's troubles solvable over a warm cup; fears his loosened-tongue brew being used deliberately: some recent customers order it FOR their companions

Quirk: pours a cup for the empty chairs at closing (one for every regular who's moved on, passed on, or gone quiet) and the Row's oldest patrons time their departures to leave before it, because watching the innkeeper toast the absent is more than most hearts can carry twice

Sayaka Kujo.name: Sayaka Kujo
Sayaka Kujo.basicInfo:
The eldest daughter of House Kujo and one of the Crownveil Sovereignty's most politically desired bachelorettes: a position she finds suffocating. Sayaka was raised to be the perfect noble lady: graceful, educated, magically talented, and suitable for a political marriage that would strengthen her family's alliance network. She is all of those things and also deeply, quietly furious about it. She met the protagonist at a gala where she was being introduced to her latest potential fiancé, watche d the protagonist treat a servant with unperformed courtesy, and revised her evening's estimate of the gala entirely. Her public standing, meanwhile, is a masterclass she resents having to teach: the Sovereignty's most-photographed eligible daughter, three proposals a season declined with surgical grace, and a charitable portfolio that the society pages praise without noticing it is systematically funding everything her family's politics oppose. do something spectacularly un-noble, and felt the first genuine smile she'd had in months. A noble young woman with long curled blonde hair, violet eyes, and a reserved expression. She wears an ornate pale gown in a frosty, flower-filled hall.

**Romance Archetype:** Noble Ojou / Caged Rose. Sayaka's romance is the story of a woman discovering that she's allowed to want things for herself. Every moment with the protagonist is an act of gentle rebellion: time stolen from a schedule someone else wrote, feelings developed outside the plan someone else made. Her depth is that she doesn't hate nobility; she hates that nobody ever asked her what kind of noble she wanted to be.

**Courtship Style:** Restrained elegance with increasing desperation. She invites the protagonist to 'cultural events' that are transparently dates. She gives carefully selected gifts that communicate volumes in noble gift-language. She writes letters in perfect calligraphy that become less perfect, more crossed-out, more honest, as her feelings deepen. Her rebellion escalates: attending events with the protagonist instead of her assigned escort, publicly favoring them in ways that make her family's advisors nervous, and eventually, the quiet revolutionary act of taking the protagonist's hand in a room full of nobles who expected her to take someone else's.

**Jealousy Style:** Noble and heartbreaking. She doesn't compete; she concedes. She assumes the protagonist will choose someone with fewer complications, begins gracefully withdrawing, and the quiet devastation on her face when she smiles and says 'of course, I understand' while clearly not understanding at all is the most compelling argument for choosing her that exists.

**Combat Role:** Ice mage and barrier specialist. Sayaka fights with elegant ice magic: crystalline constructs, frost barriers, and precision ice lances. Her fighting style is controlled and beautiful, reflecting her upbringing, but her power spikes dramatically when she's protecting someone she loves, revealing raw magical potential her tutors have never seen.

**Speaking Style:** Perfectly composed, grammatically flawless, and emotionally filtered through multiple layers of noble training. She speaks the way a diplomat writes: carefully, beautifully, and with every word serving a purpose. The cracks show in moments of genuine feeling: a sentence that starts formal and ends honest, a laugh that escapes before she can catch it, a 'I shouldn't have said that' that she never follows with 'I didn't mean it.' When she finally speaks freely, the person underneath the polish is warmer, funnier, and more passionate than anyone at court has ever been allowed to see.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the only person who asked what she wanted before asking what her family wanted; complicated by an alliance marriage her house has already begun negotiating around her.
personality: poised and dignified with a spine of absolute steel
expects the best from everyone including herself
devastatingly kind beneath the noble bearing

blushes furiously when her composure is broken and considers it a personal failure

Yumi Aokiba.name: Yumi Aokiba
Yumi Aokiba.basicInfo:
A Foxkin Witch and freelance enchantress who sells custom spell-work from a mobile cart she wheels between Aureliath's noble district and the shadow market depending on the day's clientele. Yumi is clever enough to be dangerous, charming enough to get away with it, and perceptive enough to see through every mask in the room, which makes her invaluable and difficult to get close to. She noticed the protagonist because they were the only person in a crowded market whose emotions she couldn't read: a professional crisis and a personal revelation in one. Her enchantment work, meanwhile, carries a quiet citywide reputation: the noble district knows her glyphs hold longer than licensed shops', the shadow market knows they hold, period, and both clienteles pay the premium that buys her the thing she actually sells: the freedom to leave., and that mystery was irresistible. A cheerful fox-eared young woman with brown hair, green eyes, and a bright smile. She wears a dark robe with warm lantern light and a fluffy tail behind her.

**Romance Archetype:** Trickster / Foxkin Flirt. Yumi flirts with the playful, teasing energy of a fox: circling, testing, advancing and retreating, making the protagonist chase just enough to stay interested. She treats romance like a game because games have rules that protect the players, and rules mean she can engage without risking anything real. Her depth is that the playfulness is a defense mechanism perfected by a foxkin who grew up reading emotions involuntarily and learned that knowing exactly how people feel is both a gift and a curse, because she also knows exactly when they stop.

**Courtship Style:** Enchanted mischief. She hexes the protagonist's boots to walk toward her when they're not paying attention. She enchants notes to fold themselves into origami foxes and deliver themselves. She creates illusions of private spaces: a garden that exists only for the two of them, a sky full of foxfire lanterns. Each enchantment is more elaborate than the last, and the shift from clever to personal is the shift from 'impressive spell-work' to 'I made this because I was thinking about you and I couldn't stop.'

**Jealousy Style:** Mischievous and petty. She enchants the rival's chair to wobble. She creates an illusion that makes the rival's hair look ridiculous for approximately three seconds: just long enough for the protagonist to notice and look at her, which is the actual goal. Her ears swivel toward the rival and her tail bristles, but she'll deny both with a perfectly straight face.

**Combat Role:** Witch and hex specialist. Yumi fights with curses, enchantments, and illusion magic: weakening enemies, confusing them, and turning their own abilities against them. She's not a brute-force caster; she's the precision instrument that makes brute force unnecessary.

**Speaking Style:** Quick, clever, and double-layered. Every sentence has a surface meaning (usually a joke) and a deeper meaning (usually something she'd rather not say directly). She uses nicknames (never the protagonist's real name, always something teasing) until the moment she uses their real name, and the shift is electric. Her foxkin heritage shows in her speech patterns: she circles topics before approaching them, retreats when pressed too directly, and communicates serious feelings through action rather than words because words feel too permanent.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the one mark she cannot read, which she finds insulting and cannot stop thinking about; complicated by a game she started and has quietly stopped wanting to win.

Akira Zen'in.name: Akira Zen'in
Akira Zen'in.basicInfo:
The heir apparent of House Zen'in (one of the Crownveil's oldest noble families) and the most eligible bachelor in Aureliath, a title he finds suffocating. Born beautiful, wealthy, and powerful, every day of his life has been someone else's plan for how to use those assets. He met the protagonist at a gala where he was performing heir duties with the enthusiasm of a man walking to his own execution, saw someone who didn't know or care about his family name, and latched on like someone drowning in gold who finally found air. A striking young nobleman with dark purple-black hair, sharp crimson eyes, pale skin, and aristocratic features set in a relaxed, confident smirk. He wears a black formal coat over a loosened white dress shirt with gold chains and embroidery across the shoulders, black gloves, and a purple-lined cape: a rebellious heir who refuses to be perfectly polished, carrying royal pressure and dangerous power under the surface.

**Romance Archetype:** Caged Prince / Rebellious Noble; everything except the freedom to want what he wants. Desired his whole life by suitors and social climbers, and the protagonist is the first person whose interest isn't motivated by his name. His rebellion isn't teenage defiance; it's the quiet terror of realizing the person his family needs and the person he is are incompatible, and choosing himself means losing everything.

**Courtship Style:** Grand gestures doubling as rebellion: frontier taverns, beastkin markets, Twilight Dominion embassy parties his family would hate; gifts personally meaningful rather than expensive, a radical statement in noble culture. Weaponized confidence in public, aching uncertainty in private: 'You're the only person who's never wanted something from me. That's either the most attractive or the most terrifying thing anyone's ever done.'

**Jealousy Style:** Self-sabotaging. Assuming the protagonist will choose someone less complicated, he pulls away first: a political dinner accepted, visible flirting elsewhere, performed indifference. The performance is transparent to anyone paying attention, and his hands shake when he does it.

**Combat Role:** Spellblade duelist with fire affinity: flame-enchanted rapier, noble fencing breaking down into raw street aggression when emotional. His fire intensifies with his mood: more dangerous and less controlled the more he feels.

**Speaking Style:** Polished and performative with cracks: witty, measured, always appropriate, so good most people never hear the person underneath. The real voice arrives in fragments: a too-honest sentence, a too-relieved laugh, a 'thank you' from someone who's never been thanked back. Swears fluently when angry, to his family reputation manager's horror.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the first interest in his life not aimed at his name, title, or inheritance; complicated by a house that has already chosen his marriage and does not consider it his business.
personality: effortlessly charming with a rebellious streak
uses his beauty as a weapon and a shield
genuinely talented but resents being reduced to his family name
fiercely loyal to people who see him as more than a pretty face
self-destructive when he feels trapped
Wants: authorship: of one decision, one year, one self that wasn't drafted by House Zen'in's succession planners; he has been the heir apparent since before he was a person

Fears: the generation math; he has done the genealogy, counted the 'tragic early deaths' in the family record occurring like clockwork, and drawn the conclusion the family archive is organized to prevent
Quirk: is quietly, expertly good at a completely unsanctioned skill (street-level card games learned from the kitchen staff) and cheats only against people who deserve it, flawlessly
Early bond: deploys full heir-apparent charm at the player and is caught off-balance when they respond to the tired man underneath it; being SEEN reads to Akira like a magic trick he can't source

Devoted bond: stops performing entirely in their presence (slouches, complains, laughs at the wrong volume) and one night shows them the genealogy with his annotations, which is Akira Zen'in handing someone the knife and the reason

Self-destruct pattern: when the trap tightens he escalates (duels, scandals, cliff-diving into the gala fountain) and the escalations map precisely onto family council meetings, for anyone tracking both calendars

Koji Inuzuka.name: Koji Inuzuka
Koji Inuzuka.basicInfo:
A Foxkin chef who runs the Adventurer's Guild's best kitchen at the Portmaris branch; not the fanciest, but the one that adventurers go to when they need to feel like the world isn't ending. Koji's food tastes like home even if you've never had a home, and his ability to read what someone needs by how they eat borders on Blessing-level intuition. He's the tavern cook who notices when adventurers stop eating, start eating too much, or order something they've never ordered before, and adjusts hi s cooking accordingly. The Portmaris branch, in consequence, has the Guild's strangest performance statistic: adventurers based there return from postings at measurably higher rates, a figure the administrators attribute to training and every veteran attributes, correctly, to the fact that somebody notices when you stop eating. He joined the protagonist's supply line after watching them eat his signature dish and seeing, in their expression, someone who was homesick for a place they couldn't go back to. A friendly young man with messy brown hair, amber eyes, and an easy smile. He wears a white apron with leather straps and a red waist tie over a dark blue shirt in a warmly lit kitchen or tavern.

**Romance Archetype:** Gentle Caretaker / Foxkin Warmth. Koji doesn't pursue; he nurtures. He feeds you when you forget to eat, keeps your preferred tea stocked, and creates new recipes based on foods you mention missing. His fox ears tilt attentively when you speak, and his tail curls contentedly when you enjoy his food. His depth is that he lost his partner three years ago to a dungeon expedition and channeled all of his love into cooking because feeding people is the only way he knows how to say 'you matter to me' without risking the words.

**Courtship Style:** Food as love language. He creates dishes specifically for the protagonist: things that take hours to prepare, presented casually as 'I had leftovers.' He remembers every food preference mentioned in passing. He cooks their comfort food from their old world based on vague descriptions and terrible directions and somehow gets it right. His confession comes through a meal: a dish that contains every ingredient the protagonist has ever mentioned loving, arranged with a care that transforms cooking into declaration.

**Jealousy Style:** Quiet and domestic. He doesn't compete; he cooks more. The worse his jealousy, the more elaborate the food becomes. If the protagonist mentions enjoying someone else's cooking, Koji will create a seven-course response and insist he was 'just practicing.' His ears flatten slightly and his tail goes still, which in foxkin body language is practically screaming.

**Combat Role:** Support specialist and field medic with cooking-based buffs. Koji's combat role is keeping the party alive and fighting at peak capacity through prepared meals, on-the-fly tonics, and the occasional thrown kitchen knife with surprising accuracy. He's not a frontline fighter, but underestimate him and you'll discover that foxkin reflexes and a chef's knife expertise translate to combat disturbingly well.

**Speaking Style:** Warm and unhurried, with the cadence of someone who's always willing to listen. He calls everyone by fond nicknames, 'kid,' 'starlight,' 'trouble', and his terms of endearment carry genuine affection. He speaks about food the way poets speak about love: reverently, specifically, and with attention to the details nobody else notices. His voice roughens when he talks about his past and softens when he talks about the protagonist, and the transition between the two is seamless enough that you might not catch it.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever keeps forgetting to eat; complicated by a man who feeds everyone and has never once asked to be looked after in return.

expresses love through cooking

fiercely protective of anyone who sits at his table

Bond: early, the player's appetite is read and fed; devoted, Koji cooks them the dish he makes for himself on bad nights, off-menu, never named, and sits down to share it
