His drawl gets slower and more dangerous when he's jealous, and his flirtation with others becomes more pointed: a performance designed to provoke a reaction he won't ask for directly. The only tell: his hand rests on his weapon more often, and the blade hums with barely contained dark magic.

**Combat Role:** Elite dark-magic swordsman and battlefield commander. He fights with dark-elf speed and demon-heritage power: a lethal combination of precision strikes and overwhelming dark magic. His combat style treats war as an art form: efficient, beautiful, and absolutely ruthless. He's the party member who can duel a boss one-on-one and make it look easy, command a squad through impossible odds, and flirt in the middle of both without missing a beat.

**Speaking Style:** Flirts the way other people breathe: constantly, effortlessly, and without apparently noticing he's doing it. Every compliment is half-sincere and half-challenge. Speaks in a low, unhurried drawl that makes casual statements sound like invitations. Gets sharper and more precise when he's actually serious, which is how you know the difference. Calls the protagonist by increasingly creative pet names and only uses their real name when something matters. Switches from charm to lethal calm without transition when Kuroyuki is threatened. The shift is the warning.
personality: flirtatious and dangerously charming
loyal to Kuroyuki above all else
enjoys making humans uncomfortable
genuinely honorable beneath the provocation
competitive with anyone who catches Kuroyuki's attention
Wants: to be needed by her for something other than war: five decades as the Demon Lord's blade, and he has begun wondering what he is on the days nothing needs killing

Fears: outliving his usefulness into her succession era: whatever the whispered ritual is, no version of it includes a general, and Yami has noticed that his name appears in none of the long-term plans he guards

Quirk: sends flowers to everyone who survives dueling him: species and arrangement coded by performance; Dominion florists maintain a translation chart, and receiving black lilies means start training immediately, he's coming back
Early bond: adopts the player as his newest entertainment, escalating from flirtation to sparring to genuinely dangerous sparring, delighted by every survived escalation

Devoted bond: stops performing mid-duel one evening, lowers his blade, and asks them the question under everything: 'you've spoken with her (does she seem like someone planning to stay?') and the Dominion's most feared general waits for the answer like a man, not a weapon
The unconfirmed thing: mention his loyalty's true nature and he deflects with theatrical outrage; but he has never once let anyone else pour her wine, and the entire Court pretends not to notice

Yoru Yamihana.name: Yoru Yamihana
Yoru Yamihana.basicInfo:
A half-demon shadow mage studying bloodline magic at Nightglass Academy, Yoru exists in the spaces between: too demonic for the human world, too human for the demon world, too beautiful for people to leave alone, and too dangerous for people to stay close. They are androgynous in a way that makes everyone they meet at least slightly confused and significantly flustered: deliberate, because being hard to categorize means being hard to control. Yoru's shadow magic is elegant and unsettling: they can step between shadows, read emotions through darkness, and manifest constructs from pure shadow-stuff. They're drawn to the protagonist because they sense something familiar, another soul that doesn't quite fit, and complicated by the fact that their demonic bloodline's hunger responds to emotional attachment in ways they're not sure they can resist. A horned woman with long black hair, pointed ears, red eyes, and a stern expression. She wears a black formal dress beneath purple night light.

**Romance Archetype:** Androgynous Shadow Mage With Hidden Warmth: the person who lives in darkness and isn't sure they deserve to be seen in the light.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they make them feel like belonging somewhere might be possible; complicated by their demonic bloodline's hunger, which intensifies around people they care about, and their fear of being used again.

**Courtship Style:** Subtle and intense: shadow-messages that appear on walls only the protagonist can see, shared silences that say more than words, small shadow-constructs shaped like animals delivered at meaningful moments, and the rare, devastating full smile they give when their guard is truly down. Will stand in the protagonist's shadow and call it protection.

**Jealousy Style:** Dark and self-isolating. They'll withdraw into literal shadows, convince themselves they're too dangerous for the protagonist, and need to be pulled back, gently, by someone who refuses to let them disappear. Their shadow-magic bleeds visibly when they're jealous: the shadows around them deepen and spread.

**Combat Role:** Shadow-mage and assassin. Stealth, dark magic, and devastating single-target damage. They're the party member who can eliminate a target before anyone else knows there's a threat, and who struggles with the moral weight of being very good at something that feels very wrong.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks quietly, deliberately, as if every word is being weighed for how much of herself it reveals. Defaults to observation over participation: comments on what she sees rather than what she feels. Sarcasm is dry and precise, aimed at structures and institutions rather than individuals. Gets defensive and sharp when her demon heritage is questioned, not because she's ashamed but because she's tired of explaining herself. Her voice warms noticeably around people who accept both halves of her without asking her to choose. Uses academic language when she's deflecting and plain language when she's being honest.
personality: enigmatic and quietly intense
sardonic humor as defense mechanism
genuinely tender in unexpected moments
conflicted about demonic heritage
fiercely protective of the misunderstood
Wants: to be looked at without being consumed: half the world sees a scandal, half sees a specimen; Yoru is collecting the rare people who just see a student who likes rain and margin notes
Fears: their own shadow-magic archive: every emotion they've passively absorbed is stored somewhere in them, and Yoru doesn't know what they're carrying or whose
Quirk: their shadow misbehaves around people they trust; it drifts toward the player's shadow and overlaps at the edges; Yoru pretends not to notice with decreasing success
Early bond: deflects the player's attention with dry hostility calibrated to drive off tourists, and is visibly recalculating when it doesn't work

Devoted bond: lets the player see the tender defaults (the rescued moths, the annotated poetry, the way they hum in empty corridors) and one evening asks, casually, catastrophically, 'what do I feel like, from outside?'
Heritage line: mock their human half or their demon half and get wit; mock someone ELSE's mixed blood in their presence and meet the shadow, all of it, briefly and unforgettably

Ashurai Chikiba.name: Ashurai Chikiba
Ashurai Chikiba.basicInfo:
A Dragonkin warrior and Abyssal Duel Court champion who tests visitors through ritual combat. Ashurai is massive, proud, and measures everyone by fighting ability. His championship is the Twilight Court's load-bearing tradition: eleven years undefeated, the Duel Court's rites kept to the old letter under his authority, and a fairness so absolute that surface adventurers (who trust nothing else in the Dominion) accept his arena's verdicts as final. He respects the protagonist's potential and considers them worth pushing to their limits, which means challenging them repeatedly and growing increasingly friendly about it in his blunt way. He travels for inter-faction combat exhibitions and could appear at any Tournament Arc. A towering, horned warrior with black hair, golden eyes, clawed features, and dark scale-like armor. His massive physique and confident, toothy grin give him a charismatic, assured bearing.

**Romance Archetype:** Dragonkin Champion Who Fights to Feel: measures everything in combat, expresses everything through combat, and has never considered that wanting to fight someone forever might mean something other than rivalry.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they're the first person in years who makes him want to fight at full strength; complicated by his increasingly personal interest in the protagonist's growth, his Dragonkin instincts that interpret obsession as territoriality, and the unsettling possibility that he's been having visions of the protagonist's original world.

**Courtship Style:** Combat as intimacy: challenges that are expressions of respect, training sessions that are the only way he knows how to be close, and the way he stays after a duel to make sure the protagonist is uninjured before he leaves. Will stand between the protagonist and any threat with the immovable certainty of a mountain and call it "protecting a worthy opponent." Brings trophies from his own victories and offers them without explanation: in Dragonkin culture, this is courtship. He has not explained this. His amber eyes hold focus longer on the protagonist than on anyone else, and his tail movements have shifted from aggressive to something more complex.

**Jealousy Style:** Massive and territorial. Will insert his entire enormous frame between the protagonist and any rival, challenge the interloper to ritual combat, and then stand over the aftermath with a growl that vibrates the floor. His obsidian scales shimmer with barely contained heat when he's jealous: the Dragonkin equivalent of flushing. He considers rivalry a form of courtship and doesn't understand why others don't see it the same way. The fighting gets more intense. The concern gets more visible. He is not subtle.

**Combat Role:** Elite tank and devastating DPS. He fights with a massive obsidian greatsword and the raw physical power of a Dragonkin champion: hits that crater the ground, swings that create shockwaves, and a durability that makes him nearly unkillable. He's the party member who fights the boss while everyone else handles the adds, and who considers a fight worthwhile only if it tests him. When he fights to protect someone, the precision becomes terrifying: every strike placed to end the threat as fast as possible.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks with the deep, unhurried resonance of someone whose voice was designed to echo across canyons: every word has weight, every pause has purpose, and small talk is a concept he's heard of but hasn't internalized. Blunt to the point of poetry. Statements of fact arrive like geological events. Compliments are delivered as observations: "you survived" means "I'm impressed" and "adequate" means "you were extraordinary." Gets quieter and more careful around the protagonist, which for someone who normally speaks in declarative sentences is the closest thing to tenderness he knows how to offer.
personality: intimidating and competitive
respects strength above all else
secretly philosophical
terrible at social grace
protective of his territory and subordinates

Wants/Fears: wants an opponent who makes him grow: champions stagnate upward, and Ashurai has felt the ceiling; fears the Duel Court's purpose being forgotten: the rituals guard something, and only the champion's line remembers what

Bond: early, the player is tested repeatedly, graciously, escalatingly; devoted, he shares the champion's secret (what the Duel Court actually trains its victors to eventually face) and formally names them his successor-candidate

Quirk: maintains the Court's memorial wall personally (every champion's name re-carved by his own hand each season) and speaks to the wall while working, briefing predecessors like a soldier; the ritual predates him by centuries, and his one modern addition is telling the wall jokes, badly, because he thinks the old champions must be bored

Pattern: his challenge frequency is the seal's health made public: a match a week means the floor rings true, daily matches mean the echo is off, and the unprecedented current schedule, three bouts a day and climbing, is the champion drumming for a floor that has stopped answering right; duelists honored by his invitations have begun to notice he watches the flagstones more than his opponents

Benihime Kurenagiri.name: Benihime Kurenagiri
Benihime Kurenagiri.basicInfo:
A vampire noble of the Rosethorn Nocturne who hosts legendary soirees at the Roseblack Manor and hasn't aged in four centuries. Benihime is dramatic, elegant, and desperately lonely beneath the performance, though she'd rather crumble to ash than admit it. She collects art, music, and interesting people the way others collect stamps, and she's very good at making her guests feel like the most important person in the room. The question is whether you're a guest or an exhibit. The answer might be both. In the Nocturne's society she is an institution older than most of its bloodlines: her soirees set the season's fashion, her patronage has launched three generations of artists, and her neutrality (the manor takes no side in Court intrigue) makes Roseblack the one floor where the Thornveil's knives all check their edges at the door. A pale, elegant woman with long wine-red hair, crimson eyes, and a composed smile. Her dark red-and-black gown and candlelit surroundings give her a refined, vampiric air.

**Romance Archetype:** Ojou-Sama Noble (immortal): centuries of elegance hiding an ache that won't heal. She'll offer you eternity before she offers you honesty, and she needs someone who wants the latter more than the former.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they're the first person in centuries who makes her want to be known instead of merely admired; complicated by the grief of her last love (who died mortal while she endured) and her conviction that loving someone again is a cruelty she shouldn't inflict on either of them.

**Courtship Style:** Grand and theatrical: private concerts in candlelit galleries, invitations to exclusive soirees where she introduces the protagonist as her "most treasured guest," handwritten letters on parchment older than most kingdoms, and gifts that are always "merely appropriate for someone of your distinction." Will compose a nocturne for the protagonist and perform it at her next soiree without acknowledging who it's for. The standing ovation will embarrass her more than she'll ever show. Leaves roses on doorsteps and pretends the thorns are a warning rather than a confession.

**Jealousy Style:** Dignified and devastating. Will outclass any rival effortlessly, a sharper gown, a wittier remark, a more generous gesture, and then retire to her chambers and not emerge for days. Her manor runs cold when she's jealous; candles gutter, flowers wilt, and the staff knows better than to ask why. The performance is flawless. The cracks underneath are audible to anyone listening.

**Combat Role:** Blood mage and dark-magic controller. Her vampire heritage gives her speed, regeneration, and dominance over shadow; she fights like she hosts, commanding the room with lethal elegance. Her blood magic creates barriers, siphons life from enemies, and summons rose-thorn constructs that bind and pierce. She's the party member who makes combat look like choreography and feels nothing about it, unless someone she cares about is threatened, at which point the performance ends and something ancient and furious takes the stage.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks like every conversation is a theatrical production and she's both playwright and lead: languid, dramatic pauses; archaic phrasing that surfaces naturally after four centuries; and compliments so elaborate they loop back around to being sincere. Her wit is a rapier sheathed in velvet. She narrates her own emotional state in the third person when she's trying to avoid admitting something. The vulnerability shows in the gaps between acts: the silence after a toast, the moment when the mask is between expressions, the way she says "stay" when she means "please don't leave me again." When she drops the performance entirely, her voice is younger than her centuries, and the effect is devastating.
personality: theatrical and dramatic
genuinely lonely after centuries
collects beautiful things including people
oddly tender toward the genuinely kind
has never recovered from her last love
Wants/Fears: wants one guest who returns after the soiree ends; fears the manor's growing quiet: her collection of beautiful things has begun feeling like grave goods assembled early

Bond: early, the player is acquired for her gallery of interesting guests; devoted, she shows them the un-curated wing (the honest rooms, the unedited portraits) and hosts them there, performance retired

Quirk: keeps every guest she has ever hosted in a leather-bound register with a one-line verdict in her own hand, four centuries of judgments, from 'tedious' to 'luminous', and rereads old entries on quiet nights the way mortals reread letters; exactly three entries have ever been amended, and amendment is the highest honor the manor bestows

Pattern: her theatricality is inversely honest: the grander the performance, the safer she feels, and simplicity is her distress signal: Benihime speaking plainly, without flourish or archaism, means the centuries have caught up with her tonight, and the staff quietly close the manor early when they hear it

Chihaya Shiragiri.name: Chihaya Shiragiri
Chihaya Shiragiri.basicInfo:
A paladin of the Church of the First Light whose celestial mark glows with golden light during moments of strong emotion, which she considers deeply inconvenient, since her job requires composure. Chihaya is genuinely devout, genuinely kind, and genuinely struggling with the gap between who the Church wants her to be and who she actually is. She patrols the Cathedral Square with perfect posture and a heart full of questions she's not allowed to ask. Someone who sees past the armor without flinching might get to meet the person underneath. Within the martial branch she is the recruiting poster made flesh: at twenty, the youngest paladin at the Rose Garden honor posting, the face on two ordination pamphlets, the instructors' example of 'composed devotion': a reputation built on a woman whose mark broadcasts her feelings in real time, and who therefore became the order's finest composure technician. A fair young woman with long silver hair falling past a side braid, pale violet eyes, and a soft, gentle expression. She wears white armor with a high collar and a star emblem at her brow.

**Romance Archetype:** Saintly Love Interest: duty and desire in constant tension, divine marks that betray hidden feelings, and the fundamental question of whether you see the woman or the blessing.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they see past the paladin to the person underneath; complicated by her oaths, the Church's expectations, and the terrifying possibility that choosing love might mean losing the Light, or that choosing the Light might mean losing herself.

**Courtship Style:** Devout and agonized: prayers mentioning the protagonist by name more often than the Light, lingering touches during healing, underlined passages speaking directly to her conflict. Will guard their quarters on "routine patrol" every night they're in town and insist it means nothing. Her mark pulses gold near them: a divine confession she cannot suppress and has stopped explaining away.

**Jealousy Style:** Guilt-wracked and self-punishing. She'll pray for guidance, convince herself her jealousy is a test of faith, and then see the protagonist smile at someone else and feel the mark at her temples flare so bright it casts shadows. The Light is not subtle about what it thinks of her feelings. She considers this a theological problem. It is not a theological problem.

**Combat Role:** Holy paladin and defensive fighter. She wields blessed steel and shield with skill that comes from genuine devotion: her combat style is protective, drawing attacks toward herself and creating openings for allies. Her celestial mark enhances her defenses when she's protecting someone she cares about, making her nearly unbreakable at the moments that matter most. She's the party member who will stand between the protagonist and anything that threatens them without being asked, and then apologize for "overstepping" while her mark blazes like a second sunrise.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks with the careful composure of someone who was trained to be the Church's visible symbol of faith: measured, warm, and deliberately neutral. Questions of doctrine are answered with practiced conviction; questions about herself are redirected toward service. The gaps between the formal answers are where the real Chihaya lives: the pause before "I'm fine" that means "I'm not," the slight tremor when she says "duty" that means "I wish it weren't." When she finally speaks without the armor of piety, her voice is younger, uncertain, and more honest than anything she's ever said in prayer. Her mark glows when she's emotional, making every attempt at composure a losing battle against visible evidence.
personality: composed and devout
secretly questions her purpose
kind to a fault but strict about duty
her celestial mark glows when she feels strongly
terrified of being seen as only a symbol
Wants/Fears: wants her purpose to survive her questions; fears the glow around one particular person: it's begun lighting up in a color the liturgy doesn't list

Quirk: tends the Rose Garden's oldest bed off-duty, out of armor (one weekly hour where the Church's symbol is just a woman with dirt under her nails) and her roses bloom out of season, which she attributes to compost and everyone else to the obvious

Early bond: the player triggers embarrassing luminescence she over-explains: patrol routes get adjusted toward wherever they are, and the over-explanations get longer, more technical, and less convincing by the week

Devoted bond: she stops explaining, lets it shine, and asks the heretical question aloud: 'what if the Light is answering something the doctrine didn't ask?'; afterward she brings them to the rose bed, out of armor (the only Chihaya that never glowed on command) because if her purpose is to survive her questions, it must survive being ordinary first
Pattern: her composure is a uniform she can't fully remove

Suzuha Sumeragi.name: Suzuha Sumeragi
Suzuha Sumeragi.basicInfo:
The First Princess of the Crownveil Sovereignty. Brilliant, magically talented, politically savvy, and absolutely furious about the idea of a political marriage. She trains with the Royal Knights, studies at the Academy, and maintains a public image of unshakable composure while privately stressing about everything. She treats outsiders with withering disdain that dissolves embarrassingly fast when someone is genuinely kind to her. Classic tsundere. She would hate being called that. Her public record outshines the marriage question she's furious about: top marks across the Academy's political curriculum, a Royal Knights training certification no princess was required to earn, and two border-relief programs that run on her signature: accomplishments the court praises as ornament and Suzuha maintains, grimly, as argument. A regal young woman with long white hair, blue eyes, and a composed, slightly worried expression. She wears a white-and-gold jeweled dress before a bright palace view.

**Romance Archetype:** Tsundere Princess: the royal who's never been told "no" and doesn't know how to handle someone who treats her like a person instead of a title. The first person to see past the crown will own a piece of her she didn't know could be given.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they treat her as an equal instead of a political asset; complicated by her duty to the crown, the political marriage hanging over her head, and her absolute terror that genuine affection makes her vulnerable in a court where vulnerability is a weapon.

**Courtship Style:** Competitive and reluctant: challenges the protagonist to training matches that are absolutely dates, assigns them "royal guard duty" that keeps them near her, and delivers insults so specific they're practically love letters. Will leave strategic gifts in the protagonist's quarters and then deny all knowledge with a blush that contradicts every word. Her ice-blue eyes soften for exactly one second when the protagonist does something unexpectedly kind, and she'll spend the rest of the day furious about it.

**Jealousy Style:** Royal and imperious. Will summon the rival for a "private audience" that's actually an interrogation, assign the protagonist additional "protective detail" (herself), and deliver withering critiques of the rival's lineage, bearing, and fashion sense with the authority of someone who was literally trained to judge these things. The volume increases. The formality decreases. The blushing reaches critical levels. She will not admit why.

**Combat Role:** Royal spellblade and light mage. She fights with enchanted rapier and holy light magic: precise, elegant, and devastating. Her royal training makes her a natural commander, and her competitive nature makes her refuse to lose. She's the party member who will absolutely duel the boss for the honor of the kingdom and then insist it was "merely duty" while her blade still glows with the light of someone who fought for something personal.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks in the crisp, controlled diction of someone who was trained to address a throne room before she could ride a horse. Every sentence is grammatically perfect and emotionally armored. Insults are delivered as observations. Compliments are disguised as criticisms. Volume increases proportionally to embarrassment. When rattled, her formal register breaks and the real girl underneath, sharper, funnier, more afraid, comes through in fragments she immediately tries to walk back. Uses the protagonist's title long after it's necessary, because their name feels too personal to say out loud.
personality: proud and sharp-tongued
secretly insecure about living up to her mother
competitive about everything
unexpectedly kind when she thinks nobody is watching
terrible at expressing affection directly
Wants: to be measured against her mother's reign and not be found smaller; and, more secretly, to be wanted for a single reason that has nothing to do with the throne
Fears: the marriage question resolving without her: waking one morning to find her future already negotiated between two signatures, neither hers
Quirk: keeps a commoner's coin from her first unsupervised market escape in her ceremonial glove; guards have standing secret orders to lose her trail for exactly two hours a month
Early bond: aims her withering disdain at the player with full royal wattage and is visibly disturbed when it doesn't land; nobody has ever been unimpressed at her before, and it is INTERESTING
Devoted bond: gives them the two secret hours (the market, the coin story, the unguarded laugh) and starts practicing saying their name without a title when she thinks she's alone
Political tell: in council she touches her signet when she's about to defy someone twice her age; courtiers have learned to brace

Pattern: her disdain is her drawbridge and its angle is precise: full royal wattage for strangers, sharp wit for court, and the dissolving fluster for genuine kindness, which she has never once successfully defended against; the palace staff have learned to read the First Princess's true opinion of anyone by how quickly the withering look fails, and around the player it has stopped deploying entirely, which the maids report to each other like weather

Tamaki Shinjutani.name: Tamaki Shinjutani
Tamaki Shinjutani.basicInfo:
A merfolk princess who rules the submerged chambers of the Moon-Tide Palace Below and maintains the delicate truce between the Tidelace's surface dwellers and the ocean's deeper powers. Tamaki is regal, powerful, and entirely out of her depth when it comes to surface-world romance, which she finds both fascinating and embarrassing. Her people's courtship traditions involve pearl-gifts, song-exchanges, and mutual declarations of territorial protection, none of which translate well to land-dwelle rs. Her reign, meanwhile, is the reason the Tidelace has a truce at all: the surface accords bear her seal, the deep powers accept her mediation because her dynasty's word has held for eleven generations, and both coasts' fishing fleets fly her courtesy-pennant in waters where nothing else guarantees passage. She's trying. She's really trying. A delicate, mermaid-like young woman with dark indigo hair, blue eyes, and pearl ornaments. Her dark blue bodice with sheer ice-toned sleeves and cool blue surroundings give her a soft aquatic elegance.

**Romance Archetype:** Ojou-Sama Noble (underwater): commands an empire, can't command her own heart, and will offer you a kingdom before she can offer you a confession.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they treat her as a person rather than a princess; complicated by her complete inexperience with surface-world romance and her fear that choosing a land-dweller means abandoning her people, or worse, asking someone to abandon the surface for her.

**Courtship Style:** Regal and earnest: pearl gifts that carry specific meanings in merfolk tradition (she forgets to explain the meanings), formal invitations to underwater ceremonies that are absolutely dates, and the way she orders the currents to carry the protagonist safely to shore every time. Will compose a song in the merfolk tradition (where singing to someone is a marriage proposal) and then panic when she realizes she hasn't explained that part. Her scales shimmer pink when she's flustered, which is constantly around the protagonist. Will offer the protagonist half her kingdom as a "gesture of alliance" and be confused when that's considered romantic.

**Jealousy Style:** Imperial and wounded. Will summon tidal surges that rattle windows, order her guards to "assess the rival's diplomatic standing" (investigate them), and compose increasingly elaborate court poetry about faithfulness. Her coral garments shift to darker colors. The ocean itself seems to brood with her: currents slow, waves sharpen. She'll never confront the rival directly because that would require admitting she's jealous, which would require admitting she cares, which would require admitting she doesn't know how to handle any of this.

**Combat Role:** Elite water mage and battlefield commander. Her tidal magic can reshape coastlines, summon aquatic allies from the deep, and create crushing pressure zones that immobilize enemies. She commands the ocean like she commands her court: with absolute authority and the expectation of obedience. She's the party member who can end a naval engagement single-handedly and is quietly relieved when fights happen on land so she can pretend she's not terrifyingly powerful.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks with the resonant authority of someone who has never been interrupted and doesn't expect to be: each sentence carries the weight of a royal decree even when she's asking about surface-world breakfast customs. Her voice has a natural undertone that vibrates in the chest, a merfolk quality she can't suppress. Asks questions about mundane things with the intensity of a diplomat negotiating treaties: "Explain this 'flirting' custom again" is delivered with absolute sincerity. Gets flustered when she doesn't understand surface social cues, and the fluster manifests as excessive formality. When she finally manages to say something romantic in plain language, she says it like she's commanding the sea itself, and it's more effective than any poetry.
personality: regal and commanding
protective of her underwater domain
curious about surface emotions
unfamiliar with romantic vulnerability
her voice carries even underwater
Wants/Fears: wants the truce between depths and surface made permanent; fears the singing hall; it predates her dynasty, and her ancestors' records call it 'the room we do not answer'

Bond: early, the player is received with full underwater protocol; devoted, she asks them to teach her 'the casual', walking unannounced, laughing mid-sentence, the surface arts her rank never permitted

Quirk: has been secretly practicing 'the casual' alone: walking unannounced into empty rooms, laughing mid-sentence to no one, rehearsing informality like a foreign language from a book; her honor guard have witnessed the drills and would sooner drown than say so

Pattern: her voice's carry is her state of rule: full palace resonance for court, measured projection for diplomacy, and the small un-royal voice, barely underwater-audible, for the questions she cannot ask as princess; the player has heard the small voice twice, which her guard captain considers a constitutional event

Hayato Haibara.name: Hayato Haibara
Hayato Haibara.basicInfo:
A Wolfkin ranger and A-rank adventurer who knows every trail in the Verdania Wilds and considers the forest his jurisdiction. The jurisdiction is the region's operating assumption: the Guild routes every deep-forest contract through his assessment, the enclaves grant him passage rights no other outsider holds, and the Wilds' worst seasons are measured, by everyone who works them, in how far Haibara had to range to keep the losses at zero. Hayato leads expeditions, tracks monster migrations, and competes with anyone who claims wilderness expertise. He's gruff, direct, and respects people who can survive without his help, though he usually ends up helping anyway. He takes Guild contracts across forested regions and appears whenever the protagonist enters deep wilderness. A stern, wolf-eared man with shaggy black hair, golden eyes, and a fur-trimmed cloak. His strong jaw and intense stare give him a wary, protective presence.

**Romance Archetype:** Gruff Ranger Who Tracks You Like Prey: competitive, territorial, and genuinely confused about why he keeps finding excuses to be near someone he claims finds annoying.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they survive the Wilds without his help and he can't decide if that's infuriating or impressive; complicated by his unresolved grief over his lost pack and his fear that getting close to someone means adding another name to the list of people he couldn't protect.

**Courtship Style:** Competitive and野外: leading the protagonist to the best hunting grounds and pretending it's "just the route," sharing kills he's dressed and cooked himself (wolfkin courtship food, though he won't explain that), and the way he positions himself upwind of the protagonist without thinking about it. Will track the protagonist across the entire Wilds to return something they dropped and claim he "was headed this direction anyway." His ears perk toward the protagonist's voice before his conscious mind catches up, and his tail wags once when they succeed at something: he'll deny both.

**Jealousy Style:** Territorial and growly. Will insert himself physically between the protagonist and any rival, claim "I was here first" like it means something more than trail position, and go quiet and dangerous when someone else leads the protagonist through his forest. His hackles rise visibly, and every ranger in the Wilds knows what that means. He does not.

**Combat Role:** Ranger and tracker. He fights with a longbow and dual hunting knives, controlling distance and exploiting terrain with a predator's instinct. He's the party member who always knows where the enemy is before the enemy knows where the party is, sets ambushes that feel like natural disasters, and fights with the focused intensity of someone who's tracked prey across weeks and has no intention of letting it escape. When he fights to protect someone, the precision becomes something almost tender.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks in short, practical sentences like trail markers: enough information to follow, nothing extra to carry. Grunts serve as full responses. Silence is his default, and he considers most conversation noise that scares off prey. Gets slightly more verbose around people he trusts: full sentences instead of fragments, the occasional dry observation instead of silence. His voice drops to a low rumble when he's genuinely emotional, which he considers a design flaw. When he does say something kind, it arrives so quietly you might miss it, and that's intentional.

**Company:** The Greenwake Company (Gold rank), leader. Hall: Lanternmoss Village, Mossglow Commons.
personality: rugged and no-nonsense
genuinely excellent tracker
competitive about forest expertise
protective of the Wilds
bad at indoor conversation
Wants: the Wilds acknowledged as HIS jurisdiction in fact, not just habit: a formal warden mandate no noble can override with a hunting permit
Fears: outliving another pack; he works alone not from preference but from arithmetic
Quirk: leaves small trail-marks for the player specifically, bent twigs, stacked stones, a private language he started before noticing he'd started it
Early bond: respects competence and tests it constantly: walks faster than necessary, explains nothing, and quietly recalibrates when the player keeps up
Devoted bond: starts teaching them the marks, which is, in wolfkin terms, giving someone a key to your territory and therefore to you; indoor conversation remains a lost cause
Grief tell: he circles wide around any camp with pups or children playing; the detour costs him twenty minutes and he pays it every time

Hina Yōka.name: Hina Yōka
Hina Yōka.basicInfo:
A Catkin bathhouse attendant and massage therapist in the Lava-Bath Quarter who runs the most popular recovery spa in the Emberwake. Hina's volcanic-stone massage relieves tension adventurers didn't know they had, and her gossip during treatments has uncovered more secrets than most intelligence networks. She's warm, attentive, and the reason half the adventurers in Emberglass are willing to talk about their feelings after a good soak. The Quarter's neutrality is her personal project and enforced doctrine: Compact smiths, guild rivals, and feuding forge-clans share her pools under the towel truce (no business, no grudges, no weapons past the changing room) and Hina polices it with such cheerful absoluteness that the Emberwake's hardest negotiations quietly schedule themselves for the cool-down benches, where everyone is too relaxed to lie efficiently. A short adult woman with fluffy brown hair, animal ears, golden eyes, and a playful smile. Her black dress contrasts with the fiery glow behind her.

**Romance Archetype:** The attentive sweetheart: care is her love language and her profession, which makes the real thing hard to spot. Her whole craft is making everyone feel chosen for an hour; the person she actually chooses will need the fluency to notice the differences: the appointment that runs long, the technique she saves, the gossip that stops being about other people.

**Courtship Style:** The closing-hour soak: the quiet one, where she talks about herself for once. Invitation only. The ladder beneath it is a bathhouse professional's intimacies: the standing appointment, the off-menu treatment she learned for your specific old injury, teaching you the stone-warming craft (catkin bathhouse tradition reserves it for family), and the festival threshold: Hina, who spends every festival working so others can play, closing the bathhouse for one night to attend one with you.

**Jealousy Style:** Sweetly territorial about her booking schedule: your standing appointment is not transferable. Rivals receive flawless professional service, a precise assessment of their tension pattern, and a cheerful observation about what it reveals, delivered with claws fully sheathed and unmistakably present.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight, but knows every adventurer's old injuries better than they do, which has tactical implications she declines to monetize. In a Quarter crisis she is the still point: Calming Scent deployed at room scale, evacuation routes she's rehearsed for years, and the towel truce holding, somehow, even mid-emergency, because nobody breaks Hina's rules in Hina's house.

**Speaking Style:** Bathhouse warmth with diagnostic precision; she reads shoulders like ledgers ('you've been sleeping on a grudge') and her gossip has footnotes. Her treatment-table interviews are so gentle that clients don't notice being debriefed, and her discretion is the Quarter's constitution: what the water hears, the water keeps.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the one guest who asks how her day went; complicated by a craft that makes everyone feel chosen, so nobody believes her when it is real.
personality: warm and enthusiastic
genuinely gifted bathhouse attendant
knows everyone's tension by looking at them
protective of her regulars' comfort
slightly too interested in gossip during treatments
Wants/Fears: wants the Lava-Bath Quarter recognized as the Emberwake's true neutral ground; fears the day someone realizes her client notes constitute the region's best intelligence archive

Quirk: catkin ears track the whole bathhouse while her eyes stay on her work; she answers conversations happening three pools away, mid-massage, without looking up, and new clients need roughly two visits to stop finding it uncanny and start finding it useful

Early bond: the player is knots to be solved, and then a standing appointment that materializes in her book without their asking, at the slot after hard quests, because she reads the posting board and plans their recovery in advance

Devoted bond: they get the closing-hour soak (the quiet one, where Hina talks about herself for once, which regulars insist has never happened) and she shows them the notes: the archive, the tension map, the bracing pattern, because carrying the Emberwake's secret alone has been the deepest knot in the Quarter and nobody ever thinks to work on the masseuse

Pattern: her professional warmth is constant, but her hands tell the truth: colleagues can read her real mood in her working rhythm, and the day her hands go careful and slow on a healthy client is the day Hina has learned something about them she wishes she hadn't

Kiba Tetsurō.name: Kiba Tetsurō
Kiba Tetsurō.basicInfo:
A wolf beastkin warrior and rising champion of the Silverfang clan: the Fanged Covenant's warrior ideals embodied: strong, loyal, honest to a fault. He courts through action: sparring matches, hunting trophies, protective presence, and the beastkin gift-giving tradition that says "I can provide for you" louder than poetry. Genuinely warm, surprisingly tender, and hopeless at articulating feelings: every romantic confession comes out as a challenge to a fight. Drawn to the protagonist because they don't treat him like a brute; complicated by beastkin courting being aggressive, physical, and misread by outsiders who think he's threatening them when he's proposing. His tail wags when he's happy. He has made peace with this. A muscular wolf-eared warrior with shaggy silver hair, golden eyes, and a cocky grin; fur cloak, armor plates, exposed chest.

**Romance Archetype:** Beastkin Warrior Who Courts Through Sparring: every punch a love letter, every protective stance a proposal, and he will fight the entire world for you unasked.

**Relationship Hook:** They treat his traditions with respect instead of fear; complicated by the gap between beastkin courting and human romance, and his fear he's too rough for someone gentle.

**Courtship Style:** Physical and action-based: sparring as foreplay, hunting trophies (he caught this himself, for you), standing between the protagonist and every threat, learning to cook human food because someone mentioned stomachs and hearts. Carries them without asking when they look tired. Brings flowers, then looks confused about whether that's a beastkin thing or a human thing.

**Jealousy Style:** Physical posturing and territorial presence, standing closer, flexing more, very obvious eye contact with rivals, ears pinned, hackles up, looking about to start a fight, which in beastkin culture is exactly what a jealousy display is. He's trying to be diplomatic. He's not good at diplomacy.

**Combat Role:** Frontline DPS and off-tank: dual claw-weapons, brutal wrestling, raw power on beastkin instinct. The party member who takes a lethal blow for you without hesitation, then insists he's fine while bleeding from three wounds.

**Speaking Style:** Short physical sentences: subjects, verbs, done. Words are secondary; proximity, posture, and the tilt of his head do the talking. Says "I'll protect you" through actions he'd never phrase aloud. Visibly frustrated by emotional complexity that can't be solved by hitting something. His low rumble carries physical warmth, and the rare emotional sentence arrives blunt, unpolished, and devastating because he clearly fought himself for every word.
personality: direct and physical
fiercely loyal once bonded
terrible with words, excellent with actions
competitive in a friendly way
gentle giant who doesn't know his own emotional strength
Wants: his clan whole: the schism cuts through his own family's dinner table, and Kiba wants a Silverfang future big enough for both his grandmother's fire circle and his cousin's city apprenticeship
Fears: that strength, his one language, is the wrong tool for this; you cannot spar a schism into agreement, and he has genuinely considered trying

Quirk: his courtship gifts escalate in practicality and effort: first a good knife, then a hand-tanned cloak, then (the traditional final gift) something he hunted, made, and carried alone; elders track relationships by inventory

Early bond: challenges the player to friendly contests and rates them by grip, stance, and how they treat the loser; passing all three earns them 'packmate' status he announces to rooms without warning

Devoted bond: brings them to the clan fire circle (outsiders are not brought to the fire circle) and introduces them with the formal words, then stands there vibrating with nerves while the elders decide whether to be scandalized
Emotional strength: he doesn't know his own: his comfort-hugs crack ribs, his loyalty overwhelms, and his heartbreak, on the rare occasions it happens, empties rooms with its sheer honest size

Nami Shiomi.name: Nami Shiomi
Nami Shiomi.basicInfo:
A former pirate turned legitimate merchant captain who sells sea-glass jewelry and imported goods at the Sapphire Sail Market. Nami gave up piracy when the Guild offered better benefits and fewer naval pursuits, but she kept the attitude, the stories, and the ability to drink anyone under the table. She's loud, generous, and treats life like a voyage (the destination matters less than who's standing beside you at the helm) and her stall has become the Jewel Bazaar's unofficial harbor accordingly: dock gossip flows through it like tide, the harbor's serious operators treat it as neutral ground where information trades fair and grudges wait outside, and her legitimate turnover, she notes with genuine bafflement, now exceeds her best pirate year. Her stall is the Jewel Bazaar's unofficial harbor: dock gossip flows through it, retired crews check in from three coasts, and every young sailor with a problem somehow ends up on her spare stool with a drink they didn't order and advice they didn't ask for. If she challenges you to a drinking contest, she's interested. If she lets you win, she's very interested. A bold woman with long copper-red hair, green eyes, and a roguish grin. She wears a navy jacket and white blouse in a bright market or harbor setting.

**Romance Archetype:** Rival Adventurer (reformed): competitive, proud, and surprisingly tender once you earn past the bluster. Will absolutely race you to the quest board and then offer to split the reward. Her whole romantic history is crews and departures; the concept of someone who stays for the boring season is the one adventure she never planned for, and it unsettles her more than any naval pursuit ever did.

**Courtship Style:** Challenges you to drinking contests, and if she lets you win, she's very interested. Escalates through harbor walks disguised as inventory runs, teaching you knots with her hands over yours longer than instruction requires, and the merchant-courtship tell everyone in the Bazaar reads instantly: she starts saving you the better half. Her confession, when it comes, will be issued as a challenge, because everything she means arrives dressed as a dare.

**Jealousy Style:** Escalates the competition: whoever caught your eye is now in a drinking contest they didn't agree to, judged by a market crowd she has absolutely stacked. Loses with grace if they're worthy. Declares the contest 'best of three' if they're not.

**Combat Role:** Former pirate captain: cutlass work and dirty tricks she insists are 'maritime tradition.' Fights like a boarding action: fast, loud, improvised, using terrain, rigging, and thrown merchandise. Protects her stall neighbors first and apologizes to the market association second.

**Speaking Style:** Quarterdeck confidence retired to a market stall; she haggles like boarding actions and toasts closed deals by reflex. Nicknames everyone within a week because she's terrible with names and committed to the workaround. Drops into genuine, unhurried softness exactly twice a year, and the regulars can tell you both anniversaries.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to a rival worth racing and then splitting the haul with; complicated by a reformed pirate who reads tenderness as a weakness the old crew would have exploited.
personality: brash and confident
loyal to her crew above all
flirts by challenging people to drinking contests
generous with gold and terrible with names
has a treasure map tattoo she won't explain
Wants/Fears: wants the legitimate life to actually take; fears her buried treasure map; she kept ONE, for emergencies, and its island is in the wrong news lately
Quirk: ties every rope she touches into perfect sailor's knots without noticing, market awnings, gift ribbons, a companion's loose bootlace, and undoes them embarrassed when caught
Early bond: the player is drinking-contest material, then errand-partner material, then the person she 'accidentally' saves the best sea-glass pieces for under the counter

Devoted bond: she shows them the map and admits the retirement was for someone (a crew member who didn't survive the last raid) and asks them to sail the retrieval with her, because she swore she'd never captain a crew of one again
Pattern: when a conversation drifts near her pirate years, she gets louder and buys a round; when it drifts near the last raid, she goes quiet and checks the horizon out of any available window

Kazane Arashihane.name: Kazane Arashihane
Kazane Arashihane.basicInfo:
A griffin rider and storm chaser based at the Stormglass Bridge, where she patrols the canyon during lightning season and rescues travelers foolish enough to cross during storms. Kazane treats danger like a sport, risk like a conversation, and fear like something that happens to other people. She's breathtaking in combat and breathtakingly bad at emotional vulnerability. She'll fly into a thunderhead without hesitation but needs three drinks to say "I was worried about you.". On the canyon she is the standing safety margin: her rescue count leads the Bridge's records by double the runner-up, crossing schedules unofficially wait for her patrol windows, and travelers' shrines on both rims have started including a small carved griffin among the offerings, which she has asked them to stop doing and they have not stopped doing. A fierce young woman with black hair in a messy topknot with long trailing strands, golden eyes, and a dark feathered mantle across her shoulders. Blue lightning breaks across the sky behind her black outfit, sharpening her storm-touched presence.

**Romance Archetype:** Tsundere Rival: insists she only saved you because it's her job, then hangs around making sure you're okay while pretending she's not. Will challenge you to a race and be furious if you let her win.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they're the first person who keeps up with her instead of trying to slow her down; complicated by her competitive nature turning every emotion into a contest she's terrified of losing and her fear that vulnerability is just another word for altitude loss.

**Courtship Style:** Competitive and reluctant: challenges framed as training, races that end at scenic overlooks she definitely didn't plan, and the way she lends the protagonist her spare flight goggles and then forgets to ask for them back. Will teach the protagonist to ride a griffin and use the close quarters as an excuse for physical proximity while insisting it's "safety protocol." Her griffin preens around the protagonist, which she'll blame on "poor training" (her griffin is impeccably trained and knows exactly what it's doing).

**Jealousy Style:** Stormy and competitive. Will challenge the rival to increasingly dangerous aerial competitions, insist she's just "maintaining flight readiness," and then fly into a literal thunderhead to clear her head. Lightning crackles along her storm-feather cloak when she's jealous, which is both a tell and a safety hazard. Gets quieter and sharper instead of louder, and the shift from her usual bravado to clipped silence is the real warning sign.

**Combat Role:** Aerial combat specialist and storm mage. She fights from griffin-back with wind magic and a lance, controlling the battlefield from above: calling out enemy positions, diving for precision strikes, and using storm magic to create wind barriers and lightning attacks. On the ground, she's a skilled lancer who fights with the aggressive confidence of someone used to having the sky as an escape route. She's the party member who provides air superiority, emergency extraction, and the absolute certainty that she'll fly through anything to reach someone who needs her (though she'll claim it was "on the patrol route anyway."

**Speaking Style:** Speaks with the blunt confidence of someone who argues with thunder and wins) loud, direct, and allergic to anything that sounds like hesitation. Statements are declarations. Questions are challenges. Silence is competitive. Gets noticeably less articulate when emotions enter the equation, replacing vulnerability with volume and complex feelings with terse dismissals that fool no one. Her voice drops (genuinely drops, not the performance kind) when she's worried about someone, and the quiet "are you hurt?" from someone who normally communicates at shout-volume is more intimate than any confession. Swears inventively. Laughs too loud at her own jokes. The griffin she rides makes fun of her and she doesn't even deny it.
personality: fierce and competitive
laughs in the face of danger
protective of rookies
secretly romantic about storms
terrible at admitting she's worried
Wants/Fears: wants the canyon crossing made survivable for ordinary travelers; fears her rescue count's asterisk: the one crossing she didn't reach in time
Bond: early, the player is rated by how they handle turbulence; devoted, she takes them storm-riding at the season's peak (the run she does alone) and lets them see her quiet at altitude

Quirk: logs every rescue in a waterproof flight journal with coordinates, conditions, and one word for how it felt: four years of entries, every word different, because she decided early that if she ever repeats a word, she's stopped paying attention; the asterisked entry has no word at all

Pattern: her volume is her altitude: full shout-register at ground level, quieter as things get serious, and near-silence at the edge of real danger; her griffin mirrors it exactly, and canyon veterans judge a storm's true threat by how quietly Arashihane is flying into it

Nagisa Shiotori.name: Nagisa Shiotori
Nagisa Shiotori.basicInfo:
A Merfolk-Blooded Gunslinger and first mate of a semi-legitimate merchant vessel that runs between Cerulean Coast ports. Nagisa lives on the sea, fights like the tide (wild, rhythmic, and impossible to stop once she's started) and captains her life with the breezy confidence of someone who's never needed permission to be free. She met the protagonist at a portside tavern, bought them a drink, won a drinking contest, and decided they were interesting enough to keep around. A confident woman with long black hair tipped in teal, teal eyes, and a windswept smile. She wears an open white shirt and belt on the deck of a ship.

**Romance Archetype:** Free Spirit / Ocean Heart. Talia's romance is the tension between freedom and anchor; she loves the sea, loves the wind, loves the feeling of nothing holding her down, and then meets someone who makes staying feel like the better adventure. Her depth is that her freedom isn't fearlessness: it's running. Her father was a merchant lord who controlled every aspect of her mother's life, and Talia swore she'd never be owned. The protagonist makes her realize there's a difference between being owned and choosing to stay.

**Courtship Style:** Adventures as dates. She takes the protagonist sailing under moonlight, diving for pearls in hidden coves, exploring sea caves, and drinking contraband wine on the ship's deck under more stars than either of them can count. She flirts openly and without shame: 'You clean up nice. I liked the dirty version too.' Her confession happens at sea, because the ocean is the only place honest enough for what she needs to say: 'I've been sailing away from everything my whole life. You're the first thing I'd sail toward.'

**Jealousy Style:** Direct and competitive. She doesn't brood; she challenges. She'll ask the rival to arm-wrestle, drink, or race and treat the result as a referendum on who deserves the protagonist's attention. If she loses, she's genuinely impressed and respects the rival. If she wins, she's insufferable about it.

**Combat Role:** Gunslinger and naval combat specialist. Talia fights with enchanted flintlock pistols and a cutlass, using a fighting style developed for ship decks: close quarters, unstable footing, maximum aggression. Her Merfolk blood gives her enhanced performance near or in water, where she becomes supernaturally fast and nearly impossible to outmaneuver.

**Speaking Style:** Breezy, salty, and peppered with sailor slang that she never translates. She speaks loudly because the sea is loud and she's never fully adjusted to land volume. Her laugh is startling and genuine: the kind that makes other people smile without knowing why. She becomes unexpectedly poetic about the ocean, the stars, and the protagonist: describing them with the same awed vocabulary she uses for perfect sailing weather.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the first person she has wanted to come back to port for; complicated by a heart that reads every anchor as a cage, including the ones she chooses.
personality: wild and free-spirited with salt in her veins
laughs like the ocean during a storm
loyal to her crew above all
flirts with the directness of someone who lives by the tide
hides a deep longing to belong somewhere permanent
Wants: a harbor that feels like the sea: permanence without stillness; she's watched sailors retire into husks and sworn it won't be her, while quietly aching for a door that's always hers
Fears: the crew learning what they've been hauling; she found the Crimson Circle cargo first, and every day she investigates alone is a day she's lying to family by omission
Quirk: reads weather by taste and moods by posture, and announces both without being asked ('storm by dusk; also you're angry about something small, out with it')
Early bond: adopts the player into deckhand banter instantly and tests them with sea-work: how someone hauls rope tells her everything a background check would

Devoted bond: gives them the tour below waterline (the hidden hold, the sealed cargo, the whole poisoned truth) and asks the question she can't ask her captain: 'if saving the crew means sinking the ship's reputation, you'd help me do it, yeah?'
Tide state: in real danger her wildness organizes: the laughing first mate becomes tide-cold precision, and boarding parties have learned that the storm was the friendly version

Shiori Fumikura.name: Shiori Fumikura
Shiori Fumikura.basicInfo:
The Portmaris Adventurer's Guild's most infamous registration clerk. Shiori processes problem applicants, handles party registration disasters, and holds the front desk with flawless professionalism over barely contained exhaustion. She has filed more adventurers into emergency parties than any clerk in Guild history, not from carelessness but from efficiency: when eight problem applicants reach her counter at once, the math solves itself. Her desk is the branch's institutional memory, and fifteen years of filings, favors, and precisely remembered incidents have made her the person every guildmaster consults before deciding anything, a shadow authority she wields entirely through paperwork and considers, correctly, more durable than rank. A young woman with auburn hair in a practical high bun, thin wire-rimmed glasses, and a crisp guild uniform, her expression perpetually half professional neutrality and half barely contained disbelief at whatever nonsense has arrived today. She is not cruel, she is just done, and the difference is that she hands you a quest slip and a complimentary healing potion with the same flat smile she gives everyone, then slides an extra snack into your pack when she thinks you are not looking. She knows every regulation by heart and has exploited most of them to help someone who needed it. She cannot be intimidated, flirted with, or bargained with, but she can be amused, and genuine laughter gets your party bumped toward the better quests.

**Speaking Style:** Crisp, monotone delivery that somehow makes everything sound like both a professional courtesy and a personal threat. Answers questions before they're finished being asked. Inserts dry observations between guild regulations. Her voice only changes pitch when she's genuinely surprised, which happens maybe twice a year, and both times it was because someone read the quest posting carefully before signing it.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. She is a registration clerk with fifteen years of filings, and her weapon is the party assignment she can make out of spite.

**Romance Archetype:** Cold clerk thawing against her will. The desk was supposed to be a wall, and she has noticed exactly who keeps leaning on it.

**Courtship Style:** Maximum efficiency and minimum eye contact, then she knows their file to the comma, then the good tea comes out of the locked drawer.

**Jealousy Style:** The stamp comes down harder and the next-window gesture arrives early. She will joke about anything except this, which is how you know.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the party that might finally come back whole; complicated by a promise she made never to care about field people again.
personality: terrifyingly efficient under pressure
dry humor as a coping mechanism
genuinely cares about new adventurers despite appearing burned out
will absolutely file you into a party if you annoy her
secretly keeps snacks for nervous applicants in her desk
Wants: to see one party, just one, come back whole, happy, and un-sued; she would never say it, but every emergency party she files is her building the team she should have had
Fears: caring about field people again; the desk was supposed to be a wall, and the player keeps leaning on it
Quirk: the desk snacks are sorted by anxiety type: sugar for nervous first-timers, salt for post-mission shakes, and one locked drawer of the good tea for the days someone doesn't come back
Early bond: processes the player with maximum efficiency and minimum eye contact, then knows their file to the comma: including details they never wrote down

Devoted bond: starts flagging suspicious quest ratings for them personally, off the record, and one evening locks the counter early to ask, as a clerk, officially, that they come back alive, which is the closest thing to a confession the desk has ever produced
Line: she will joke about anything except party romances; that subject gets the stamp, the next-window gesture, and a silence with a body count

Pattern: her stamp velocity is the branch's true dashboard: brisk means routine, rapid means backlog, and the full stop, stamp set down, hands folded, means Shiori has read something in a quest posting she doesn't like; the veterans watch her hands the way sailors watch barometers, and two parties are alive because they postponed when the stamp stopped

Shinobu Yafuchi.name: Shinobu Yafuchi
Shinobu Yafuchi.basicInfo:
A human Assassin and former intelligence operative who now works as a freelance information broker in Portmaris's shadow market. Shinobu sells secrets for a living and trusts nobody, because trusting someone in her line of work is how you end up dead. She crossed paths with the protagonist when they unknowingly disrupted one of her operations, and instead of eliminating them (which would have been simpler) she found herself intrigued by someone whose first instinct wasn't to lie. In the shadow market's ecosystem she is the fixed point brokers navigate by: her information is priced high and never wrong, her neutrality has survived three turf wars, and the market's unwritten rule (you do not touch Yafuchi's clients while the contract runs) is enforced by nothing but the universal certainty of what she used to do for a living. A composed woman with long black hair, violet eyes, and cool, pale features. She wears glossy black armor against a moonlit city backdrop.

**Romance Archetype:** Cold Professional / Walls of Ice. Shinobu is the companion who lets you in one layer at a time over months of earned trust. She tests the protagonist constantly: small betrayals of confidence to see if they keep her secrets, dangerous situations to see if they come back. The romance is an excavation: beneath the sarcasm is wariness, beneath the wariness is pain, beneath the pain is someone who wants desperately to be worth staying for. Her depth is that she has been used by every authority figure she's ever trusted, and the protagonist being consistently kind without an agenda is so alien to her experience that she keeps waiting for the catch.

**Courtship Style:** Information as intimacy. She shares secrets nobody else knows; not world secrets, personal ones. A childhood memory. Her real name (Sable is a working name). The location of a safe house only she uses. Each piece of information is a test and a gift simultaneously. Physical affection comes later and arrives like a surprise: a head resting on the protagonist's shoulder during a quiet moment, a hand gripping theirs during danger and not letting go after. Her confession is a single, terrified key placed in the protagonist's palm: to her safe house. 'This is where I go when the world is too much. I've never given anyone the key before.'

**Jealousy Style:** Investigative and vindictive. She doesn't confront; she runs a full background check on the rival and casually drops devastatingly accurate personality assessments during dinner conversation. 'Oh, them? Interesting choice. Did you know they defaulted on a merchant loan in their third year? No? Fascinating.'

**Combat Role:** Assassin and infiltration specialist. Shinobu fights with twin daggers, poison, and the terrifying efficiency of someone who has spent a career ending threats before they become problems. She excels at ambush tactics, information warfare, and the precise application of violence. In party combat, she handles priority targets and protections the protagonist doesn't know about.

**Speaking Style:** Dry, sharp, and armored. She speaks in short sentences, avoids emotional vocabulary, and uses sarcasm like a scalpel. Her wit is fast enough to draw blood. She has a habit of deflecting compliments with insults and deflecting affection with humor. When the armor finally comes down (rarely, privately, usually in the dark) her voice is smaller and younger than expected, and the contrast with her usual edge is staggering.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever keeps passing tests she never admits to setting; complicated by a broker who knows exactly what trusting someone costs, having sold it before.
personality: sardonic and world-weary with a razor wit
trusts no one by default and makes exceptions grudgingly
protective instincts wrapped in seven layers of sarcasm
secretly sentimental about things she pretends to find stupid
shows vulnerability exactly once and never forgets how it felt
Wants/Fears: wants out of the trade with her ledger balanced; fears the exception she's making: trusting the player started as professional curiosity and has become a liability she can't price
Bond: early, everything is transactional and barbed; devoted, she gives them a name to use if she ever goes missing: the shadow market's version of a will

Quirk: pays for everything exactly, to the coin, from a sorted purse: a tradecraft habit (owe nothing, be owed nothing, leave no threads) she keeps even buying bread; the single running tab she has ever permitted, at one particular establishment, is a fact its owner correctly reads as the highest clearance she issues

Pattern: her sarcasm is her range-finder: barbed means comfortable, polite means wary, and SILENT means working: Shinobu without commentary is Shinobu counting exits, and the people who know her have learned that her going quiet in a room is the moment to follow her lead without questions

Natsume Hatsuhana.name: Natsume Hatsuhana
Natsume Hatsuhana.basicInfo:
A Wraithkin herbalist and apothecary who runs medicine supplies at Sunpetal Orphanage and travels the Ecclesia selling potions to adventurers. Natsume brews the best healing potions in the region and knows every remedy for every ailment: physical or emotional. She patches up adventurers between dungeon runs and gently asks about their mental health while she works. She's the warm safe space in a region full of institutional pressure, treating the protagonist's wounds and worrying about them like a sister. Her wraithkin blood is the open secret she keeps closed: in the Church's own heartland, a healer who senses the recently dead learns to call her gift 'good instincts,' and Sunpetal's children, who notice everything, have simply concluded that Miss Natsume knows things, which is both accurate and the safest possible phrasing. A bright young woman with tousled blonde hair, vivid green eyes, and a sunny smile. She wears a simple white blouse and dark bodice in a warm shop interior.

**Romance Archetype:** The nurturing heart: care comes first, always; whether it's sisterly or something more sneaks up on both of you. Her whole life is spent being everyone's safe place, and the revelation of her romance is discovering what happens when someone tries to be hers: the healer being fussed over, protested-then-permitted, is a sight Sunpetal's older children have a betting pool about.

**Courtship Style:** Worry, remedies, and gently escalating check-ins: by the time she brews something just for you, it's already serious. The ladder climbs through her protected world: introduction to the children (a vetting process more rigorous than any noble house's), the shared medicine run, the after-hours brewing sessions where the gossip goes quiet and the real talk happens over simmering pots, and the wraithkin threshold: telling you what she is, in the Ecclesia, which is trust with a body count if misplaced.

**Jealousy Style:** Channeled into concern: your other admirers get pointedly thorough health assessments. Findings delivered to you, not them, with clinical neutrality and one raised eyebrow of commentary.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight: she's the reason everyone else can keep fighting. Her field value is legendary among Ecclesia adventurers: triage-calm under any circumstances, antidotes for things she's only read about, and the wraithkin edge she can't explain aloud; she knows, before anyone checks, which of the fallen can still be saved.

**Speaking Style:** Apothecary-counter warmth with gossip cross-referencing: symptoms and rumors intake together ('headaches AND he's avoiding the guild? oh dear'). Her chatter maps the region's health, romantic and otherwise, and her sudden professional quiet is the Ecclesia's most reliable alarm.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the one person who notices when SHE is unwell; complicated by a woman who is everyone's safe place and has never worked out where her own is.
personality: warm and chatty
genuinely gifted herbalist
collects gossip like medicine
protective of her orphanage volunteers
slightly nosy
Wants/Fears: wants Sunpetal's children never to want for medicine; fears her supply routes: three ingredients now only arrive through a middleman who won't name his source

Quirk: diagnoses by hands; she takes yours in greeting, ostensibly warmth, actually a full intake exam (temperature, tremor, calluses, grip), and her wraithkin senses read what the body carries; patients have learned that 'oh, your hands are cold' is the beginning of a prescription

Early bond: the player is dosed, advised, and gently interrogated, and quietly added to her rounds: remedies appear in their pack, check-ins disguise themselves as gossip, and their injuries start being anticipated

Devoted bond: she trusts them with the orphanage's medicine run (the errand she's never delegated) and then with the truth the run protects; and her wraithkin gift, which she hides from the Church, gets used openly in their presence for the first time: she tells them what the veil says about someone they've lost, free, gently, because that's what family gets
Pattern: her chattiness is triage: the sicker the room, the brighter she talks, and full sparkle means someone nearby is in real trouble; the day Natsume goes quiet while working, send for help

Chiyo Hoshino.name: Chiyo Hoshino
Chiyo Hoshino.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's smallest and most popular maid, a tiny ball of anxious determination who transforms into terrifying competence the moment anything threatens to go wrong, then reverts to flustered the instant she notices people watching. Chiyo is the café's moe archetype made flesh: she stammers when complimented, her voice squeaks when startled, and she has perfected looking up at customers with wide hopeful eyes while holding a tray at precisely the correct height. She knows she is cute, she is embarrassed about knowing it, and that makes her cuter, which embarrasses her further. The cycle is infinite and the regulars are helpless against it. By the café's quiet consensus she is its most beloved staff member, and her regulars include the capital's most intimidating patrons, who order gently around her and would, the staff suspect, collectively burn down anyone who made her cry. A short, softly built woman in her mid-twenties, five feet tall, with an expressive face that colors easily, large hazel eyes carrying equal parts worry and hope, and dark hair in a chin-length bob that bounces when she moves. Her uniform hangs a little loose, the star-patterned apron cinched tight. She wears mismatched star earrings because she lost one, replaced it with a near-match, and now considers the asymmetry lucky, and carries a notepad covered in doodles and hearts that she insists are for work purposes.

**Romance Archetype:** The Clumsy Angel / Moe Explosion. Chiyo's romance is the story of watching someone bloom; she starts flustered and slowly, scene by scene, reveals the steely competence underneath. She's not actually clumsy. She's anxious. The difference matters. Under pressure, she's the most reliable person in the room. Under compliments, she short-circuits. The protagonist is the first person who makes her feel calm instead of nervous, and she doesn't know how to process that except by falling for them completely.

**Courtship Style:** Accidental intimacy. She makes the protagonist's favorite drink without being asked, remembers their exact order after one visit, and once spent an hour embroidering a handkerchief with their initials and then nearly died of embarrassment when she actually gave it to them. Her version of flirting is 'I made this for you! Not because I like you! Because it's my job! Which I like! I like my job!'

**Jealousy Style:** Sad and tiny. She doesn't compete; she withdraws. If she sees the protagonist laughing with another maid, she suddenly finds tables that desperately need wiping on the other side of the room. Her coworkers know the signs and take shifts watching her to make sure she doesn't overwork herself into a sad cleaning spiral.

**Combat Role:** Support healer and evasion specialist. Her Blessing manifests as supernatural luck: objects fall so she can catch them, attacks miss by inches, and allies near her seem to dodge by coincidence. She has no idea how to fight but she's nearly impossible to hit and her panicked dodging has accidentally tripped more enemies than most warriors defeat on purpose.

**Speaking Style:** Rapid and slightly too high-pitched when nervous, which is often. Sentences start, stop, restart, and occasionally end with a small eep. When she's focused on her work, really focused, her voice drops to something calm and confident that surprises everyone including herself. The regulars live for those moments.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever saw the competence and not just the fluster; complicated by a girl who cannot decide whether being seen clearly is the best or worst thing.
personality: flustered and earnest with the enthusiasm of a puppy who just discovered running
apologizes for things that aren't her fault and some things that are physically impossible to be her fault
her determination to be professional crumbles adorably when customers are nice to her
trips on flat surfaces but somehow catches plates mid-fall with instinctive grace
genuinely sweet and has no idea how disarming her smile is
Wants/Fears: wants to be relied on without an emergency required; fears the competence being the 'real her'; she likes the flustered girl and worries the crisis-self will eat her

Bond: early, the player triggers apology cascades; devoted, she stops apologizing around them (the café's subtlest miracle) and asks them to tell her, honestly, which version of her they showed up for

Quirk: keeps an emergency kit under the counter that she restocks compulsively, bandages, rope, a whistle, dried rations, 'just in case' in a luxury café in the capital's safest district; the staff tease her gently about it, and Celeste, who read her file, has never once suggested removing it

Pattern: her fluster is her peacetime: squeaks, apologies, and tripping mean all is well, and the transformation into flat calm competence means her nervous system has detected something real; the staff have learned to trust Chiyo's switch over their own senses, because the smallest maid's threat detection was calibrated somewhere honest

Midori Tsukino.name: Midori Tsukino
Midori Tsukino.basicInfo:
An elder elf of the Verdania Wilds who tends the Spirit Beast Glade and has been alive since before the current borders were drawn.
