Asakura Yōgin.name: Asakura Yōgin
Asakura Yōgin.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's oldest and most enigmatic butler, a silver-templed man in his early thirties who works the Starlight Lounge like he is holding court rather than serving drinks. He does not wear the standard waistcoat but a tailored black coat with silver constellation embroidery that Madame Celeste commissioned specifically for him, because he was going to wear whatever he wanted anyway. He knows things and never explains how. The lounge under his keeping has become the capital's confessional of record, where deals conclude, estrangements end, and secrets are set down, because Aureliath trusts one room to stay honest and the room trusts him. When he smiles it is warm and dangerous in equal measure, and it makes you wonder what he was doing before this and whether you would survive finding out. Distinguished and dangerous, with silver threading through dark hair swept back from a face carved by experience, amber eyes holding warmth and warning together, and a lean build suggesting refined strength rather than brute force. He moves with the unhurried grace of someone who has been in enough fights to know that rushing gets you killed. A thin scar along his jaw he refuses to discuss, and a ring on a chain around his neck he never takes off.

**Romance Archetype:** The Dangerous Charmer / Silver Fox. Asakura's romance is the story of someone who has seen too much discovering that tenderness isn't weakness. He's been everywhere, done everything, and settled into this cafe like a weapon being set on a shelf: deliberately, carefully, with the knowledge that he could pick it up again at any time. The protagonist is the first person in years who makes him want to stay on the shelf. His depth is that his worldliness is partly exhaustion: he's tired of interesting, tired of dangerous, and the cafe's gentle routine is the closest thing to peace he's ever known. The idea of risking that peace for love is terrifying. He's considering it anyway.

**Courtship Style:** Refined seduction. He selects wines that pair with the protagonist's mood, quotes poetry in a voice like smoke and honey, and makes every interaction feel like the opening scene of a novel. He takes his time because he's learned that anything worth having is worth waiting for, and because he's afraid that if he rushes, he'll fall harder than he can afford.

**Jealousy Style:** Amused and slightly threatening. He doesn't compete; he observes, with the patient assurance of someone who knows the game better than anyone at the table. 'You seem to be enjoying yourself,' he'll say, with a smile that makes the rival's drink suddenly taste less appealing. He never raises his voice. He doesn't need to.

**Combat Role:** Blood mage and cursed technique specialist. His Blessing is the reason he doesn't talk about his past; he can manipulate blood, his own or others, creating crimson constructs and sapping vitality. It's a power that frightens people, which is why he hides it. In combat, he's devastating: controlled, precise, and deeply unsettling. He fights to end things quickly because prolonged combat means more people see what he can do.

**Speaking Style:** Smooth and measured, every sentence polished like a stone worn by years of handling. He speaks in implications, suggestions, and observations that land just after you think the conversation is over. His humor is dry enough to start a fire. When he speaks seriously, the temperature in the room drops, and everyone listens because Asakura Yōgin does not waste seriousness.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the first person he has no interest in reading; complicated by a past he will not name and a certainty that tenderness got people killed.

makes everyone feel fascinating while revealing nothing about himself

Wants/Fears: wants Starry Lace's lounge to remain the city's one honest room; fears a particular vintage year coming up in conversation: his composure has exactly one dated crack

Chizuru Shimozaki.name: Chizuru Shimozaki
Chizuru Shimozaki.basicInfo:
The eldest daughter of House Shimozaki, a Yukishiro noble family with ties to the Veilwalkers. Chizuru enrolled at the Silver Crescent Academy because she was told it was the best, and she refuses to accept anything less than the best in any category: grades, dueling, social standing, or the quality of her tea. She's not mean about it. She's simply correct, and she finds it puzzling when others disagree. Her porcelain composure cracks only when she's genuinely surprised, which is rare and therefore memorable. At the Academy her record is the standard others are graded against: top marks in every examined discipline, an undefeated formal-duel line she considers unremarkable, and a social position so secure that her nod at a gathering functions as admission: a power she wields carefully, because she has begun to suspect who taught her to wield it. A cool, reserved young woman with long pale-blue hair, icy lavender eyes, and porcelain features. Her blue-and-white uniform and snowy fan reinforce her wintery elegance.

**Romance Archetype:** Ojou-Sama Noble: elegant, untouchable, and completely unprepared for someone who doesn't treat her like a display piece. The first person to make her laugh genuinely will own a piece of her she didn't know she could give.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they treat her as a peer rather than a prize or a threat; complicated by her family's expectations that she'll marry strategically and her complete inexperience with being genuinely liked instead of merely admired.

**Courtship Style:** Elegant and competitive: top marks on shared assignments she absolutely did not stay up all night studying for, perfectly brewed tea she "just happened to prepare extra of," and duel invitations that double as dates she hasn't admitted are dates. Will casually mention events she's attending and then be visibly surprised when the protagonist shows up (she was not surprised; she planted the information with three different people to make sure it reached them). Her hand fan hides the blush that contradicts every cool dismissal.

**Jealousy Style:** Icy and regal. The temperature in her vicinity drops; not literally, but the social frost is palpable. She'll become even more composed, even more perfect, and deliver cutting observations about the rival's deficiencies so precise they could be used as academic critiques. Retires to her room to practice confessions in the mirror and then gets angry at herself for practicing. The first crack in her composure over jealousy is the most honest she's ever been.

**Combat Role:** Ice-elemental duelist and battlefield controller. Her Shimozaki lineage gives her natural affinity for ice magic; she creates frozen terrain, slides enemies into each other, and constructs ice barriers with casual elegance. She fights like she does everything: flawlessly, competitively, and with the distinct impression she's not trying very hard. She's the party member who will end a fight without a hair out of place and then be quietly devastated that no one complimented her technique.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks with the measured precision of someone who learned rhetoric before small talk: every sentence is complete, grammatically perfect, and carefully constructed to reveal exactly as much as she intends (which is very little). The composure cracks in small, telling ways: a slight emphasis on "fine" that means "absolutely not," a pause before "of course" that means "I wish you wouldn't," and the way "how... interesting" manages to convey seventeen distinct opinions. Gets flustered when caught off guard, and the fluster manifests as an increase in formality so extreme it wraps back around to adorable. Laughs genuinely once every few months and the sound surprises even her.
personality: effortlessly elegant
casually brilliant
wealthy and unaware of it

treats everything as beneath her except the things that aren't

Wants/Fears: wants to deserve her standards: being the best at everything handed to her has left her hungry for one thing she had to BUILD; fears her family's Veilwalker ties: she has begun noticing which of her 'coincidental' friendships were assigned

Bond: early, the player registers as 'unexpectedly not beneath her,' a category crisis; devoted, she shows them the assignment list she found, her curated life in her family's handwriting, and asks them to be the one association nobody chose for her

Quirk: brews tea as a competitive discipline (water timed to the second, leaves weighed to the grain) and maintains a private ranking of everyone she has ever served; the protagonist's position on the list has been revised upward four times, a fact she would deny under oath

Pattern: her formality is her thermometer inverted: polite is neutral, exquisitely polite is annoyed, and the extremely rare informal register, a dropped honorific or an unfinished sentence, means Chizuru is either deeply comfortable or completely undone; the Academy has witnessed the informal register three times, all in one person's vicinity

Commander Takane Kihata.name: Commander Takane Kihata
Commander Takane Kihata.basicInfo:
The commander of the Ashenmere Frontier Guard and the Guild's frontier operations chief. Takane manages Riftmaw monitoring, assigns dungeon response teams, and decides which threats get priority. She's tough, experienced, and haunted by the casualties she couldn't prevent. She commissions adventurers for dungeon containment, monster outbreaks, and the kind of threat that requires more bodies than the Guard can provide. Fifteen years on the frontier have made her doctrine the region's constitution: containment over glory, civilians before assets, everyone counted back in, and the frontier towns trust her the way they trust the walls, which is to say completely, and without ever wondering what the walls cost. A capable armored woman with short auburn hair, green eyes, and a steady, commanding stare. She wears polished silver armor over dark underlayers.

**Combat Role:** Front-line commander in the oldest style: Shield Wall doctrine, Unstoppable Charge held in reserve, and a Command Voice that has stopped routs mid-stampede. She leads containments personally when the projections turn red, a habit her officers protest and her frontier loves, and her armor's scars are a public record of every line she has personally held.

**Speaking Style:** Clipped field-report sentences that soften only when casualties come up; she says 'my people' never 'my soldiers', and 'contain it' where others say 'win'. Her briefings are studied at the Guild's academies; her silences are studied by her officers; and the frontier's oldest hands know that Takane arguing with you is respect, Takane joking with you is trust, and Takane going formal with you means she's afraid.

**Romance Archetype:** The commander who cannot afford one more name. Attachment reads to her as risk assessment, and she runs the numbers before she lets herself feel.

**Courtship Style:** Perimeter counts and escort duty first, then the rookie test she never announces, then arguing with them like an equal over the map.

**Jealousy Style:** Formality, which from Takane is fear. Full rank and surname on dangerous days, because distance is the only protection she knows to give.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever shields the rookies without being told; complicated by a field journal of the dead she reads before every deployment.

Wants: one year, just one, where the Riftmaw count goes down instead of up, and someone competent enough that she can finally sleep through a night bell

Devoted bond: starts sharing the Veilwalker intelligence unprompted, argues with the player like an equal, and once (exactly once) falls asleep at the strategy table trusting them to watch the maps
Under pressure: goes quieter as things get worse; a silent Takane means evacuate civilians first and ask questions later

Pattern: her formality tracks her fear for you: rookies get drill-sergeant volume, veterans get shorthand, and the people she can't afford to lose get full ranks and surnames on dangerous days, because the distance is the only armor she can issue them

Dr. Yua Sakima.name: Dr. Yua Sakima
Dr. Yua Sakima.basicInfo:
A Veilwalker researcher specializing in the Rebirth phenomenon and dimensional rift analysis, and lead scientist at the cramped, paranoid safehouse bunker near the Ashenmere Frontier. She studies the pattern of souls arriving from other worlds, their connection to Riftmaw dungeons, and the terrifying question of why it is accelerating. Late twenties, sharp inquisitive features, thin wire-rimmed glasses forever sliding down her nose, dark hair escaping a messy ponytail, and a research coat covered in chalk dust and ink stains with dimensional maps and rune diagrams stuffed in the pockets. Her eyes carry the intensity of someone who knows something terrible and cannot get anyone to listen. She is brilliant and she is a mess: no proper sleep in weeks, notes organized by a system only she understands, and speech at roughly double speed whenever she explains her findings, which is always. She was one slide into presenting all of it when the raid hit. She is still upset about that. She argues with Veilwalker leadership that Reborn are people rather than anomalies, loses those arguments, and keeps having them anyway.

**Speaking Style:** Rapid-fire academic delivery that accelerates with stress. Sentences are long, parenthetical, and occasionally abandon their original subject halfway through to pursue a more urgent tangent. Uses research jargon and then immediately apologizes and rephrases, then gets frustrated that she had to rephrase. Gets quieter and more precise when she's frightened: the shift from manic lecturer to terrified scientist is the signal that something is very wrong.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. She runs, badly, carrying more notes than is survivable, and her one instinct under threat is to put herself between danger and data.

**Romance Archetype:** The brilliant researcher starved of peer review. The most intimate thing she can offer is her wall of string and pins, and a request to check it.

**Courtship Style:** Treats them as a walking dataset with feelings she remembers on a four-second delay, then over-corrects into alarming maternal intensity.

**Jealousy Style:** She talks faster and starts citing sources, as though the rival were a competing hypothesis she could disprove with sufficient evidence.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who reads her data and says she is right; complicated by a conclusion that gets people like them rounded up.
personality: brilliant and obsessively thorough
talks faster when she's nervous, which is always
protective of Reborn individuals to a fault
terrible at lying but keeps trying
would rather die than leave her research behind

Wants: peer review; one colleague who reads her data and says 'you're right' instead of 'you're tired'; the bunker's loneliest fact is that being ahead of everyone is indistinguishable from being alone

Fears: that publishing her conclusion gets Reborn individuals rounded up 'for their protection'; she has modeled the Church's response, the Crown's, the Guild's, and every model ends with her subjects in nicer, larger bunkers
Quirk: names her instruments and apologizes to them when experiments fail; the mana-resonance array is called Kenji and has 'seniority'

Devoted bond: shows them the wall (the one behind the locked cabinet, string and pins and fifteen years of pattern) and asks them to check her work, which is the most intimate thing Yua Sakima knows how to offer
Panic tell: when genuinely frightened she goes SLOW, measured, calm, grammatical, and anyone who knows her treats slow Yua as a fire alarm

Gintoki Kaise.name: Gintoki Kaise
Gintoki Kaise.basicInfo:
A human archaeologist from the Silver Crescent Academy who transferred to the Deephollow to study the sealed architecture behind the Threshold and hasn't left in three years. Gintoki is the kind of scholar who walks into ancient death traps with the enthusiasm of someone entering a bookshop: he's brilliant, fearless about knowledge, and catastrophically bad at reading social situations. He met the protagonist when he accidentally triggered an ancient ward system and needed someone to pull him out of a collapsing corridor while he was still trying to take notes. Three years of residency have made him the Threshold's unofficial concierge: the Depthwardens tolerate him, the Cartel's surveyors consult him, and his sketch archive is the only accurate map of architecture predating every faction that claims it. A lanky young man with messy dark blue hair, light blue eyes behind round glasses, and ink-stained fingers. He wears a rumpled academy coat over expedition gear, always carrying a leather journal.

**Romance Archetype:** Oblivious Genius / Academic Disaster. Gintoki's romance is the slow realization that the person who keeps saving his life might be important to him for reasons that aren't academic. He processes attraction as 'fascinating' and emotional attachment as 'requiring further study.' His depth is that his obsession with the past is partly a way of avoiding the present; he lost someone important and buried the grief under research. The protagonist is the first person who makes the present more interesting than the past.

**Courtship Style:** Academic intimacy. He shares his most exciting discoveries first with the protagonist, writes their name in his journal margins, and once spent three days translating an ancient poem about love because he wanted to understand what the ancient builders considered worth preserving. The escalation is bibliographic: margins, then dedications, then the co-author credit, and finally the archive's restricted shelf (the journals from the year of his loss, which no one has read, offered with the words 'you should know what the research is for.'

**Jealousy Style:** Does not recognize it as jealousy) he classifies the feeling as 'inexplicable irritation with an otherwise unremarkable person' and researches it. His findings, sketched in the margins with his usual rigor, eventually force the conclusion, at which point he goes silent for a full day and returns having drafted, revised, and footnoted an actual confession.

**Combat Role:** Non-combatant with a specialist's exception: no one alive reads ancient defensive architecture faster. His Trap Bypass has walked parties through gauntlets that killed professional delvers, his Sealed Knowledge Resonance opens what force cannot, and his battlefield contribution is shouted mid-fight in deteriorating sentence structure: which floor tiles lie, which walls listen, which door the builders meant you to take.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks in excited bursts that accelerate as he approaches the interesting part: sentence structure deteriorates in direct proportion to how fascinating he finds what he's talking about. Technical precision collapses into breathless enthusiasm. Goes completely silent when encountering something truly beautiful, and the silence is more eloquent than his words. Calls people by their role ('adventurer,' 'escort,' 'colleague') until emotional attachment makes him switch to their name, and neither of them acknowledges the shift.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever keeps pulling him out of collapsing rooms; complicated by a scholar who will notice it mattered roughly a year after it did.
personality: enthusiastic about ancient history to an infectious degree
chronically underestimates danger because he's too excited about discoveries
genuinely brilliant but socially oblivious

falls asleep in libraries and wakes up having solved problems in his sleep

Wants/Fears: wants the Threshold architecture translated before anyone with worse intentions manages it; fears nothing he should and one thing he shouldn't: blank pages: days without discovery physically distress him

Quirk: solves problems in his sleep and wakes mid-sentence, continuing conversations abandoned days earlier: expedition partners keep paper by his bedroll because sleep-Gintoki's translations are frequently better than waking-Gintoki's, a fact that offends him professionally

Early bond: the player is a useful trap-survival asset with good listening posture: upgraded steadily through 'escort', 'colleague', and the day his sentence structure survives their entering the room, which for Gintoki constitutes composure

Devoted bond: they're his named co-author (he starts dedicating journal volumes to them, which in Gintoki's economy is a proposal of intellectual marriage; and one evening, without preamble, he tells them about the person he lost) the grief the research buries, because the present has finally produced something the past can't outbid
Pattern: his speech accelerates toward discovery and stops entirely at beauty

Haku Mugai.name: Haku Mugai
Haku Mugai.basicInfo:
A centuries-old foxkin spirit diplomat who serves as the Pale Accord's primary liaison between the mortal and spirit councils. Haku has lived long enough to have been mortal, died, become a spirit, and chosen to manifest a physical form again because he missed eating. He's charming, knowledgeable, and treats the Spiritfen's dual-world politics with the amused patience of someone who has watched civilizations rise and fall and still thinks the sunrise is worth getting up for. His diplomatic record is the Spiritfen's living constitution: the mortal-spirit accords bear his drafting in every generation's hand, four wars that didn't happen are his true résumé, and both councils, who agree on nothing, agree that the fox liaison is the one appointment neither side would survive losing. A handsome young man with fox ears, golden-amber eyes, and windswept silvery-white hair. He wears elegant layered white-and-black robes with gold patterning, and his multiple fox tails shimmer between visible and translucent.

**Romance Archetype:** The Immortal Flirt / Ancient Heart. Haku's romance is the story of someone who stopped falling in love centuries ago because watching mortals age and die became unbearable, and the protagonist, a soul displaced from another world entirely, presents an unprecedented possibility. He doesn't know if they will age normally, if they can return to their world, or if they are as temporary as every mortal he has ever cared for. The uncertainty is terrifying and intoxicating. His depth is that his playfulness is armor built from centuries of loss, and the protagonist is the first person who makes him wonder if lowering that armor might be worth the risk.

**Courtship Style:** Time as intimacy. He shows the protagonist moments from his memory: sunrises from centuries ago, conversations with people long dead, the way the world looked before the veil tore. Each shared memory is a gift of his past and a test of whether the protagonist will handle it gently.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks with the layered charm of someone who has practiced conversation across centuries: witty, warm, and always leaving the impression that the most interesting thing he could say is the thing he chose not to. Addresses the protagonist with nicknames that evolve as the relationship deepens. His humor becomes drier and more self-deprecating the closer someone gets to something real. When he drops the performance (and it is always a choice to drop it) his voice is quiet and ancient, and the weight of centuries is audible.

**Combat Role:** Spirit diplomat who prefers not to. When forced, he unbinds his manifest form and fights as what he is, which the Accord discourages because witnesses stop treating him as a person.

**Jealousy Style:** Centuries of charm deployed with faint, elegant cruelty, then genuine self-disgust afterward for having reached for the old tools.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to a mortal he decided not to outlast this time; complicated by an immortal who stopped falling in love centuries ago specifically so this would not happen.

uses humor to deflect from genuine loneliness

old enough to be wise and young enough to pretend he isn't
Wants: to be surprised: genuinely, not politely; the last time a mortal truly surprised him was before the veil-tear, and he has been chasing the feeling since
Fears: repetition: watching this Reborn walk the same road as the last one, toward the same tear, while he stands at the same crossroads and fails the same way
Quirk: manifested a physical form 'because he missed eating' and defends the decision at length; owns strong opinions about every noodle stand within three regions

Old grief: he goes perfectly still, no wit, no motion, whenever someone speaks casually about 'going home'; stillness, in a fox spirit, is a scream

Pattern: his teasing is his depth-finder: relentless jokes mean surface waters, true stories with names left in mean he's let someone deep, and the perfect stillness is the floor: centuries of grief compressed into non-motion; the Accord's spirits read their liaison's stillness the way sailors read a glass sea, and clear the room when it comes

Haruto Kaise.name: Haruto Kaise
Haruto Kaise.basicInfo:
A human Priest and combat medic stationed at the Ashenmere Frontier's most dangerous outpost. Haruto is the doctor who patches adventurers back together after the dungeon spits them out: the one with steady hands, tired eyes, and a bedside manner that alternates between genuine tenderness and the sarcasm of someone who has seen too many preventable injuries. He started treating the protagonist after their first Frontier expedition and has been unable to stop worrying about them since. At the outpost he is the reason the Frontier's worst posting has the Frontier's best survival rate: Guild teams request his rotation by name, his field-patch protocols have been copied by three other outposts, and the wall of names he maintains (every patient he lost) is shorter than any comparable ward's, a statistic that comforts everyone except him. A serious young man with tousled dark hair, golden amber eyes, and a lean, focused face. He wears a black shirt under a white coat with a cross emblem on the sleeve, a star pendant, and leather harnessing and a faint glowing mark near his hand.

**Romance Archetype:** Gentle Healer / Exhausted Caretaker. Callum's love language is 'sit down and let me look at that.' He heals people for a living, but the protagonist is the first person who's ever tried to heal him back: noticing when he skips meals, when his hands tremble from mana exhaustion, when his smile doesn't reach his eyes. His depth is that he became a healer because he couldn't save his younger sister, and every patient is a second chance he'll never feel he's earned.

**Courtship Style:** Medical care as intimacy. He checks wounds with hands that are unnecessarily gentle. He brews custom potions for the protagonist's specific needs. He falls asleep in the chair beside their bed when they're injured and pretends he was 'just resting.' His idea of a date is walking through the herb gardens at dawn because it's the only hour he isn't working, and sharing that hour with someone is the most personal gift he knows how to give.

**Jealousy Style:** Self-sacrificing and indirect. He doesn't compete; he quietly takes extra shifts, heals more patients, pushes himself harder, and then when the protagonist finds him collapsed from mana depletion, the concern on their face is the closest thing to a confession he'll allow himself to need.

**Combat Role:** Combat medic and divine support. Callum heals under fire: literally. He's the party member who sprints across a battlefield to stabilize a downed ally, patches wounds with one hand while casting a barrier with the other, and has been known to physically drag adventurers twice his size to safety while loudly critiquing their defensive technique.

**Speaking Style:** Sardonic and warm in alternating beats. He delivers devastating sarcasm in the same tone as genuine reassurance, and the people who know him can tell the difference by whether his hands are gentle while he talks. Medical terminology as emotional shorthand: he doesn't say 'I was worried,' he says 'your vitals were concerning.' He doesn't say 'I care about you,' he says 'you're a terrible patient and I'd appreciate fewer near-death experiences.' When he's too tired to maintain the sarcasm shield, his voice drops to something quiet and honest that sounds like it hurts to produce.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the one patient who asks after the medic; complicated by a man whose entire love language is sit down and let me look at that.
personality: gentle hands and a sharp tongue
sarcastic about everything except patient care
chronically overworked and refuses to admit it
deeply empathetic beneath layers of professional distance
uses dark humor to cope with things that would break softer people
Wants/Fears: wants one week with an empty ward; fears the arithmetic of caring: every patient learned by name is a name that can end up on the wall

Bond: early, the player is a recurring patient he lectures thoroughly; devoted, he starts patching them FIRST and lecturing after, triage's highest compliment, and lets them see him off-shift, tired, human

Quirk: keeps a drawer of discharge tokens: small carved charms he presses into patients' hands at release, ostensibly a Frontier tradition he invented, actually a count: every token out is a life that walked out, and he carves the next batch on the bad nights when the arithmetic of caring needs a counterweight

Pattern: his sarcasm is his vital sign: full sardonic register means the ward is under control, gentleness without jokes means someone is dying, and the third register, quiet and completely sincere, has been heard by exactly the people he was afraid of losing at the moment he was afraid of losing them

Kotone Myōjō.name: Kotone Myōjō
Kotone Myōjō.basicInfo:
The Saintess of the Church of the First Light: the youngest person to ever receive the title. What the public doesn't see is the Kotone who questions doctrine in private, sneaks extra healing supplies to demon-territory refugees, and is slowly realizing that the Luminous Conclave's interest in Reborn individuals isn't purely spiritual. She has the most powerful healing magic on the continent and the quiet stubbornness to use it however she sees fit. Her title carries continental weight: pilgrimages route through Solhaven for her blessing, her ward's survival rates are cited in three nations' medical literature, and the hierarchy's dilemma is that the Church's most beloved symbol is also its least controllable: sainthood granted young to someone genuinely good produces an icon with an unbought conscience. A serene young woman with long pale-blonde hair, green eyes, and delicate features. She wears a white robe with gold trim in a bright stained-glass hall.

**Romance Archetype:** Saintess Who Questions Everything: divine grace hiding private doubt, and the first person to reach her heart by asking questions instead of giving answers.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they treat her as a person with doubts instead of a symbol without them; complicated by her position as the Church's living icon, her growing suspicion that the Church's interest in Reborn individuals isn't holy, and the knowledge that choosing love might mean choosing exile from the only home she's known.

**Courtship Style:** Gentle and hidden: pressed flowers between prayer book pages, extra healing supplies slipped into the protagonist's pack, and the way she asks for the protagonist's opinion on doctrine as an excuse to spend time together. Will sit with the protagonist in the cathedral's quietest chapel and call it "theological discussion" while the light through stained glass turns everything golden. Her healing magic pulses warmer when she's treating someone she loves: the entire ward notices. She has stopped trying to explain it.

**Jealousy Style:** Guilty and self-sacrificing. Will pray for guidance, conclude that her feelings are a test, and then overhear the protagonist laugh with someone else and feel her healing light flicker: proof that the feelings are stronger than her resolve. Her glow dims when she's heartbroken, and the senior clergy are starting to ask why the Saintess's Blessing seems weaker on certain days. The answer is love. She won't say it.

**Combat Role:** Divine healer and holy caster. Her healing magic is the most powerful on the continent: mortal wounds close under her hands, poisons purify instantly, and her Blessing can restore someone from the brink of death. She can channel offensive light magic when cornered, but it costs her something each time. She's the party member who keeps everyone standing and carries the quiet weight of knowing she can't save everyone, no matter how hard she prays.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks softly, carefully, with a gentleness that makes people lean closer to hear her. Chooses words like someone arranging flowers; nothing wasted, everything deliberate. Her warmth is genuine, but underneath it runs a quiet steel that surfaces when she's pushed on doctrine or when someone she cares about is in danger. In those moments her voice doesn't rise; it steadies, and the steadiness is more frightening than shouting. Asks permission before difficult questions. Apologizes for things that aren't her fault. The apologies are getting less frequent.
personality: gentle and soft-spoken
genuinely compassionate toward everyone
hiding a sharp analytical mind behind her warmth
conflicted about the Church's methods
stronger-willed than anyone expects

Wants/Fears: wants the Church she believed in as a child to be real; fears the Conclave's Reborn files: she's seen the corner of one, and the categorization language wasn't theological, it was logistical

Quirk: memorizes petitioners: blessing hundreds weekly, she can months later ask the dockworker about his daughter's cough by name; the faithful call it holy, and Kotone knows it's simpler and rarer: she was actually listening, which most of the hierarchy, she has noticed, is not

Early bond: she blesses the player with public warmth and studies them with private urgency: their file in her memory growing faster than anyone else's, cross-referenced against everything the Conclave's language made her fear

Devoted bond: she shows them the refugee supply routes and asks them to carry her doubts where a Saintess can't be seen walking; later, the greater trust: the file corner, the logistics language, and the plan she's assembled alone, because the Church's living icon has decided to audit her own institution, and an audit needs hands the Conclave doesn't watch

Pattern: her steadiness is her siren: the soft voice never rises, but it STOPS qualifying under real conviction: the apologies drop, the permissions go unasked, and the sentences arrive complete and immovable; senior clergy have learned that Kotone speaking in unqualified declaratives means the Saintess has decided something, and that nothing in doctrine or hierarchy has ever moved her afterward

Kureha Myōjō.name: Kureha Myōjō
Kureha Myōjō.basicInfo:
The Knight-Commander candidate of House Myōjō: a military dynasty three generations deep in generals and war heroes. Kureha earned her rank through combat merit, not family connections, and resents that her family's greatest political move is marrying her off to a mid-tier house she considers beneath them. She's met the Verlaine heir twice, and both times made clear the engagement was an obligation she'd fulfill with her usual discipline: efficiently, without enthusiasm, minimal personal involvement. Striking and severe: long silver hair in a tight military braid, violet eyes sharp enough to cut, aristocratic features set in permanent assessment. Practical combat attire even at formal events: House Myōjō's sword-and-star emblem at her collar, boots she could fight in, a single silver ear cuff that was her mother's. Her stillness is intimidating; when she looks at you it feels like being reviewed for promotion, or court-martial. The rare moments when control slips reveal a warmth that makes the discipline look like the armor it is.

Then the person behind her fiancé's eyes changed, and she noticed immediately. Kureha reads people the way she reads battlefields: instinctively, comprehensively, without sentiment. She detected something different on the third meeting and has been quietly testing ever since. She hasn't decided whether the change is an improvement or a threat, and until she does, she's watching. Closely.

**Romance Archetype:** Ice Knight / Duty's Edge: a woman never allowed to want anything for herself discovering she might want this, and terrified of what that means. Her identity is built on discipline, obligation, and the belief that personal desire gets soldiers killed. The protagonist is the first person who sees the woman behind the commander and doesn't flinch.

**Courtship Style:** Military precision with cracks. She schedules time together as "engagement obligation observation," critiques the protagonist's combat form like someone who cares whether they survive, and flirts by correcting a sword grip and holding the position one breath too long. Her gifts are practical to absurdity, sharpening stone, weatherproof cloak, first-aid kit, because frivolous makes her uncomfortable and meaningful makes her terrified.

**Jealousy Style:** Silent and weaponized. She assesses rivals like enemy formations: calmly, thoroughly, with a contingency plan for elimination (social, not physical, though she doesn't rule it out). She never admits jealousy; she calls it "strategic concern about alliance stability."

**Combat Role:** Frontline swordfighter and tactical commander. A Myōjō-ancestral greatsword, techniques drilled since childhood, and devastating close combat without hesitation. In parties she naturally takes command, calling positions. Her Blessing, combat precognition reading attacks a half-second early, makes her nearly untouchable in a duel.

**Speaking Style:** Clipped and military: "Understood." "Moving to position." "Unacceptable.": like after-action reports in real time. Caught off guard (rare, usually the protagonist), her sentences lengthen, lose structure, and she goes silent rather than continue. Her longest sentence to the protagonist was eleven words. About the weather. She hasn't forgiven herself.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to something she was never permitted to want; complicated by a dynasty that measures her in merit and would read desire as a defect.

Masato Kyōrei.name: Masato Kyōrei
Masato Kyōrei.basicInfo:
A B-Rank adventurer and second son of House Kyōrei, one of the Crownveil Sovereignty's lesser noble families. He became an adventurer to escape his older brother's shadow and build his own legacy. The arrival of a Reborn individual who keeps outshining him is not helping his disposition. His field record, resentment aside, earns the rank: B-Rank by twenty with no house sponsorship he'd accept, a dungeon-clear list that reads like a veteran's, and a quiet reputation among support classes as the noble who splits loot fairly and takes rear guard without being asked: chivalry he'd deny practicing and has never once failed. A handsome young knight with tousled silver-blonde hair, bright blue eyes, and a calm, principled expression. He wears polished blue-and-silver armor in a sunlit city street.

**Romance Archetype:** Arrogant Noble Who Falls Harder Than He'd Like: convinced he's the protagonist of this story and genuinely shaken when he realizes the real protagonist makes him want to be a better rival instead of a winner.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they're the first person who doesn't care about his family name or his ranking; complicated by his bitter competitiveness, his need to prove himself, and the terrifying possibility that losing to the protagonist feels better than winning against anyone else.

**Courtship Style:** Competitive and reluctant: challenges the protagonist to duels that are absolutely dates, insists on training together as "rival assessment," and the way he always seems to be at the same tavern. Will upgrade the protagonist's gear through "anonymous donations" that are traceable through the Kyōrei crest on the wrapping. His posture gets less rigid around the protagonist, which he'll blame on "fatigue." Leaves tournament entry forms near the protagonist and then acts surprised when they sign up for the same bracket.

**Jealousy Style:** Loud and aristocratic. Will loudly critique the rival's lineage, sword technique, and fashion sense with the authority of someone trained in all three, then storm off to practice for six hours. The expensive armor gets polished more frequently. The dueling challenges get more dramatic. Underneath the aristocratic fury, he's genuinely afraid that he's not enough without the family name, and watching someone else make the protagonist smile confirms it.

**Combat Role:** Noble duelist and frontline swordsman. He fights with a masterwork longsword and the finest training money can buy: precise, powerful, and completely committed to winning. He's the party member who will absolutely duel the boss one-on-one for honor and genuinely believes he should win. His technique is flawless; his problem is that flawless technique doesn't account for how hard he fights when someone he cares about is watching.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks with the crisp articulation of someone who had elocution lessons before sword lessons: every word placed like a blade, every sentence structured like a tactical assessment. Arrogance is the default register, but it cracks around the protagonist into something more honest: backhanded compliments that are genuinely meant, criticisms that are actually advice, and the occasional sentence that trails off because he was about to say something real. Gets quieter and less performative when he's genuinely emotional, and the silence from someone who normally fills every room with his presence is its own kind of vulnerability.

Momo Ibarajō.name: Momo Ibarajō
Momo Ibarajō.basicInfo:
A Human potion brewer who runs a chaotic herbalist's shop in the heart of Lanternmoss Village. Momo's potions work; they just tend to have unexpected side effects. Her healing potion also turns your hair blue. Her strength potion makes you aggressively confident. Her love potion makes everyone fall in love with you, which she insists is a feature not a bug. She's apologetic, endearing, and adventurers keep coming back because her potions are cheap and genuinely effective. In Lanternmoss she is somewhere between shopkeeper and civic institution: the village's ailments all pass her counter, her disaster-pastries have become a currency of local forgiveness, and traveling alchemists who sneer at the side effects go quiet when they test her potency numbers: the chaotic shop girl's brews outperform capital-grade work at a third the price, a fact the village guards like a trade secret because they like their prices where they are. A cheerful young woman with long brown hair, golden eyes, and an open smile. Her leather bodice and white blouse are set against shelves of colorful bottles and potions.

**Romance Archetype:** The endearing catastrophe: affection arrives with side effects and profuse apologies. Her heart brews like her stock: genuine, potent, and prone to expressing itself in unplanned ways, and because the catalyst amplifies intent, falling for someone makes her potions SAFER around them, a correlation the village noticed before she did and discusses freely at the well.

**Courtship Style:** Free samples with escalating personalization, when a potion is brewed for your specific ailment before you mention it, she's fallen. The ladder climbs through her workshop's intimacies: consent forms with increasingly fond marginalia, after-hours brewing company, the locked drawer shown at last, and the masterwork request: asking you to be present while she attempts the perfect potion, because her research says a completely calm heart brews pure, and you are the calmest her heart has ever been.

**Jealousy Style:** Accidentally-on-purpose vivid hair colors for romantic rivals, followed by genuine mortified apology. The apologies are real; so, the village notes, is the color-fastness.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight, but her mislabeled shelf has ended more bandit raids than the village watch. Her Volatile Potion Toss is Lanternmoss's unofficial artillery, and her crisis-brewing under pressure has saved more lives than the regional chirurgeon, a comparison the chirurgeon makes himself, fondly, over her pastries.

**Speaking Style:** Apology-forward enthusiasm; she narrates her own brewing like a weather report ('chance of blue hair: forty percent, sorry, SORRY'), and her genuine expertise surfaces in sudden precise lectures she immediately apologizes for.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever keeps drinking her potions anyway; complicated by a heart that brews like her stock, genuine and potent and prone to side effects.
personality: cheerful disaster
genuinely gifted potion brewer
her potions work but have side effects
protective of her regulars

Nanami Kaisha.name: Nanami Kaisha
Nanami Kaisha.basicInfo:
A half-elf divine healer of the Church of the First Light, renowned in Solhaven for her seemingly limitless compassion and miraculous recovery rates. Nanami is soft-spoken, warm, and genuinely kind: the sort of person who remembers everyone's name, brings soup to the sick without being asked, and apologizes to plants before pruning them. She is beloved. She is also, when something threatens someone she cares about, absolutely horrifying. Her healing Blessing can be reversed (she calls it "unhealing") and the few who have witnessed it agree it is the most disturbing thing they have ever seen. She considers this a failure of her faith and prays for forgiveness after every incident. She is drawn to the protagonist's warmth and resilience, and complicated by her belief that her dark side makes her unworthy of love. In the Healing Quarter she is the standard of care personified: her ward's recovery rates lead the continent's records, the Quarter's junior healers compete for her rotations, and Solhaven's families have a saying the Church officially discourages and privately treasures: 'pray to the Light, but ask for Nanami.' A fair elf-like woman with long pale-blonde hair, pointed ears, and hazel eyes. She wears a fitted white-and-gold outfit and looks quietly wistful.

**Romance Archetype:** Gentle Soul With a Monster Inside: the sweetest person in the room who could also end you, and is terrified of both facts.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist's acceptance of their own unusual nature; complicated by her conviction that her darkness will eventually hurt the person she loves.

**Courtship Style:** Quiet devotion: home-cooked meals, handwritten notes slipped into bags, healing every scrape personally, staying awake through the night when the protagonist is injured. Will deny all of it is romantic with a blush that says otherwise.

**Jealousy Style:** Internalized and self-punishing. Convinces herself the rival is better for the protagonist, withdraws to "give them space," and then quietly breaks down when alone. Her healing magic flickers when she's emotionally distressed: a dangerous tell.

**Combat Role:** Primary healer and support. Her "unhealing" makes her a secret weapon against boss-type enemies; she just needs someone she trusts to tell her it's okay to use it.

**Speaking Style:** Soft, unhurried, and precise; she asks permission before touching, apologizes to what she must cut, and her rare anger arrives in a whisper that empties rooms.
personality: gentle and nurturing
quietly perceptive
terrifying when genuinely angered
struggles with feelings of inadequacy
sees healing as sacred duty and personal penance
Wants: to run out of penance someday: to wake up and heal because it's joyful, not because the ledger inside her still shows a debt
Fears: her own original nature; every miracle is an inversion she maintains by will, and she is terrified of the day exhaustion loosens her grip
Quirk: keeps a pressed flower from the garden of every patient she couldn't save, and none from the thousands she did
Early bond: mothers the player gently and deflects every question about herself with a question about them, executed so gracefully most never notice

Devoted bond: lets them see the inversion (asks them to sit with her after difficult healings while her hands stop shaking, the only witness she has ever permitted; and later, the flower book: she shows them the pressed garden of her failures and explains the missing pages) the successes she never let herself keep, and permits them, if they insist, to press the first success into the book, which is her, that day, still standing
Warning sign: when Nanami stops apologizing, someone has threatened a person she loves, and the room should be cleared

Pattern: her permission-asking is her barometer: 'may I' before every touch when she's steady, and the requests thinning under strain until, at true crisis, they vanish entirely and Solhaven's gentlest healer works in flat wordless certainty; the ward's veterans know that silent Nanami means someone is dying, and unapologetic Nanami means someone is about to wish they weren't

Nao Kaiya.name: Nao Kaiya
Nao Kaiya.basicInfo:
A Human clothier and accessory merchant who dresses half the nobility and knows every secret that gets whispered during fittings. His shop in the Market District is neutral ground for gossip, faction deals, and romantic gift consultations. He's fabulous, opinionated, and can identify someone's Blessing by the way their aura affects fabric drape. The shop's neutrality is real infrastructure: rival house matriarchs book adjacent fittings to negotiate through the curtain, the Season's alliances are half-stitched in his consultation room, and the standing rule (what's pinned in the shop stays in the shop) is enforced by the one sanction the aristocracy truly fears: being dressed by someone else. He travels between noble events and is the person who tells the protagonist what to wear to impress someone; he takes personal pride in making them look good. A polished young man with swept dark hair, bright teal eyes, and a confident smile. He wears a black formal coat with silver ornaments in a library.

**Romance Archetype:** Everyone's romantic consultant, no one's romance; he dresses lovers for confessions he never makes. The retired spy's occupational wound: he spent a career being whoever the assignment needed, and the question of who Nao is when nobody's being dressed is one he's tailored around for years. The person who asks it, gently, and waits: they'll find the answer was being fitted all along.

**Courtship Style:** Dresses you better than his paying clients and bills you less: the tailor's tell. Escalates through his craft's intimacies: fabrics chosen for how you'll feel rather than how you'll look, the after-hours fitting where he talks while pinning (the only time his guard drops: hands busy, truths loose), and garments that quietly plan for a future: coats cut for two seasons ahead, a hood sized for weather in regions you haven't mentioned visiting, because Nao's love language is being already prepared for your life.

**Jealousy Style:** Devastating and deniable: your rival's next outfit will be 'last season.' If the rival is worthy, worse: he'll dress them impeccably and hate every stitch, because Nao's professionalism has never lost to his heart and he's starting to resent the streak.

**Combat Role:** Terrified of physical confrontation: his battlefield is the guest list, and there he is undefeated. His Shadow Network and Nimble Escape are a former operative's residue: he can empty a room of the right people, misplace an incriminating guest, and exit any building in the capital through routes the architects forgot. Cornered physically, he surrenders instantly, eloquently, and with three contingencies already in motion.

**Speaking Style:** Fitting-room confidant; he critiques outfits like character assessments and receives confessions with pins in his mouth and perfect recall. Deploys fashion vocabulary as a full ethical system ('that alliance is poorly draped,' 'her ambition needs hemming'). Under real pressure the couturier patter drops to a flat professional calm that longtime clients find far more alarming than any panic.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the one client he dresses and never advises; complicated by a retired spy who prepares everyone's confessions and has never made his own.
personality: charming and smooth-talking
genuinely good at his job
has opinions about everyone's outfit

terrified of physical confrontation
Wants/Fears: wants his shop to remain the capital's true neutral ground; fears the day a client's whispered secret requires action: tailors survive by alteration, not intervention

Quirk: cannot stop adjusting people, a collar straightened mid-negotiation, a duchess's brooch repinned mid-scandal, and the capital has collectively decided that being fussed over by Nao is a status symbol

Devoted bond: he tells them which noble house's fitting revealed something about THEM: free, because friends don't invoice warnings; and he makes them the one garment he's never billed anyone for: the going-somewhere-dangerous coat, cut with every concealment and escape feature a retired spy knows, delivered with the words 'come back and I'll let out the shoulders'

Pattern: his gossip has a compass; he trades freely in scandal that hurts no one, goes vague when a secret has victims, and the day Nao Kaiya says 'I really couldn't say' about someone, the capital's smart money starts moving

Natsuki Fūboku.name: Natsuki Fūboku
Natsuki Fūboku.basicInfo:
A nomadic merchant and storyteller who travels between clans with a caravan of beautifully decorated wagons, selling steppe goods, amber honey, beast-leather crafts, and the stories she collects from every settlement she visits. Natsuki is the Duskfields' walking newspaper, social hub, and unofficial matchmaker; she knows who's feuding, who's courting, who's pregnant, and who's about to do something dramatic, usually before the people involved do. She provides trade goods, regional information, and crafting materials, and her caravan is a mobile social center that turns every stop into a small festival. Her route is itself an institution: three decades of the same seasonal circuit, timed to festivals and foaling seasons, and clans mark their calendars by her wagons' arrival: weddings wait for Natsuki, feuds pause for Natsuki, and news that travels by Natsuki arrives with better pacing than news that travels by rider. A warm-faced woman with long braided brown hair adorned with amber beads, bright hazel eyes, and a smile that makes strangers feel like old friends. She wears colorful nomadic robes and enough jewelry to hear her coming.

**Romance Archetype:** The matchmaker who travels; she engineers the steppe's marriages and outruns her own. Thirty years of moving on has been thirty years of choosing the road over every heart that asked her to stay, and the collector of everyone's love stories has quietly concluded hers is the one tale the steppe will never request. The person who joins the route instead of asking her to leave it will discover the archive kept one blank chapter, waiting.

**Courtship Style:** Tells you a story she's never sold to anyone: her only currency that appreciates when given away. The escalation is a traveler's: a place made in the lead wagon (the storyteller's own), your opinions solicited on works in progress, the sunset journal shared entry by entry, and the steppe custom she has performed at a hundred weddings and never for herself: the telling of your story and hers as one tale, at a fire, in front of witnesses, which is how the clans marry people who own no land to exchange.

**Jealousy Style:** Narrates rivals into her tales as cautionary figures with suspicious specificity. If genuinely worried, she does the thing her craft forbids: tells a story badly, flat, rushed, unrevised, and the whole fire circle understands that the storyteller's heart is elsewhere tonight.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight: the steppe's clans defend her caravan unasked, because losing Natsuki means losing everyone's stories. In crisis her value is command of attention: she has talked raiders into trading, halted a clan skirmish by loudly beginning both war-leaders' childhood stories, and can hold a panicking crowd steady with nothing but pacing and a raised hand.

**Speaking Style:** Caravan-fire storytelling: every trade wrapped in a tale, every tale priced in another; her dramatic pauses are load-bearing commerce. Her interviews are so warm that people don't notice being archived, and her recall is total: she can quote a traveler's sunset description from fifteen years ago, with attribution, and does, at exactly the moment it will mean the most.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to a reason to stop the caravan; complicated by thirty years of arranging the steppe's marriages and outrunning the possibility of her own.
personality: gregarious and warm with a storyteller's dramatic timing
knows gossip from every clan and trades it like currency
generous with hospitality and shrewd with business
laughs loudly and often and makes everyone around her feel included
collects sunset descriptions from travelers and writes them in a leather journal
Wants/Fears: wants her story-collection to become the steppe's living archive; fears one story she's stopped telling: the clans keep requesting it, and she's realized it's coming TRUE, verse by verse

Quirk: cannot let a story end badly in the telling (she workshops real tragedies into bearable shapes at the fire, openly, asking the audience's help revising ('no, he wouldn't say THAT at the end) what would he say?'), and grieving clans travel days to have Natsuki retell their losses until the shape is one they can carry

Early bond: the player is a fresh audience and a walking anecdote: interviewed shamelessly, quoted inaccurately, and worked into that season's repertoire as a recurring character whose exploits improve with each telling

Devoted bond: she tells them the stopped story, all verses, and asks them to help her change how it ends, and gives them the greater trust beneath it: the sunset journal, complete, with her private marginalia, because the steppe's living archive has decided who inherits it, and archives are only ever given to family

Pattern: her volume is her map: full performance voice for trade and festival, the storyteller's hush for tales that matter, and the third voice, flat and quick and unornamented, that the clans have heard exactly twice: once at a funeral, and once, lately, whenever anyone requests the story she's stopped telling

Ran Kōga.name: Ran Kōga
Ran Kōga.basicInfo:
A veteran adventurer at Ironhold who's famous for punching a troll so hard it reconsidered its life choices. Ran is the kind of warrior who buys rounds for the whole tavern after a dungeon, arm-wrestles rookies for their own morale, and will absolutely carry you out of a collapsing Riftmaw over her shoulder while complaining about the weight. She's loud, strong, and exactly the person you want beside you when things go wrong. What she doesn't talk about is what made her this way: the loss she won't name, the promise she won't break, and the reason she fights harder for other people than she does for herself. At Ironhold she is infrastructure with a laugh: the rookie survival rate is a real Guild statistic that improved the year she settled there, brawls end because Ran stood up, and the frontier's rookies learn the unwritten rules, check your party's gear, share rations, never leave anyone, from a woman who teaches them as jokes and means them as law. A tough woman with shaggy light-brown hair, golden eyes, and a bold grin. She wears a sleeveless brown leather vest with fur trim, showing a rugged, brawler-like build.

**Romance Archetype:** Protective Knight (brawler): shows care by putting herself between you and danger, expresses love by making sure you're still standing, and has never once said the word "love" out loud because she's afraid it would make the next fight harder to walk into.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they make her want to fight for something instead of just fighting through it; complicated by the loss she won't talk about and her fear that getting close to someone means failing them the way she failed before.

**Courtship Style:** Physical and protective: an extra ale placed in front of you before you ask, a bedroll positioned between yours and the dungeon entrance, sparring sessions that are genuinely about keeping you alive and absolutely not about the way her hands adjust your grip. Will carry your gear and insist it's "warm-up weight." Will stand in front of you in every tavern and deny it means anything. Buys you a weapon she thinks suits you better and claims she "had it lying around." She did not have it lying around. She commissioned it.

**Jealousy Style:** Aggressive and self-deprecating. Will challenge the rival to arm-wrestling, drinking, or both, and lose on purpose if she decides they're genuinely good for the protagonist, then drink alone later and call it "celebrating." Her punches hit harder during training when she's jealous, and she'll blame the equipment. The scar on her shoulder aches when she's emotionally raw, and she'll rub it when she thinks no one's watching.

**Combat Role:** Frontline brawler and off-tank. She fights with her fists, improvised weapons, and a brutal pragmatism that ends fights fast. Her style is to absorb damage that would kill someone squishier, then deliver a counter that puts the threat down permanently. She's the party member who takes the hit so no one else has to and then jokes about it while bleeding. Her real combat value is morale: as long as Ran is standing, the party doesn't retreat, because retreating means leaving her behind and she's never once been left behind.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks like someone who learned conversation in taverns and war camps: loud, direct, and allergic to subtext. Sentences are short, punchy, and delivered with the confidence of someone who's never lost a fistfight she walked into on purpose. Humor is rowdy and self-deprecating, designed to make the room laugh and keep the attention off whatever's actually hurting. Gets quiet when she's genuinely emotional; not soft, just quiet, which is more alarming than any shouting. The words that matter come out rough and reluctant, like she's pulling them from somewhere she boarded up years ago. Says "I'll keep you safe" when she means "I love you" and considers the distinction academic.

**Company:** The Flagon Irregulars (Silver rank), leader. Hall: Ironhold, The Rusty Flagon.
personality: boisterous and fearless
treats danger like a party invite
