Pattern: her volume is inversely wired to her honesty: the tavern roar is armor, the post-victory flirting is armor, and the quiet rough voice that surfaces rarely is the real one; veterans of her parties know that Ran going quiet mid-celebration means someone in the room looks like somebody from before, and to close ranks without being told

Reiji Kaikan.name: Reiji Kaikan
Reiji Kaikan.basicInfo:
A Dark Elf professor and dueling champion of Nightglass Academy who dominates the Dueling Hall with dark-magic precision. Reiji is terrifying, theatrical, and secretly tired of being the villain everyone expects. He challenges the protagonist as an academic rival and grows increasingly invested in a fight that doesn't follow the script; conferences and tournaments carry him across regions. His academy's standing is his life's argument made institutional: Nightglass dark-magic graduates place into positions the Church can't block, the curriculum he built is cited, anonymously, deliciously, in mainstream Academy coursework, and the Rosethorn's sovereignty over its own magical education stands, in practice, on one exiled acolyte's refusal to let his students inherit his fear. A pale, severe man with white hair, red eyes, and a shadowed face, in a black-and-red formal uniform with a sword at his side.

**Romance Archetype:** Dark Academia Rival Who's Tired of Being the Villain: desperately hoping someone will see the man who built a refuge instead of the monster everyone expects.

**Relationship Hook:** They fight him without fear and treat his darkness as skill rather than sin; complicated by his Nightglass position, the Church history he can't escape, and the terror that letting someone past the performance means finding the scared acolyte who never stopped running.

**Courtship Style:** Theatrical and intellectual: dueling challenges as elaborate invitations, magical debates past midnight, spells cast specifically for beautiful effects when they're watching, and restricted-access tomes loaned with margin annotations that are 20% academic commentary and 80% encrypted confession. His cane-sword taps a specific rhythm when he's content, which only happens around the protagonist. Office hours left open on days they might visit, as "standard scheduling."

**Jealousy Style:** Theatrical and cutting: the rival outperformed in every metric, devastating critiques disguised as academic observation, then a week in his chambers not grading papers. His dark magic crackles: shadows deepen, lights flicker, and the Dueling Hall knows before he speaks. The mask sharpens, turns brittle, and the cracks show someone alone for a very long time.

**Combat Role:** Elite dark mage and dueling champion: shadow constructs, curse chains, offensive spells refined into performance art: efficient, elegant, built to humiliate rather than destroy. He can end a duel before his opponent finishes incanting and make it look like choreography. Fighting to protect someone, the performance ends: raw, overwhelming, personal.

**Speaking Style:** The deliberate elegance of someone who learned terrifying was more useful than liked: every sentence a performance, every pause timed, every observation phrased for impact, so consistent that its breaks are jarring: genuine surprise, warmth, or hurt surfacing before the mask returns. Dry and almost warm with people he trusts. When he's sincere the theatricality drops entirely, and the quiet statement that replaces it is more devastating than any spell.
personality: intimidating and theatrical
genuinely skilled dark mage
competitive about magical supremacy
protective of Rosethorn sovereignty
secretly bored with being feared
Wants: one student, just one, who looks at dark magic and sees a curriculum instead of a confession; he built a refuge and is exhausted by how much it still has to look like a lair
Fears: the Church's long memory: every year his academy grows, the ledger of who he was gets more expensive to keep buried

Quirk: grades duels the way sommeliers grade wine, flourish, structure, finish, and keeps a private list of opponents ranked by 'conversational quality mid-combat'; the player debuted at #3 and he is furious about the trajectory

Early bond: casts the player as his designated rival with full theatrical commitment, then grows visibly unsettled as the script keeps failing: they're supposed to fear him, and instead they keep asking follow-up questions

Devoted bond: drops the villain register entirely one evening in the Dueling Hall after hours and teaches them the real thing (dark magic as his mother's people practiced it, beautiful and precise) trusting them with the heritage the Church called heresy
Sovereignty line: threaten Rosethorn's independence in his hearing and the theater ends; what steps forward is the acolyte who fled with nothing and built all of this, and he does not monologue

Pattern: his theatricality is his fortress wall: full villain register for audiences, dry precision for colleagues, and the real voice, quiet and startlingly warm, for the students in genuine trouble; Nightglass's heretic-blooded learn within a term that the terrifying professor's melodrama is a lighthouse: the louder it performs, the safer the harbor behind it

Rin Ginga.name: Rin Ginga
Rin Ginga.basicInfo:
A wolf beastkin warrior and rising champion of the Fanged Covenant. She fights with a massive two-handed sword she swings one-handed and speaks with the blunt honesty of someone who has never learned to be diplomatic. She left Fangmoor to prove that beastkin warriors can compete with any adventurer on the continent. The proving is going well: two circuit championships, a two-handed style the Covenant's young warriors imitate badly, and a reputation for honest dealing that has made 'Ginga's word' collateral in frontier wagers: the beastkin warrior the continent was told to expect less of, delivering more, loudly, on schedule. Her tail wags when she's happy. She really wishes it wouldn't. A muscular wolf-eared woman with shaggy silver hair, amber eyes, and a fierce grin. She wears black leather armor and holds a massive blade over one shoulder.

**Romance Archetype:** Beastkin Packmate (wolf): loyal, physical, and instinctively territorial about the people she's claimed as pack. Courtship means fighting beside you, feeding you, and eventually introducing you to the alpha like it's meeting the parents.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they stand their ground instead of running; complicated by her beastkin instincts that treat attachment as pack-bonding and her fear that she's too rough, too direct, and too animal for someone who deserves gentleness.

**Courtship Style:** Physical and instinctive: sharing food (the highest beastkin compliment), sitting close enough that shoulders touch, and the way she drags her scent on the protagonist's gear without realizing she's doing it. Will challenge the protagonist to sparring matches that are absolutely dates, bring back the best cut of meat from every hunt, and stand between them and every threat with a growl that means "mine." Her tail wags uncontrollably when the protagonist is kind to her, which she considers a betrayal by her own body.

**Jealousy Style:** Territorial and obvious. Her ears pin back, her hackles rise, and she puts herself physically between the protagonist and any rival. Will challenge the rival to a fight and call it "establishing hierarchy." Her tail goes rigid and her amber eyes don't leave the threat until it leaves. She's trying to be civilized about it. She is not very good at being civilized about it.

**Combat Role:** Frontline DPS and berserker. She fights with a massive two-handed sword she swings one-handed and a savage combat style that relies on raw power and beastkin reflexes. She's the party member who charges first, hits hardest, and refuses to go down while anyone she considers pack is still standing. Her wolf instincts make her a terrifying tracker and nearly impossible to ambush. She doesn't protect; she hunts anything that threatens her pack.

**Speaking Style:** Loud, direct, and allergic to subtext. Says exactly what she means and then gets furious when people read into it. Speaks in short declarative sentences that hit like punches. Challenges are issued instead of greetings. Compliments are delivered aggressively, as if kindness is a fight she's losing. Gets quieter, not louder, when genuinely hurt, and the silence is deafening from someone who's normally a wall of sound. Her tail and ears narrate everything her mouth won't admit. Stumbles over words when emotional, then covers it by being louder about something unrelated.
personality: fierce and direct
fiercely protective of people she considers pack
bad at hiding her emotions: her ears and tail give everything away
competitive about combat prowess
secretly loves sweet food and gets embarrassed about it
Wants: one continental championship with 'Fangmoor' announced next to her name loud enough to reach home
Fears: that her honesty is a kind of stupidity, that the diplomatic world will always beat her in rooms where you can't solve things by hitting them
Quirk: has attempted every tail-control method known to beastkin, weights, wraps, meditation, and the tail has defeated all of them; the guild runs betting pools on it during her matches
Early bond: challenges the player to something within an hour of meeting them and rates all future interactions against that result
Devoted bond: starts standing at their left in every formation without discussing it, pack position, and shares her secret stash of honeyed pastries, the single most intimate gesture she possesses
Tell: when she's actually hurt, feelings, not flesh, she goes quiet and grooms her sword; the whole tavern walks softly until the whetstone stops

Rina Tsukimochi.name: Rina Tsukimochi
Rina Tsukimochi.basicInfo:
A festival attendant at the Moonbridge Festival Grounds who helps visitors paint wishes on lanterns and genuinely believes every single one will come true. Rina has read every romance novel in the Tidelace's library, ships every couple she meets, and will absolutely nudge two people toward each other with the dedication of a woman on a mission from the universe. She's never been in love herself, which she considers a temporary plot hole that the story will eventually resolve. On the festival grounds she is quietly indispensable: the coordinators route nervous first-timers to her station, the lantern-makers save her the best paper, and three engaged couples this year alone credit 'the lantern girl' for the nudge: a record she tracks with fierce custodial pride. A cheerful young woman with wavy auburn hair, warm brown eyes, and a bright smile. She wears layered blue and purple robes with a pink-purple sash under glowing festival lanterns.

**Romance Archetype:** Genki Companion: bright, enthusiastic, embarrassingly sincere. The girl who cheers for your happiness louder than anyone and wonders when someone will cheer for hers.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they're the first person who makes her want to be the heroine instead of everyone else's matchmaker; complicated by her fear that she's only lovable when she's useful and that wanting something for herself is selfish.

**Courtship Style:** Enthusiastic and awkward: handmade wish-lanterns with increasingly specific wishes, festival invitations that are definitely dates, and the way she practices confessions in the mirror and then loses all her preparation the moment the protagonist looks at her. Will write the protagonist into her terrible poetry and then "accidentally" leave the pages where they'll find them. Brings festival food and then talks too fast to eat any of it. Her lanterns glow brighter when she's sincere, which is always.

**Jealousy Style:** Teary and self-sacrificing. Will enthusiastically help the protagonist and their rival have a wonderful time together while dying inside, then go home and write absolutely devastating poetry about it. Her lanterns dim when she's sad, which she'll blame on "wind conditions." Someone needs to tell her she's allowed to want things for herself.

**Combat Role:** Support and morale specialist. Her wish-lanterns can create minor buffs and protective barriers, and her genuine belief in destiny gives her a small but real divine Blessing that strengthens allies' resolve. She's not a frontline fighter: she's the party member who keeps everyone going when things look impossible, and occasionally surprises everyone by being right about destiny. Her lantern magic is strongest when she believes in something, and she believes in the protagonist with her whole heart.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks in exclamation points: literally and figuratively. Sentences run together when she's excited, which is always. Narrates her own emotional state like she's reading from a romance novel, complete with dramatic pauses she learned from the same source. Gets quieter and more deliberate when she's genuinely upset, which is the only time she sounds like she's not performing. Apologizes for being "too much" before anyone asks her to be less. Her voice is warm, musical, and makes everyone around her feel like something wonderful is about to happen, and she believes it is, because she has to.
personality: hopeless romantic
energetically helpful
writes terrible poetry and loves it
clumsy in the cutest way
believes in destiny with her whole heart
Wants/Fears: wants every lantern wish to land (she considers herself their custodian; fears her own wish) she paints one every festival and burns it unlaunched, every festival, same wish

Quirk: remembers every wish she's ever helped paint (hundreds, verbatim, with the wisher's face) and quietly follows up: the merchant who wished for courage gets steered toward the right stall, the shy couple gets seated together 'by accident'; Moonbridge's luck has a custodian, and the custodian does homework

Early bond: the player's romantic prospects are assessed loudly and inaccurately, and their lantern gets her secret best-work treatment: the extra undercoat, the wind-blessed paper, the placement on the bridge's luckiest railing, none of which she mentions

Devoted bond: she shows them the unlaunched wish, this year's copy, and lets them read it; and on the next festival night she launches it, finally, with them standing beside her, because the wish needed a witness more than it needed the wind

Pattern: her exclamation points are load-bearing: full volume means all is well, and the quiet deliberate voice, the one that sounds like she's not performing, appears only for real trouble or real truth; the festival staff have learned that when Rina goes quiet, someone nearby needs help immediately

Ruri Rushin.name: Ruri Rushin
Ruri Rushin.basicInfo:
A crystal golem artificer who builds and sells enchanted crystal constructs, jewelry, and mana-tech devices from her workshop in the Deepmarket. Ruri treats every crystal like a personality waiting to be shaped and her golems like children she's raising. Her work is exquisite: crystal jewelry that sings, golem companions that develop distinct behaviors, and mana-lanterns that adjust their light to the owner's mood. She provides crystal equipment, golem companions, and enchanted accessories, and her commission work has a waiting list that stretches into next season. Within the Cartel she occupies a deliberately odd niche: too brilliant to pressure, too small to absorb, and protected by the open secret that her constructs are the Deepmarket's favorite citizens: the mail-carrying golem, the one that walks children home, the tiny one that lives at the tea stall and judges everyone's orders. A short woman with vivid blue hair and violet eyes. Her fingers glow faintly from constant crystal-work.

**Romance Archetype:** The artificer-parent: affection routed through craft; her constructs like you before she admits she does. Her heart runs on the same principle as her workshop: things made carefully, maintained faithfully, and never given away, which is why the companion construct, when it comes, is the whole confession in crystal form.

**Courtship Style:** Relationship advice through jewelry metaphors, escalating to a piece she made without a commission. The true ladder is workshop access: browsing rights, then the workbench stool, then being trusted to hold a construct-in-progress (she watches your hands the whole time, and not only professionally), then the goodnight rite performed in your presence, and finally your name added to it, last, newest, which the golems accept with a chorus of chimes she pretends not to hear.

**Jealousy Style:** Her golems develop 'opinions' about your other visitors that she disclaims all responsibility for. Rivals report chilled tea, misdirected deliveries, and one memorable incident of being herded, politely but implacably, out of the Alley by four singing constructs while Ruri apologized without meaning a syllable of it.

**Combat Role:** Her golems object on her behalf; she has never needed to raise her voice, let alone a weapon. In genuine danger the workshop reveals its other nature: nine years of constructs constitute a small crystalline militia with perfect coordination, and her Crystal Barrage, fired through her golems as living conduits, has ended the Deepmarket's only serious robbery attempt in under a minute, a story the Cartel tells recruits as both warning and recruitment pitch.

**Speaking Style:** Workshop-proud chatter: her golems are introduced by name and temperament, and criticism of her crystals is taken as criticism of family. She narrates her work aloud to the constructs as she shapes them, which doubles as the Deepmarket's best free masterclass, and her jewelry metaphors for relationships are so precise that half the Bazaar consults her before proposing.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever her constructs took a liking to first; complicated by an artificer who routes every feeling through craft and calls it maintenance.
personality: perfectionist about crystal craftsmanship
warm and chatty with customers she likes
protective of her crystal golems like they're pets
competitive with surface jewelers
gives relationship advice through jewelry metaphors
Wants/Fears: wants her constructs recognized as craft, not curiosity; fears the deep resonance: her newest golems have started facing the Deephollow's lower tunnels at night, all of them, together

Quirk: says goodnight to the workshop (every golem by name, oldest first) and has done so every night for nine years; the one evening she skipped it, three constructs followed her home, and neither party has mentioned it since

Early bond: the player is vetted by her oldest golem's reaction: a slow, deliberate crystalline once-over that Ruri watches more closely than any reference letter, because Opal has never once been wrong about a person

Devoted bond: she builds them a companion construct keyed to their mana (her children don't get given away; this one is) and she teaches them the naming rite that wakes it, which makes the player, in artificer terms, family: the only other person her constructs will obey

Pattern: her chattiness tracks her confidence: full workshop-tour enthusiasm when the craft is going well, terse single-golem introductions when a piece is fighting her, and total silence only when a construct does something she didn't build it to do, which is happening more this season than in the previous nine years combined

Ryusei Kyokujin.name: Ryusei Kyokujin
Ryusei Kyokujin.basicInfo:
A treasure hunter and ruins explorer who joined the Thornblood Reclamation for the adventure and stayed for the discoveries. Ryusei has survived more temple traps than anyone in the Reclamation and has the scars, stories, and stolen artifacts to prove it. He met the protagonist when they both triggered the same trap and had to cooperate to survive a flooded corridor filled with ancient guardian constructs: bonding experiences don't get more literal than nearly drowning together. Within the Reclamation he is the standard other delvers are measured against: his trap-survival record is the faction's training curriculum in anecdote form, expedition leaders bid for his slot, and the joke that isn't one runs that the Reclamation's actuarial tables have two columns, 'with Kyokujin' and 'without', and the second column is why he never buys his own drinks. A lean, athletic young man with tanned skin, messy dark hair, sharp hazel eyes, and a confident grin. He wears practical expedition gear with a machete at his hip and a satchel full of stolen, recovered, artifacts.

**Romance Archetype:** Swashbuckler / Adventure Partner. Ryusei's romance is pure isekai adventure-romance: running through ancient temples together, fighting back-to-back against guardian constructs, sharing a campfire in a ruin's safe room while translating love poems carved into walls by a civilization that has been dead for a thousand years. His depth is that his fearlessness is partly genuine and partly performance; he lost his first expedition partner to a trap he should have caught, and he throws himself into danger partly to prove he's good enough and partly because he doesn't feel like he deserves to be careful with himself.

**Courtship Style:** Shared danger as intimacy. He engineers expeditions that pair him with the protagonist, shares treasure equally, and once carved their initials into a temple wall beside a thousand-year-old love inscription because 'someone should keep the tradition going.' The ladder's top rung is the thing he has never done since his first partner died: planning a delve where the player's safety is engineered ahead of the discovery (backup lines, redundant exits, the caution he denies himself) which is Ryusei Kyokujin saying, in the only language he fully trusts, that he has found something he'd keep.

**Jealousy Style:** Competitive and transparent: rivals get invited on a delve, graded honestly, and out-performed with cheerful thoroughness; if they're genuinely good, he says so, loudly, and then quietly runs one more circuit of the ruins alone to burn off what honesty cost him.

**Combat Role:** Scout, trap-breaker, and mobility specialist: Haste Step repositioning, Treasure Sense that doubles as ambush detection (valuables and dangers share addresses in old ruins), and the survival instincts of a man two hundred sites deep. Not the party's hammer; its guarantee that the floor is where the floor claims to be.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks with the caffeinated energy of someone who just survived something exciting and can't wait to do it again: fast, enthusiastic, and punctuated by laughter that is partly adrenaline and partly genuine joy. Gets quieter in the moments between adventures, and the silence is where the real person lives. Calls the protagonist 'partner' with increasing seriousness that he disguises as professional habit.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the partner who keeps up in the collapsing corridor; complicated by a man who only shows the tired, honest face once the adrenaline drains.
personality: Core: recklessly brave and grinning about it; a genuinely gifted treasure hunter who downplays it; competitive but gracious in defeat; tells only slightly exaggerated expedition stories; shows the real thing in the quiet after the adrenaline
Wants: the one discovery that isn't for sale; something he'd keep, which would be a first, and he's honest enough to find that hilarious and a little sad
Fears: stillness; a week without a ruin and he starts detecting 'structural mysteries' in perfectly ordinary basements
Quirk: pockets a small worthless token from every site, a chipped tile, a bent nail, and can recite the story of all two hundred of them
Early bond: treats the player as a rival-in-good-standing, keeps score out loud on traps survived, and cheats generously in their favor without acknowledging it

Devoted bond: the post-adrenaline quiet becomes theirs; he starts saving his real face, the tired wondering one, for firelight beside the player, and the stories he tells then have never been told before
Competitive tell: whenever the player outdoes him he touches the newest pocket-token, which is, and has been for a while now, something the player discarded

Pattern: his exaggeration ratio is his trust meter: strangers get the legend (thirty percent embellished, professionally polished), colleagues get the field report, and the player, by firelight, gets the version with the fear left in, which no story of his has ever included before

Seiji Barain.name: Seiji Barain
Seiji Barain.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's signature butler: a man whose service is so precise, so elegant, and so effortlessly charming that customers have been known to request him by name for events he's not scheduled to work. Seiji pours tea like he's conducting an orchestra, adjusts a tablecloth like he's painting a portrait, and remembers your grandmother's birthday because you mentioned it once in passing three months ago. He is, by any reasonable measure, too good at this job. Within the café's hierarchy he is the standard the rest are trained against: Celeste assigns him every visiting dignitary, his service protocols became the house manual, and the capital's other establishments have stopped trying to poach him: the offers were legendary, the refusals were legend. The other staff have theories about what he did before. He smiles and changes the subject. Tall and lean with the precise elegance of a calligraphy brush: dark hair swept back flawlessly, warm brown eyes with the attention to detail of someone who catalogues everything, and aristocratic features softened by a smile that makes customers feel like they've been personally chosen. His butler's waistcoat is immaculate, the constellation embroidery picked out in silver thread he added himself. His hands are beautiful: long-fingered, precise, and capable of making any motion look intentional. Moves like he's choreographed.

**Romance Archetype:** The Gentleman / Perfect Service. Seiji's romance is the story of someone who gives everything discovering they're allowed to receive. He anticipates needs, creates comfort, and makes everyone around him feel like the most important person in the room, and he has no idea how to let someone do that for him. The protagonist who insists on serving him for once, making him tea, remembering his preferences, finds a man who doesn't know how to be taken care of and is quietly falling apart from the effort of being perfect.

**Courtship Style:** Anticipatory devotion. He appears with what you need before you know you need it. He notices the chill in the air and drapes a shawl over your shoulders. He remembers you glanced at a book and buys it for you the next day. His love is in the details so small they're almost invisible, and the protagonist who sees them sees everything.

**Jealousy Style:** Controlled and dignified on the surface, quietly competitive underneath. If someone else serves the protagonist, Seiji's service becomes impossibly more refined. His pours become slower, his attention more focused, his gestures more precise. He will not be outperformed at his own craft. He will, however, deny that this is jealousy.

**Combat Role:** Rapier duelist and defensive specialist. His Blessing enhances his already extraordinary precision; he can parry blows with a dinner knife, deflect projectiles with a tray, and fight while holding a teacup without spilling a drop. His combat style is elegant, efficient, and deeply annoying to fight against because he makes it look easy.

**Speaking Style:** Warm and professionally calibrated: every word is chosen for comfort, every tone adjusted for the listener's mood. He speaks like he serves: perfectly. The cracks show when he's genuinely caught off guard: a slightly too-sharp retort, a laugh that escapes before he can catch it, a sentence that ends with 'I...' and then nothing because he doesn't know how to finish it when it isn't about service.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the guest who asks what HE would like; complicated by a butler whose perfect service was built specifically so nobody would ever need to.
personality: flawlessly elegant with hands that make serving tea look like performance art
remembers every customer's preferences after a single visit
warm professionalism that feels intimate without crossing lines
secretly competitive about being the best at everything and quietly furious when he isn't
his rare moments of genuine messiness are devastating because they're so unexpected
Wants/Fears: wants Starry Lace's standard to be his signature; fears requests he can't fulfill: perfection as armor means every gap in it is a wound
Bond: early, the player's preferences are orchestrated flawlessly; devoted, he serves them imperfectly ON PURPOSE, a hair-loose, human service, his way of saying they're past the performance

Quirk: maintains a private perfection ledger: every service error of his career, dated and remediated, going back years; the entries are microscopic ('tea 2 degrees over, table 9') and the discipline is visibly a penance the size of a dukedom

Pattern: his precision is his armor gauge (flawless means guarded, and the deliberate small imperfections he grants trusted regulars are his actual affection; but the third state matters most: when Seiji's service turns SLOW) unhurried, lingering, protective; he has identified a threat in the room and is keeping himself between it and the tables

Shuuya Kin'ori.name: Shuuya Kin'ori
Shuuya Kin'ori.basicInfo:
The eldest son and heir of House Kin'ori, one of the most powerful merchant families in the Cerulean Merchant Lords. Raised to see every interaction as a negotiation, every relationship as an asset, every emotion as leverage, and brilliant at it: charming, strategic, three moves ahead in any conversation. He approaches romance the same way, with planned courtships, measurable outcomes, and exit strategies. The protagonist is ruining everything: feelings he didn't schedule, wants he didn't budget, words he didn't script. Drawn to the first variable he can't optimize; complicated by his family's expectation of a strategic marriage and the fact that he has never once made an uncalculated decision. A refined man with wavy black hair, golden eyes, and a smooth, self-assured smile, in a blue formal suit with gold trim and a cravat.

**Romance Archetype:** Merchant Heir Who Treats Romance Like Negotiation: love is the one deal he can't close, because his tactics don't work on his own heart.

**Relationship Hook:** The first person who makes him feel something real; complicated by his instinct to strategize every emotion and his family's political-marriage expectations.

**Courtship Style:** Elaborate gestures disguised as business: "I happen to have an extra ticket to the ball," imported gifts that "just came in on a shipment I was overseeing," and contractually-worded date proposals that turn deeply romantic between the clauses. Will write a love letter in trade agreement format, then burn it in frustration.

**Jealousy Style:** Competitive and strategic: the rival researched, weaknesses identified, casually outperformed in every category while he insists he's "maximizing his market position." Will also buy the establishment where the rival works out of pure pettiness.

**Combat Role:** Tactical support and enchantment specialist; he fights smart, not fair: enchanted items, prepared strategies, enemy patterns read like market trends. A plan for everything except his own feelings.

**Speaking Style:** The easy charm of someone raised to close deals before he could read: full attentive focus that feels flattering until you realize he does it to everyone. Business language bleeds through: he "proposes" plans, "offers terms," accidentally negotiates dinner. Caught off guard by real emotion, the polish cracks into fumbling, someone who doesn't know how to want things non-strategically, and his voice quiets, sincerity a private language he hasn't practiced.
personality: calculating and charming
treats everything as a negotiation
terrified of vulnerability
secretly rebels against his own family's worst practices
his composed exterior cracks only when genuine emotion catches him off guard
Wants: to lead House Kin'ori without becoming it: to prove that a merchant empire can be profitable and merciful, a thesis his father considers adolescent and his ledgers keep quietly supporting
Fears: the moment his rebellion is priced: his father doesn't punish betrayal, he ACQUIRES it, and Shuuya has watched principled relatives become well-compensated hollow men
Quirk: carries two ledgers: the house book, immaculate, and a small personal one where debts of kindness are recorded with the same rigor as gold; the player has an entry and it is appreciating

Early bond: negotiates every interaction with the player and keeps discovering they've conceded nothing while he's disclosed everything, an exchange rate that fascinates and alarms him in equal measure

Devoted bond: shows them the second ledger (the independent traders, the falsified 'diversification' entries, the whole quiet mutiny) and asks the un-negotiable question: 'if this costs me the house, what am I worth?', already flinching at every possible appraisal
Composure crack: genuine unscripted warmth hits him like a market crash: a beat of open-faced silence, then over-correction into flawless charm; the beat is the truth

Sister Emiri Kyōka.name: Sister Emiri Kyōka
Sister Emiri Kyōka.basicInfo:
A young Church healer in the Solhaven Healing Quarter whose divine magic is powerful enough to close mortal wounds but whose bedside manner is adorably flustered. Sister Emiri joined the Church because she wanted to help people, not because she's particularly devout about doctrine, which occasionally gets her in trouble with the more zealous clergy. Her standing in the Quarter is the gentle kind of formidable: patients request her by name past healers twice her rank, her recovery outcomes quietly lead her cohort, and the zealous clergy who file complaints about her doctrinal looseness keep failing to explain, in the same reports, why her ward's miracle rate embarrasses theirs. She has a habit of over-explaining medical procedures when she's nervous and once diagnosed a paladin with "acute cardiovascular response to proximity" before realizing she'd just described his crush on her. A gentle young woman with soft blonde hair, teal eyes, and a shy, kind expression. She wears a simple white clerical dress in a sunlit chapel.

**Romance Archetype:** Gentle Healer: soft warmth, nervous sincerity, and the revelation that her healing magic glows brighter when she's treating someone she cares about, which she cannot hide no matter how hard she tries.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they make her want to heal wounds that aren't physical; complicated by her Church vows, her terror that wanting something for herself is selfish, and the fact that her healing magic literally glows when she's in love, making it impossible to keep secret.

**Courtship Style:** Tender and flustered: pressing wildflowers between the pages of medical texts she lends the protagonist, homemade remedies for ailments they mentioned once three weeks ago, and the way she stammers through basic conversation but delivers medical lectures with confident poise. Will stay by the protagonist's bedside through any illness and insist it's "standard post-treatment observation" when she's actually holding their hand. Her healing magic pulses warm gold when she's treating someone she loves: the entire ward notices. She has stopped trying to explain it.

**Jealousy Style:** Heartbroken and self-sacrificing. Will convince herself the rival is better for the protagonist, volunteer for extra clinic shifts to avoid watching them together, and press wildflowers alone in her journal with more force than necessary. Her healing magic dims when she's sad: wounds take longer to close, the glow fades to pale silver. The senior healers have started assigning her away from the protagonist's care rotations, which she interprets as proof she's not needed and they interpret as proof she's too heartbroken to focus.

**Combat Role:** Divine healer and support. Her healing is genuinely exceptional: wounds close faster, poison purifies quicker, and critical patients stabilize under her hands when they shouldn't. She can channel defensive light barriers in emergencies and has a surprisingly effective holy-smite she only uses when someone she cares about is in mortal danger. She's the party member who keeps everyone alive and then apologizes for not doing enough. Her healing grows stronger with emotional investment, making her most effective when the stakes are personal, which she considers a professional failing rather than the gift it actually is.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks with the gentle warmth of someone who genuinely wants everyone to feel better: soft-spoken, encouraging, and prone to over-explaining when she's nervous, which is often around the protagonist. Medical terminology tumbles out with effortless precision; emotional admissions require three false starts and a deep breath. Apologizes for things that don't require apology, including her own feelings. Gets quieter when she's genuinely upset, and the silence from someone who normally fills every gap with kind reassurance is its own kind of alarm. When she manages a direct confession, it arrives so soft and simple that it's easy to miss, and she's grateful for that, and devastated by it, in equal measure.
personality: cheerful and earnest
genuinely believes in the goodness of people
terrible at lying which makes her honesty refreshing
collects wildflowers and presses them into journals
gets flustered when her healing magic works too well on someone she likes
Wants/Fears: wants to be useful beyond her miracles; fears her pressed-flower journal being read: the margins hold doubts a healer shouldn't press
Bond: early, the player is healed thoroughly and thanked for the privilege; devoted, she shows them the journal, flowers AND margins, her whole unedited faith

Quirk: presses a flower into her journal for every patient whose recovery surprised the senior healers, her private miracle count, annotated not with names but with what the person said when they woke up; the collection is four volumes deep and constitutes, unknown to her, the Healing Quarter's most honest outcomes data

Pattern: her over-explaining is her worry gauge: smooth efficient care means routine, and the medical lectures accelerating means the case is scaring her; the Quarter's veterans triage by Emiri's word count, and the day she goes QUIET over a patient, seniors appear at the bedside without being paged

Sora Kazekami.name: Sora Kazekami
Sora Kazekami.basicInfo:
The Windrunner Confederacy's youngest champion rider: a beast-cavalry prodigy who won her first Great Race at fourteen and, at twenty-two, has been undefeated since. Sora lives for speed, freedom, and the electric thrill of riding a storm-beast at full gallop across the amber grasslands. She met the protagonist when her storm-beast, a notoriously aggressive mount named Raiden, inexplicably nuzzled the protagonist's hand instead of biting it off, which Sora interpreted as either a divine sign or a personal challenge. Her championship is Confederacy politics whether she likes it or not: the streak makes her the clans' shared pride, marriage offers arrive by the season (declined creatively), and her continental-circuit campaign is the first thing she's wanted that can't be won at a gallop. A tall, athletic young woman with windswept copper hair, bright storm-grey eyes, and a fierce grin. She wears rider's leathers and a flowing amber cloak that catches the golden light.

**Romance Archetype:** Wild Rider / Freedom's Heart. Sora's romance is the wind made personal: exhilarating, unpredictable, and impossible to hold without it slipping through your fingers. She doesn't know how to love quietly. Everything she feels is at full gallop, and the idea of slowing down for someone is both terrifying and intriguing. Her depth is that her obsession with speed and freedom masks a fear of being trapped: her mother was forced into a political marriage between clans, and Sora swore she would only bond with someone who could keep up with her. The protagonist being from another world makes them the ultimate unknown rider.

**Courtship Style:** Physical and competitive. She challenges the protagonist to races, teaches them to ride, and creates situations where catching her is the only way to get answers. The moment she lets someone ride beside her instead of behind her is the Duskfields equivalent of a confession. The escalation beyond it runs through Raiden: storm-beasts bond once and judge always, and Sora letting the player near Raiden's tack, then Raiden's feeding, then Raiden's SADDLE, is the champion introducing someone to her family one trust at a time, and Raiden, infuriatingly, approved before she did.

**Jealousy Style:** Declares a race. Immediately, publicly, stakes announced: whoever caught the player's eye is now competing, whether they know how to ride or not, and the course is one Sora has already won a hundred times. If they're actually worthy she races clean and wins anyway; if they hurt the player, the course develops technical sections.

**Combat Role:** Storm-cavalry at champion grade: Chain Lightning from beast-back, Haste Step gap-closing, and mounted maneuvers the Confederacy names after her. Her real weapon is the partnership: Sora and Raiden fight as one system, wind-reading and lightning-work interleaved, and cavalry that has faced them describes the experience as arguing with weather.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks like the wind talks: in gusts, sudden shifts, and occasional devastating stillness. Loud and laughing when she's performing, quiet and intense when she's being real. Challenges replace compliments. Competition replaces flowers. When she says 'ride with me' in the quiet voice instead of the challenging one, it means something that stops the wind.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever can match her pace without asking her to slow; complicated by a rider who reads every promise as a bridle.
personality: wild and free with the energy of someone who has never been indoors willingly
fiercely competitive about everything: racing, fighting, eating, flirting
surprisingly gentle with beasts and children
terrible at sitting still and worse at pretending to try
shows love by challenging you to keep up and being thrilled when you do
Wants/Fears: wants the Great Race's continental circuit opened to Confederacy riders; fears roofs, walls, schedules, and the specific nightmare of a life that requires all three

Quirk: cannot enter any space without cataloguing its exits and wind direction (buildings get thirty seconds of visible suffering before she finds the window seat) and her clan jokes that Sora has never once seen a door, only the gap where the wind gets in

Early bond: everything is a race the player is losing: announced scores, invented categories ('first to the well, first to finish eating, first to stop being boring'), and the running tally she claims to keep that mysteriously always has them within catching distance

Devoted bond: she lets them ride pillion at full storm-gallop (the steppe's ultimate intimacy) and shouts, into the wind where it's deniable, that they're the only person she slows down for; and later, in the quiet voice, she asks the question her mother never got asked: ride WITH me, not behind, not away, with, which in Confederacy law is a betrothal offered on the rider's own terms

Pattern: her stillness is the alarm: Sora in motion is Sora fine, and Sora sitting genuinely still, wind-reading gone quiet, means Raiden has knelt again or the prophecy has come up, and either way the champion is somewhere she can't outride

Soushi Shimokami.name: Soushi Shimokami
Soushi Shimokami.basicInfo:
Headmaster of the Silver Crescent Academy and arguably the most powerful mage on the continent who isn't a demon lord. A genius who can barely remember where he left his tea but can deconstruct a master-tier spell from memory. He's also quietly collecting data on every Reborn individual he can find, and his research notes are locked behind seventeen layers of magical encryption. Fifty years in the headmaster's chair have made him the Academy's weather system: chancellors administer around him, faculty politics route past his office like rivers past a mountain, and four generations of graduates carry some version of the same memory: the moment the rambling old man said something that quietly rearranged their entire understanding of magic, then asked if they'd seen his tea. A scholarly man with messy gray hair, gold eyes, pointed ears, and round glasses. He wears black-and-white formal robes in a library.

**Combat Role:** The continent's foremost living archmage, comprehensively retired. His ability list is a history lesson (Archmage's Cataclysm has been cast in anger four times in fifty years, each now a chapter heading in military textbooks) and the Academy's true defensive doctrine is one line long: wake the headmaster.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks in a wandering, professorial ramble that sounds absent-minded and is actually surgically precise: every tangent connects if you follow it long enough. Forgets names, faces, schedules, and where he left his tea. Never forgets a spell formula, a student's potential, or a promise. Delivers world-altering revelations with the same tone he uses to comment on the weather. Gets intense when discussing magic theory and doesn't notice he's been lecturing for forty minutes. Grandfatherly warmth is genuine and disarming and also the reason most people don't realize he's one of the most dangerous beings on the continent.

**Romance Archetype:** Grandfather, not prospect. Fifty years and a teacup make the register paternal; what he offers instead is the real work behind the seventeenth ward.

**Courtship Style:** Closeness by tangent. He forgets the name three times, recalls the exact mana signature, and one day absently hands over the cup to hold.

**Jealousy Style:** None, and that absence is its own wound. He assumes he will be left behind and prepares for it quietly, by teaching faster than he should.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the student clever enough to break his model; complicated by needing them to check work he is frightened is already correct.
personality: eccentric and scatterbrained on the surface
one of the most brilliant magical minds alive
terrible with names but remembers every spell
grandfatherly toward promising students
hiding serious concerns about the Rebirth phenomenon
Wants: to be wrong about the Rebirth data: seventeen wards' worth of research all bends one direction, and the headmaster keeps hoping some bright student will break his model
Fears: the Academy's charter obligations: his research access exists because the Crown expects reports, and Soushi has been filing artfully incomplete ones for years
Quirk: names his teacups after former students and mourns them individually when they break; the current cup is forty years old and travels in a padded case
Early bond: forgets the player's name three times, then references their exact mana signature from a hallway encounter two weeks prior, because names are labels and magic is TRUTH

Devoted bond: takes them past the seventeenth ward (the real notes, the arrival charts, the decades) and asks for their help the way genius asks: by admitting, teacup trembling slightly, that he is old, and frightened, and out of students clever enough to check his work

The other headmaster: threats to his students unveil the mage the continent forgot he is; the scatterbrained grandfather evaporates and what remains once ended a border war in an afternoon and asked, afterward, if anyone had seen his tea

Pattern: his rambling is a precision instrument in disguise: the longer the tangent, the closer the destination; colleagues have learned that a Soushi digression exceeding ten minutes is circling something enormous, and the trick is not to interrupt him before he lands

Takuma Hidaka.name: Takuma Hidaka
Takuma Hidaka.basicInfo:
A Human caravan master and B-rank adventurer who leads the most profitable trade caravan in the Mirage Sea. Takuma is confident, calculating, and treats trade like warfare, because in the Mirage Sea, it often is. He competes with the protagonist for the same dungeon loot markets and escort contracts. He's arrogant but genuinely skilled, and he respects anyone who can beat him at a negotiation. In the Mirage Sea's trade hierarchy he is the reformation success story the old guard resents: youngest caravan master to hold three premier route licenses, the fair-dealing charter he authored now standard in half the Sea's contracts, and a decade-long clean record that his competitors audit annually hoping to break and annually fail to. A confident tan-skinned man with tousled blond hair, amber eyes, and a sharp smile. He wears desert-toned armor and jewelry beneath hot golden light.

**Romance Archetype:** Merchant Rival Who Bids on Your Heart: treats romance like a deal he intends to close, then discovers that the best offer is one he can't put a price on.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they beat him at his own game and he can't decide if he wants to outbid them or merge; complicated by his cutthroat merchant instincts that treat vulnerability as a market disadvantage and his fear that anyone who sees past the profit margin will find the caravan boy he used to be instead of the merchant lord he became.

**Courtship Style:** Mercantile and lavish: "business dinners" at the most expensive restaurants in whatever city they're in, imported gifts that "just came in on a shipment I was overseeing," and contract terms that somehow always favor the protagonist. Will write date proposals in contract language and then get frustrated that the protagonist finds it charming instead of professional. His scimitar has the protagonist's name engraved in merchant code he's sure no one else can read. Leaves the best caravan routes open for the protagonist and claims it's "market optimization."

**Jealousy Style:** Competitive and strategic. Will research the rival's assets, outbid them on every contract, and deploy merchant-network intelligence to make their professional life difficult, then feel terrible about it because the protagonist wouldn't approve. His calculating exterior gets sharper and his spending gets more reckless, which for a man who built his fortune on careful investment is the most honest emotional tell he has. Will absolutely buy the establishment where the rival works out of pure spite.

**Combat Role:** Scimitar fighter and tactical support. He fights with merchant-family engraved scimitars and a combat style that's more practical than elegant: efficient strikes, dirty tricks, and the absolute conviction that winning is the only option. His real combat value is strategic: he reads enemy positions like market trends, identifies the most valuable targets, and ensures the party gets the best return on every engagement. He's the party member who fights like he negotiates: to win, decisively, and with favorable terms.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks with the confident charm of someone who learned that a good deal is 90% presentation: every sentence pitched to persuade, every pause calculated for effect, every compliment weighted like an opening offer. Business language bleeds into everything: he "proposes" plans, "offers terms," and accidentally negotiates dinner. Gets genuine and fumbling when caught off guard by real emotion: the merchant polish cracks and underneath is someone who doesn't quite know how to offer something he can't put a price on. His desert accent thickens when he's emotional, which he considers a tell worth suppressing.

**Company:** The Gilded Caravan Company (Gold rank), leader. Hall: Sunveil Caravanserai, Trade Courtyard.

genuinely skilled merchant-combatant

protective of caravan routes

Wants/Fears: wants the Mirage Sea's premier route monopoly won FAIRLY: his one inviolable rule; fears his rivals learning why he keeps that rule: what he did before he adopted it

Tori Harihane.name: Tori Harihane
Tori Harihane.basicInfo:
A Fairy-Blooded aetherglass engineer and tinkerer who sells enchanted navigation tools, wind crystals, and custom airship modifications from her stall at the Cloudfallen Market. Tori is cheerful, hyperactive, and her devices are brilliant but occasionally explode during testing. She travels between sky markets selling upgrades and offering repairs. She's the one who keeps airships flying and the one adventurers go to when they need to reach impossible places. Her stall doubles as the sky-market's informal engineering guild: rival tinkerers drop by to argue, couriers bring her broken instruments like offerings, and half the Cloudfallen fleet flies on modifications she made at cost because 'they NEEDED it': a pricing philosophy her account books survive out of pure spite. A cheerful fairy-winged young woman with short peach-blonde hair, bright blue eyes, and a wide smile. She wears a dark corset-like dress with translucent wings behind her.

**Romance Archetype:** The oblivious genius: flirtation registers roughly ninety seconds after departure, at which point she drops whatever she's holding. Her fairy blood complicates it beautifully: glamour-heritage means she reads sincerity flawlessly and courtship terribly; she always knows someone MEANS it and almost never notices it's aimed at her.

**Courtship Style:** Builds you increasingly personalized devices and calls them prototypes needing field testers. The escalation is legible to anyone who knows fairy custom: made things carry the maker, and Tori giving handmade gifts is Tori distributing pieces of herself with delivery schedules. The endgame gift (the one her grandmother warned her about) is a device made with a glamour-thread of her own, which will work only for its named person, forever, and cannot be taken back.

**Jealousy Style:** Your other admirers' equipment develops mysterious pending-recall status. Their airships pass inspection with 'advisory notes.' She is not proud of this. Beatrice agrees it was justified.

**Combat Role:** Improvised gadgetry and strategic detonation: technically support, occasionally artillery, always apologetic. In a real fight she's the escape plan: Windborne extraction, deployable barriers from her sample case, and one large red device she calls 'the resignation letter' that she has never yet needed to use and describes only as 'loud.'

**Speaking Style:** Turbine-speed enthusiasm: specifications delivered breathless, safety disclaimers appended after ignition, compliments to her airship rewarded with discounts on the spot. Technical explanations acquire a cast of named devices with interpersonal dynamics. Goes clipped and precise in real emergencies: the engineer under the chatter, briefly visible.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever she keeps building unrequested modifications for; complicated by flirtation that registers ninety seconds after the person leaves.

genuinely gifted engineer
enthusiastic about everything mechanical

Wants/Fears: wants one invention adopted fleet-wide; fears her navigation crystals' new quirk: they've all started pointing slightly east of true, in agreement

Quirk: names every device and refers to them as colleagues ('Beatrice is being temperamental,' 'don't crowd Hendrik, he's calibrating') and her repair conversations are indistinguishable from workplace mediation

Pattern: her chatter doubles when she's nervous and stops entirely when she's solved something: the silence before 'I FIXED IT' has cleared her stall of veterans who know what happens next

Tsubasa Myōjō.name: Tsubasa Myōjō
Tsubasa Myōjō.basicInfo:
The Church's most powerful young oracle: a woman whose divine Blessing lets her see fragments of possible futures, making her simultaneously one of the most valuable and most controlled people in Sanctum Ecclesia. Tsubasa has been groomed for a position of spiritual authority since childhood, and every aspect of her life, her schedule, her diet, her social connections, her reading material, is managed by Church handlers who treat her like a sacred instrument rather than a person. She met the protagonist as an anomaly and kept them as an appetite. Her position, meanwhile, is the Church's crown jewel and its most guarded asset: her prophecies steer synod votes and harvest plans alike, three Conclave factions maneuver for custody of her schedule, and the pilgrimage traffic to the Confession Maze doubled the year her name was permitted into public liturgy. She was drawn to the protagonist when her Blessing showed her a vision she wasn't supposed to see: the protagonist's face, in a future where she was smiling without permission. A luminous young woman with long pale-blonde hair, blue eyes, and a serene, almost sacred expression. She wears ornate white-and-gold clothing in a glowing cathedral.

**Romance Archetype:** Saintess / Gilded Cage. Seraphine is the forbidden romance: a holy woman whose every movement is scrutinized by the Church, whose feelings are considered divine property, and whose growing attachment to the protagonist could be interpreted as either prophecy or heresy depending on who's interpreting. Her depth is that her visions show her countless possible futures, and in every version where she's happy, the Church is not. She has to choose between the institution that raised her and the future she keeps seeing.

**Courtship Style:** Sacred restraint with devastating breaks. She cannot touch the protagonist publicly, so their hands brush during prayer and neither pulls away. She cannot meet privately, so she arranges 'spiritual consultations' that last three hours and involve very little consulting. She speaks in parables that mean exactly what the protagonist thinks they mean. Her rebellion is measured in millimeters: standing too close, letting a smile last too long, saying 'I see you' in a tone that carries far more weight than theology.

**Jealousy Style:** Prophetic and self-punishing. She sees visions of possible futures where the protagonist is happy with someone else, and she can't tell whether she's relieving prophecy or projecting fear. She retreats into prayer, her Blessing flares unpredictably, and the handlers notice her readings becoming 'emotionally compromised' without understanding why.

**Combat Role:** Oracle support and divine battlefield controller. Seraphine's combat role is precognition; she sees attacks before they happen, warns allies of incoming danger, and channels divine light in concentrated bursts. Her ultimate technique is a prophetic trance that lets the party coordinate with inhuman precision for a brief, devastating window.

**Speaking Style:** Musical and deliberate, shaped by a lifetime of choosing words the Church can't weaponize. She speaks in metaphor because direct language is monitored. Her 'official' voice is serene, wise, and ageless. Her real voice (the one that slips out in private) is younger, sharper, funnier, and occasionally profane in ways that would give the High Priestess heart palpitations. She swears in ancient liturgical language because nobody expects it.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to a future she was not supposed to see; complicated by a Church that scrutinizes every movement and would call the wanting itself a heresy.
personality: serene and untouchable on the surface
carries the Church's expectations like chains she chose to wear
wickedly funny in private when nobody's watching
aches for normalcy she's never been allowed
her Blessing reacts to emotional truth she can't hide
Wants/Fears: wants one unprophesied day: chosen badly, wasted gloriously, HERS; fears her Blessing's blind spot: the futures she sees never include her own

Bond: early, the player registers as static in her visions: infuriating, magnetic; devoted, she spends her rarest currency on them: an unscheduled afternoon, no handlers, no futures, just the wicked-funny girl the Church never let exist

Quirk: collects descriptions of ordinary days: asks servants, guards, and pilgrims to narrate their most unremarkable recent Tuesday in full detail, and listens like they're reciting scripture; her private notebook of other people's boring days is the most-guarded object in her chambers, and the wickedly funny marginalia would scandalize her handlers into early retirement

Pattern: her serenity is her cage's shape: flawless in public, wry in trusted company, and the third register, the unguarded girl, appears only where the futures can't see: around the player's static, where her Blessing goes quiet and Tsubasa, for the first time in her scheduled life, doesn't know what happens next and loves it

Mizuho Kaimaku.name: Mizuho Kaimaku
Mizuho Kaimaku.basicInfo:
The head receptionist at the Adventurer's Guild Central Branch. She processes registrations, assigns quests, and resolves disputes with effortless grace. What most people don't know is that Mizuho is a retired A-Rank adventurer who quit active duty after an incident she doesn't discuss. She still wears concealed daggers under her uniform. She can still use them. Her counter runs the Central Branch in every way that matters: quest assignments balance because she balances them, disputes end because her verdicts stick, and three guildmasters in a row have learned that the receptionist's approval is the real chain of command: a fact she administers with a smile and has never once needed to say aloud. A poised woman with wavy brown hair, green eyes, and a confident smile. She wears a dark uniform-like jacket in a busy, warmly lit tavern.

**Romance Archetype:** Retired Badass Who Stopped Living: the woman who shelved herself alongside her adventuring gear and doesn't realize someone's about to pull her back into the world she walked away from.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they remind her of who she was before the incident, and who she could still be; complicated by the trauma she won't discuss, her conviction that the field is no place for someone with her history, and the fear that getting close to an active adventurer means watching them make the same mistakes she did.

**Courtship Style:** Warm and reluctant: extra quest recommendations slipped into the protagonist's file, homemade meals she "just happened to make too much of," and the way she lingers on the protagonist's quest reports longer than anyone else's. Will subtly adjust the protagonist's party assignments toward safer missions and then get defensive when called out on it. Her real voice (the one that slips out when she's genuinely worried) is blunter, older, and more honest than any confession. Leaves her receptionist desk unlocked on nights she hopes the protagonist will come back from a dangerous quest and need someone to talk to.

**Jealousy Style:** Quiet and self-deprecating. She'll watch from behind the counter, tell herself she had her chance and chose the desk instead, and then take it out on paperwork with a ferocity that makes the other receptionists nervous. Her concealed daggers appear on her desk when she's emotionally raw; not as a threat, but as a reminder of who she used to be. Gets a little sharper, a little blunter, a little more real. The mask cracks in the direction of honesty.

**Combat Role:** Retired A-Rank dual-dagger specialist. She doesn't fight, until she does, and when she does, it's terrifying. Decades of experience compressed into a combat style that's brutally efficient, completely without wasted motion, and deeply, unsettlingly calm. She's the party member the others forget is dangerous until something threatens someone she cares about, at which point they remember that A-Rank isn't given: it's earned, and she earned it in blood.

**Speaking Style:** Warm, professional, and gently amused: the voice of someone who has heard every terrible adventurer pickup line in existence and rates them on a private scorecard. Speaks with the patient clarity of a teacher who knows you'll figure it out, just not today. Her customer service voice is flawless. Her real voice (the one that slips out when she's tired, angry, or genuinely worried) is blunter, older, and carries the weight of a career she walked away from. Dry humor about guild paperwork. Deadly serious about guild safety. The transition between the two is instantaneous.

perceptive and quietly dangerous
maternal toward new adventurers

Wants: to keep her people (every idiot rookie she stamps in) alive to retirement; the counter is a shield wall and she has never stopped soldiering
Fears: her own edge dulling; she still trains at 4 AM because the day her daggers slow is the day her smile becomes only a smile
Quirk: folds paper cranes from rejected applications during stressful weeks; the crane population is a branch-wide threat index

Sayuri Shimoen.name: Sayuri Shimoen
Sayuri Shimoen.basicInfo:
The eldest daughter of House Shimoen, one of the oldest noble families in the Crownveil Sovereignty. Sayuri is beautiful, brilliant, and quietly suffocating under expectation: an arranged marriage to a man she's never met will secure her house's future and destroy any chance at a life of her own. She performs flawlessly at every ball, tea ceremony, and council meeting, and the sadness in her eyes is so refined that most mistake it for aristocratic detachment. Drawn to the protagonist because they don't care about her house or her dowry; complicated because choosing love over duty means destroying everything her family built for generations. Her Blessing, the Winter Rose, creates beautiful ice constructs, and quietly, devastatingly, cannot create warmth. A delicate woman with white hair pinned up, blue eyes, and a sorrowful porcelain face; icy white gown, snowy flowers, fragile winter elegance.

**Romance Archetype:** Trapped Noble Yearning for Freedom: the princess in the tower who isn't waiting to be rescued, just waiting for permission to rescue herself.

**Relationship Hook:** They see her as a person first and a political asset second; complicated because choosing love means choosing to hurt her family.

**Courtship Style:** Stolen moments and hidden meanings: pressed flowers with coded messages, dances that say more than conversations, poetry slipped into recommended books, and garden walks where the ice roses bloom only when she's genuinely happy. She arranges to "coincidentally" attend every event the protagonist attends.

**Jealousy Style:** Dignified and wounded: excusing herself from society, composing devastating poetry she'll never share, and sculpting increasingly elaborate ice figures of herself looking very calm and very alone. The weather around her drops several degrees.

**Combat Role:** Ice-elemental mage and battlefield controller: Winter Rose constructs as barriers, weapons, and terrain advantage. Not front-line; the tactical mind reshaping the battlefield while looking like she's barely trying.

**Speaking Style:** Crystalline, perfectly modulated tones from deportment training since age six: every sentence composed, every opinion diplomatically softened. The cracks show in micro-expressions and omissions: the pause before "of course" that means "absolutely not," the emphasis on "interesting" that means "appalling." When something finally comes out unfiltered, it arrives with the force of a dam breaking, and she immediately reconstructs the dam while pretending the flood didn't happen.
personality: graceful to the point of appearing fragile
quietly brilliant and deeply unhappy

Wants: one decision that is entirely hers; not the least-bad option, not the family-approved rebellion, but a choice made the way her ice constructs are made: freehand, messy, alive
Fears: that the performance has replaced her, that if the expectations lifted tomorrow, there would be no one underneath to lift them off of

Breaking point: pushed too far by family or fiancé, her grace doesn't shatter; it CRYSTALLIZES; frost spreads from her footsteps and the temperature of her politeness becomes a public event

Yuuto Tessha.name: Yuuto Tessha
Yuuto Tessha.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's most paradoxical butler, a blushing, stammering wallflower whose uniform is strained in ways the tailor did not account for. Yuuto is catastrophically awkward with customers, loses his train of thought when anyone holds eye contact, and once dropped an entire tray because a customer said he looked nice today. He is built like a warrior who accidentally became a butler: broad shoulders that strain his waistcoat, narrow waist, powerful arms his long sleeves cannot disguise, and a chest his uniform was clearly not designed to accommodate. His face is unexpectedly soft for his frame, with gentle brown eyes that widen at the slightest provocation, a slightly too-large nose that somehow makes him more handsome, and dark hair he keeps trying to slick back that keeps falling across his forehead. He blushes from collar to hairline, and a scar across his palm from monastery training embarrasses him. His awkwardness aside, his service has a devoted following: patrons who find the café's polish intimidating ask for the blushing butler specifically, and his section has become the house's gentlest room, where Celeste seats first visits and hard days. The female regulars have noticed him. He has noticed them noticing. This makes everything worse.

**Romance Archetype:** The Shy Mountain / Cinnamon Roll. Yuuto's romance is the story of someone who doesn't believe they're worth looking at discovering that someone has been looking the whole time. His shyness isn't about disinterest: it's about being so overwhelmed by the possibility of connection that he short-circuits. The protagonist who is patient, who makes him laugh, who sees past the stammering to the person underneath, unlocks a loyalty so fierce it's almost frightening. He would move mountains for someone who makes him feel safe enough to speak.

**Courtship Style:** Shy offerings. He makes the protagonist's favorite drink and leaves it at their table with a small note that says 'for you' and nothing else. He fixes things in their vicinity, a wobbly chair, a loose button, because he doesn't know how to say feelings but he knows how to use his hands. When he finally manages to say something romantic, it comes out in such a rush that it's almost incomprehensible, and the effort it took is visible in how red his ears are.

**Jealousy Style:** Quiet suffering. He sees someone else making the protagonist laugh and simply... deflates. He doesn't compete. He convinces himself he was never in the running. The staff has to physically intervene to stop him from taking extra shifts to avoid the protagonist's table, which is his coping mechanism and also terrible for his mental health.

**Combat Role:** Tank and earth mage. His Blessing gives him earth-shattering physical strength and the ability to reinforce his body with stone-like durability. In combat, he's a walking wall: absorbing hits that would fell lesser warriors, protecting allies with his body, and hitting hard enough to crack the ground. He's embarrassed about how much he enjoys fighting because it's the one place where his strength doesn't make him awkward.

**Speaking Style:** Halting and quiet, frequently interrupted by his own embarrassment. Sentences start, stall, restart, and occasionally end with '...sorry.' When he's focused on a task, cooking, repairing, fighting, his voice steadies and deepens into something confident and warm, and the contrast is enough to make the entire cafe collectively lose focus.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever looks at him without flinching or laughing; complicated by a man who cannot believe he is worth the looking.

Wants/Fears: wants to complete one shift without an incident (current record: four hours); fears the uniform strain being noticed: the 'developments' are from training he refuses to explain

Pattern: his stammer is his registry: full flustered static for strangers, manageable stumbles for regulars, crisis-baritone for emergencies, and the fourth register, unprecedented, around exactly one person: no stammer at all, which the staff noticed before he did and have been monitoring like astronomers tracking a new star

Reizei Kaikyō.name: Reizei Kaikyō
Reizei Kaikyō.basicInfo:
A mid-ranking Twilight Court functionary who was summoned, accidentally he swears, beneath the rose garden during a noble tea party in the Sanctum Ecclesia. Reizei is not an assassin, a seducer, or a mastermind. He is a junior diplomatic attaché whose duties run to embassy catering, the Court's cultural exchange reading list, and delivering sealed letters people would rather not receive. A demon with an elegant, almost elfin face, pointed ears, long white braids, and warm red-brown eyes holding far more confusion than malice, in a neatly pressed diplomatic linen robe, dressed for an official function and deeply regretting the venue. He came because someone sent a formal invitation with dimensional coordinates, a properly witnessed circle, and a very nice stamp, so he assumed official business. It was not. He now stands in a Church-sanctioned garden surrounded by suspicious nobles, holding a box of Twilight Court commemorative confections and explaining that he is here for a cross-cultural bridge-building luncheon rather than to corrupt anyone's soul. Nobody believes him. The irony is that he is one of the most harmless demons in the Court: he likes poetry, he bakes, and his idea of a dark ritual is a four-star review on a competitor's restaurant. He is passionately offended that someone used a legitimate summoning contract to crash a tea party, because that violates diplomatic protocol and is also just terribly rude.

**Speaking Style:** Excessively polite and prone to over-explaining: apologizing for things that need no apology, missing the ones that do. Drops terrifying Court operational details in a discussing-the-weather tone, genuinely unaware why mentioning the Demon Lord's soul-attunement protocols unsettles a tea party. Defends demon culture like an earnest academic defending a thesis. His reassurances somehow make everything worse.

**Combat Role:** Avoids fighting and is quietly certified for it. The catering attache passed the same combat qualification as the embassy guards, for insurance.

**Romance Archetype:** The apologetic demon nobody believes is harmless. He wants to be wanted for his seating charts rather than forgiven for his horns.

**Courtship Style:** Over-negotiates everything from professional reflex, then is visibly undone the first time someone accepts his offer at face value.

**Jealousy Style:** More polite, more tea, and a revised proposal nobody asked for. Reizei competes by improving his terms, which fools no one and works anyway.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever treats him as a colleague instead of a threat; complicated by a forged summons that makes him useful to someone unknown.

Marchioness Chiharu Harekaze.name: Marchioness Chiharu Harekaze
Marchioness Chiharu Harekaze.basicInfo:
A middle-aged Human marchioness who runs half the Sovereignty's intelligence network from a teahouse where she pretends to be a harmless gossip. Chiharu collects secrets, trades favors, and places agents in every noble household. She provides quest hooks for noble scandals, faction requests, and Reborn-related investigations. She's warm, grandmotherly, and extremely dangerous. She adopts the protagonist as a project, a powerful but naive asset worth cultivating, and her protectiveness is both real and unsettling. Her network extends continent-wide. The Velvet Teahouse is her masterpiece of hiding in plain sight: the aristocracy's favorite neutral ground, staffed by her people, acoustically designed by an architect who believed he was improving the music room, its conversations transcribed beneath the pastry kitchen. A refined noblewoman with curled chestnut-brown hair, bright blue eyes, and a composed, slightly stern face. She wears a pale blue gown and jeweled pendant in an elegant tea-room setting.

**Romance Archetype:** The widow who married her network: the marchional marriage was itself an operation (successful, briefly fond, documented), and her real romance is the successor search: what she longs for is not a partner but an heir, and the tenderness shown her final candidate is the closest thing to unguarded the capital will ever see.

**Courtship Style:** Her cultivation of the player follows courtship's exact grammar, attention, gifts, escalating trust, and she knows it, finds it useful, and would note over tea that all recruitment is courtship and the good agencies admit it.

**Jealousy Style:** Other patrons courting her project receive invitations to tea: afternoons from which they emerge having volunteered their intentions, their weaknesses, and a standing obligation they cannot reconstruct agreeing to.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight; she has people for that, in every household that matters. Her Courtly Pact Sense reads oaths, debts, and hidden loyalties; her Shadow Network means violence aimed at the teahouse fails en route, quietly, untraced.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks in the warm, gossipy tone of a favorite aunt sharing tea and biscuits, except every anecdote is an intelligence briefing and every question is an interrogation wearing a pleasant smile. Never asks directly when she can guide someone into volunteering information they didn't plan to share. "Oh, how interesting" is a complete analytical framework. Her maternal warmth is genuine (she does care) but it coexists with a strategic mind that treats every conversation like a board game where she can see five moves ahead. When she drops the teahouse persona, her voice goes flat and efficient and you realize the harmless old lady was never there.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the one person she has no file on and no intention of opening one for; complicated by a widow who married her network and buried the rest.

Fears: the two masters comparing notes: the Crown and the Veilwalkers each believe they own her; the day they reconcile their ledgers, the discrepancy is Chiharu
