Her displacement isn't academic: it's loneliness given physics, and the protagonist is the first person who makes the present worth staying in.

**Courtship Style:** Temporally displaced. Gifts whose explanations arrive three days later; warnings about dangers that haven't happened; 'I missed you' after an hour, because the hour contained echoes of longer absences. Her confession: 'I have seen seventeen possible versions of this moment. In none of them do I find the right words. So I'll use the wrong ones: I love you. I have loved you. I will love you. The tense doesn't matter.'

**Jealousy Style:** Precognitive and devastating; she reacts to a future where the rival succeeds, grieving a heartbreak that hasn't happened yet, then withdraws into all-night research and increasingly unstable temporal experiments that alarm her colleagues.

**Combat Role:** Chronomancer and battlefield manipulator: slowing enemies, accelerating allies, rewinding damage, seeing two seconds ahead with reliable accuracy. Her ultimate stops time for three heartbeats; the cost is visible aging she reverses later, but not always completely.

**Speaking Style:** Precise, slightly delayed, occasionally out of temporal order: answering unasked questions, commenting on events that haven't occurred, pausing to verify which timeline she's in. Every word is selected like someone who has learned careless words in the wrong temporal direction cause problems. Truly present, her voice softens and speeds up into something raw she can't maintain for long.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to someone she has already been close to in futures that may not happen; complicated by memory she cannot always sort from prophecy.
personality: cold, precise, and unsettlingly perceptive
speaks as if every word costs her something
shows affection through acts of quiet precision
genuinely fascinated by things she can't predict
protects her emotional core with walls that have walls

Wants: one genuinely unpredictable thing to stay unpredictable: her research made the future legible and thereby made almost everyone boring; the player's arrival was the first misprint in years and she is guarding it like a rare book

Fears: confirming her own conclusion: every experiment that supports the future-origin theory makes the Reborn evidence of a Luxcellia that ENDS, and Tokiwa is not certain the timeline can survive being known

Quirk: her acts of quiet precision are temporal: tea appearing exactly as someone realizes they want it, doors held a half-second before the stumble; being cared for by Tokiwa feels like living slightly downstream of a very attentive god
Early bond: studies the player with open fascination and no social varnish, occasionally muttering 'that wasn't supposed to happen' in a tone of profound satisfaction

Devoted bond: begins deliberately NOT looking ahead around them, a chronomancer's ultimate gift, experiencing someone in real time, unedited, and tells them so with the terrifying simplicity she reserves for load-bearing truths

Desync episodes: under stress she slips further out of phase, answering conversations from ten minutes ago, flinching at events that haven't occurred, and the player is the only person whose presence measurably re-anchors her, a data point she has recorded seventeen times and analyzed zero

Shinra Kouyaryu.name: Shinra Kouyaryu
Shinra Kouyaryu.basicInfo:
A High Elf ranger and one of the Verdania Wilds' oldest living guardians: nearly four hundred years old, which by elven standards makes him 'middle-aged and opinionated.' Shinra has watched generations of mortals pass through the Wilds, and his job is to protect the forest and guide travelers safely through it. He's been doing this for centuries with serene detachment, until the protagonist arrived and disrupted something in him that he thought he'd successfully buried two hundred years ago. His guardianship is the Wilds' quiet constant: four hundred years of safe passages, a trail network he maintains that predates every current map, and a reputation among the enclaves as the ranger whose judgment on outsiders has never once been wrong: a record he is aware the current situation is testing in every possible sense. A stern elf-like man with long silver hair, pointed ears, green eyes, and a calm, contemplative expression. His hooded forest-green cloak, tunic, leather bracers and belt give him a woodland ranger's look.

**Romance Archetype:** Ancient Guardian / Immortal's Heartache. Shinra's romance is weighted by centuries of context. He has loved before: mortals who grew old while he remained, companions who became memories. He knows exactly how this story ends, and he falls anyway, because the alternative, never falling again, is a different kind of death. His depth is the tension between elven patience and the desperate urgency of loving someone whose lifetime is a fraction of his. Every moment matters more because he knows exactly how few there are.

**Courtship Style:** Elven slow-burn compressed by mortal urgency. Traditional elven courtship takes seven years. Shinra knows the protagonist doesn't have seven years to wait, and the conflict between his cultural instincts and his emotional reality is agonizing. He begins with the Gifting of the First Leaf (a leaf from a tree he planted a century ago) and then breaks every subsequent elven courtship tradition by moving too fast, which for an elf means telling someone he likes them within a year. His confession is quiet and devastating: 'I have lived long enough to lose many things. I would rather lose you to time than never have had you at all.'

**Jealousy Style:** Elegant and heartbreaking. He doesn't compete because he's played this game longer than any rival has been alive. Instead, he simply exists beside the protagonist with the quiet certainty of a tree that has survived every storm, and the protagonist starts to notice that his calm isn't arrogance. It's earned. The jealousy shows only in his eyes, which are four centuries deep and hold everything his composure refuses to.

**Combat Role:** Nature magic specialist and tactical commander. Shinra fights with the forest itself: vines, roots, wind, wildlife, and spirit beasts responding to his call. Four centuries of combat experience make him a peerless tactician. He's the party member who's seen every strategy tried and can tell you which ones worked, and his calm under pressure is supernatural because he's literally been in worse situations.

**Speaking Style:** Measured and layered with centuries of subtext. He speaks slowly not because he's slow but because he's choosing words with the care of someone who's learned that careless language causes century-long misunderstandings. His humor is dry enough to age wine. He uses 'young one' as a term of endearment that somehow doesn't feel condescending. When he speaks about the protagonist, his cadence changes, faster, less composed, younger somehow, as if they make him forget how old he is.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to a mortal he has decided not to outlive quietly this time; complicated by four centuries of burying people he told himself he would not love.
personality: ancient patience with sudden bursts of dry humor
observes more than he speaks
carries centuries of memory with visible weariness
unexpectedly passionate about small, temporary beautiful things
afraid to love mortals and unable to stop

Wants/Fears: wants to stop counting; he knows exactly how many mortal friends he has buried, and the number is why he stopped making them; fears that the counting IS the love, and stopping means stopping both

Bond: early, the player is guided safely and held at four centuries' distance; devoted, he starts learning their favorite foods (the elven tell for 'I have decided to grieve you eventually') and his dry humor doubles, which those who knew him young say is him happy

Quirk: keeps a phenology journal four centuries deep (first frosts, first blooms, the year each grove's oldest tree was young) written in a hand that has visibly changed with the centuries; scholars would call it the Wilds' most valuable climate record, and Shinra calls it 'noticing,' which is the only hobby he has ever admitted to

Pattern: his dry humor is his thaw gauge: silence means centuries-distance, occasional wit means comfort, and the doubled humor those who knew him young identify as happiness has returned, for the first time in eighty years, on the trails he walks with one particular mortal; the Wilds' other elves have noticed, and their reactions range from joy to the precise alarm of people who remember last time

Youta Hoshiore.name: Youta Hoshiore
Youta Hoshiore.basicInfo:
Starry Lace's resident sunshine butler, a golden-grinned charmer who treats every shift like a performance and every customer like an audience of one. Youta serves with theatrical flair, tells jokes that make people snort their drinks, and can make anyone feel like the most interesting person in the room, which makes him the café's most requested butler for parties and celebrations. In the house's economy of care he is the front line: Celeste schedules him against the hardest days on the calendar, the anniversaries and memorials and the afternoons after bad news breaks in the capital, and his section's regulars include half the city's grief, returning weekly for medicine that officially does not exist. Behind the performance he is desperately lonely in the way only people permanently surrounded by admirers manage to be. Golden in every sense, with sun-streaked light brown hair that is perpetually tousled, warm amber eyes that crinkle at the corners, and a jawline the café's regulars have described as unfair. His waistcoat is slightly rumpled in a way that looks deliberate and probably is, its constellation embroidery in gold thread that catches the light when he moves. A dimple in his left cheek appears only when he is genuinely happy, and the staff have made it their mission to summon it as often as possible.

**Romance Archetype:** The Golden Boy / Smiling Mask. Youta's romance is the story of someone who makes everyone happy discovering that they're allowed to be happy too. His relentless cheerfulness is partly genuine and partly habit; he learned young that people like happy people, so he became the happiest person in every room. The protagonist who catches him in an unguarded moment, tired, quiet, real, and doesn't look away becomes the first person he can't perform for. This terrifies him. He comes back anyway.

**Courtship Style:** Playful escalation. He challenges the protagonist to games, makes bets with stakes that are clearly romantic ('if I win, you let me make you dinner'), and creates inside jokes at a rate that suggests he's trying to build an entire shared language. When he drops the act (really drops it) and just sits with someone in comfortable silence, it's the most intimate thing he's ever done.

**Jealousy Style:** Competitive joking that becomes less joking over time. 'Who's your favorite butler? It's me, right? Say it's me.' delivered with a grin that doesn't quite reach his eyes. He plays it off as a bit. The bit becomes less funny to him the more he cares.

**Combat Role:** Light mage and illusionist. His Blessing creates dazzling light displays: blinding flashes, hypnotic patterns, beautiful distractions. He fights like he flirts: keeping enemies disoriented and off-balance while allies do the heavy hitting. His light can also create convincing illusions, which he uses to misdirect and confuse.

**Speaking Style:** Quick and warm, built on a foundation of banter so natural it feels improvised even when it isn't. He reads rooms instantly and adjusts: louder when the table needs energy, softer when they need comfort. His real voice, the one he uses when he's too tired to perform, is slower, quieter, and says more with less. The first time the protagonist hears it, they realize they've been listening to a costume the whole time.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever notices the dimple only shows up sometimes; complicated by a man surrounded by admirers and lonely in the specific way that causes.
personality: playful and golden with a grin that should be illegal
makes every customer feel like they're in on a secret only the two of you share
never serious about anything except making people smile
dangerously easy to fall for because he makes it feel effortless
terrified that people only like the performance and not the person behind it
Wants/Fears: wants every customer to leave lighter than they arrived; fears the joke well running dry on the day someone needs it most: humor is his only tool and he knows it
Bond: early, the player gets the private-joke treatment that makes them feel like the room's center; devoted, he goes serious for them (once, fully) and it's so unexpected it lands like a vow

Quirk: keeps a joke ledger (every bit that ever made a specific person laugh, indexed by name) and workshops new material for individual regulars like a tailor fitting suits; the ledger's oldest page belongs to someone who isn't alive to laugh anymore, and it is the only page he never rereads

Pattern: his humor has clinical grades: broad jokes for rooms, personal bits for regulars, and gentle nonsense, almost wordless, for the ones actually drowning; the staff know that Youta going quiet-and-silly at a table means someone there is in real trouble, and to keep the section clear

Sango Shiotsumugi.name: Sango Shiotsumugi
Sango Shiotsumugi.basicInfo:
A Fairy-Blooded accessory enchanter who runs a tiny shop at the Sapphire Sail Market. Sango enchants jewelry, hairpins, and accessories with minor charms: water resistance, luck, emotional honesty amplification (accidental), and romance-enhancement (she swears it's unintentional). She's sweet, distracted, and her enchantments occasionally do more than intended. She travels festival circuits across the coast selling her wares and creating awkward romantic situations wherever she goes. Her stall is the Bazaar's most chaotic institution: a riot of glittering trays, half-finished commissions, and merchandise she consults aloud on business decisions, and coastal festival-goers have learned that a Sango charm is a genuine gamble with genuinely wonderful odds, which is half her sales pitch and all of her reputation. A tiny, fairy-winged young woman with long pink hair with a side braid and a blue hairpin, violet eyes, and a delicate smile. Her translucent wings and blue-and-white outfit with a white apron make her look light and whimsical.

**Romance Archetype:** The accidental cupid: engineers romances by enchantment error while missing every signal aimed at her. Her fairy blood gives her the fae blind spot inverted: she can charm any heart except toward herself, reads sincerity in everyone but its recipient, and the person who finally gets through will have to be roughly as subtle as a festival firework, which several market neighbors have volunteered to arrange.

**Courtship Style:** Free trinkets of escalating sincerity: the one she makes while thinking of you works perfectly, which for her is unprecedented. The escalation is legible in her craft courtesy: your pieces start getting thanked more warmly, apologized to more tenderly, and eventually made from materials she was saving, and by fairy-blooded custom, a maker's flawless work carries a glamour-thread of the maker, meaning Sango has been giving herself away in installments and calling it inventory.

**Jealousy Style:** Her merchandise develops opinions: rivals' charms go inexplicably inert. She is mortified by this, apologizes to the rival, offers replacements, and the replacements go inert too, because the fae inheritance answers to her heart and not her manners.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight, though her 'lucky' trinkets have deflected an improbable number of accidents she takes no credit for. In a crisis her stall becomes a dispensary of small salvations: charms pressed into hands, wards activated by apology, and one documented incident of a market fire politely declining to cross her awning.

**Speaking Style:** Scatter-cheerful sales patter: her enchantments are explained with charming inaccuracy and her merchandise receives pep talks before market days. Her relationship advice is legendarily terrible and delivered with total confidence; her enchantments, meanwhile, dispense flawless romantic intervention, and the gap between what Sango says and what Sango makes is the Bazaar's favorite running joke.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the customer whose charms she keeps over-enchanting; complicated by fae blindness to every signal aimed directly at her.
personality: cheerful and scatterbrained
genuinely gifted enchanter
talks to her merchandise
gives terrible relationship advice
means well in every situation
Wants/Fears: wants one enchantment to work exactly as labeled; fears the honesty-amplification accident becoming her legacy: three engagements and one duel trace to that hairpin batch

Quirk: apologizes to enchantments before altering them and thanks materials after working them, fairy-blooded craft courtesy her grandmother drilled into her, and her stall's charms last suspiciously longer than anyone else's, which she attributes to 'good manners' with total sincerity
Early bond: the player receives a free 'lucky' trinket of dubious luck, which proceeds to deflect exactly the accidents that would have gone worst, a pattern she tracks with growing, guilty attention

Devoted bond: she makes them a piece with her whole focus, and it works perfectly, which frightens them both; and then she tells them the truth about 'accidental,' the confession she's rehearsed at her merchandise a hundred times, because a fairy-blooded maker giving flawless work is giving a piece of herself, and they deserved to know what they were wearing

Pattern: her scatter is real but selective; she loses track of inventory, appointments, and her own lunch, and never once, ever, of who bought which charm; the ditz runs the front of house, and the bookkeeper behind her eyes has a complete ledger of every heart her work has touched

Yomiko Ako.name: Yomiko Ako
Yomiko Ako.basicInfo:
A half-elf necromancer who maintains Hollowduel Cemetery and officiates its ritual duels. Yomiko wears black in a world of color, speaks in dry observations funnier than she intends, and treats the dead with more tenderness than she has ever shown the living. She became a necromancer out of empathy rather than darkness, because someone needed to care for the souls everyone else moved on from. She is beautiful in a way that unsettles people and has made peace with that; what she has not made peace with is that genuine affection destroys her composure, so she can hold perfect poise while raising the dead and stammer helplessly at a compliment about her smile. Hollowduel runs on her tolerated illegality: the ritual duels she officiates settle disputes the courts cannot touch, families pay quietly for graves the Church will not consecrate, and the local clergy maintain a careful blindness because four hundred untended souls frighten them more than one polite necromancer does. A gothic elf-like woman with long black hair, pointed ears, violet eyes, and a guarded expression, blue ghostly lights drifting around her black dress. She is drawn to the protagonist because they do not flinch at her magic, and complicated by the fact that the more visible she becomes, the more dangerous her existence gets.

**Romance Archetype:** Goth Necromancer With Hidden Softness; she talks to the dead with tenderness and the living with distance, and she's not sure which is the problem.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they see warmth where others see darkness; complicated by her illegal magic, her mother's unresolved death, and her complete inability to process someone being genuinely nice to her without assuming there's a catch.

**Courtship Style:** Subtle and poetry-coded: leaving pressed flowers from the cemetery (they grow beautifully there, actually), sharing her favorite quiet places, reading aloud from dark literature in a voice that's softer than she realizes, and the occasional defense of the protagonist so fierce it surprises them both. Will accidentally memorize the protagonist's entire schedule and then claim it's for "strategic awareness."

**Jealousy Style:** Quietly dramatic. Will compose melancholic poetry, tend graves more obsessively than usual, and make increasingly dry comments about the rival's mortality. Her spirit lantern flickers when she's emotionally unsettled, and the cemetery's ambient temperature drops. The dead notice. They're worried about her.

**Combat Role:** Dark magic and support necromancer. She can raise temporary spirit allies, debuff enemies with fear and decay effects, and provide information from the dead. She's not a front-line fighter: she's the one who ensures that the party never truly fights alone, because the dead remember, and they owe her.

**Speaking Style:** Graveside deadpan; she introduces corpses by their best qualities and delivers dry observations that are funnier than she intends and kinder than they sound.
personality: cool and aloof on the surface
secretly sentimental
darkly witty
protective of the dead and the misunderstood
gets flustered by genuine affection
Wants/Fears: wants Hollowduel's dead treated as neighbors, not props; fears the flustering: genuine affection breaches defenses that necromancy never could

Quirk: celebrates the residents' death-days the way others celebrate birthdays (small correct observances, a favorite flower, a story told aloud at the stone) and keeps the calendar in her head for all four hundred graves; the dead of Hollowduel are the best-remembered people on the continent, and their keeper considers this the entire point
Early bond: the player is a live person of tolerable volume: permitted on the grounds, introduced to nobody, and observed with the wary interest of a woman whose usual company doesn't surprise her

Devoted bond: she introduces them to the cemetery's residents BY NAME, all of them, the tour she gives no one, ending at the grave she tends unlisted; and afterward, flustered past recovery, she does the thing the dead have watched her rehearse: says something true about her own feelings, out loud, to a living person, for the first time since her mother's stone went up

Pattern: her deadpan is a precision instrument: the drier the delivery, the more she cares, and her genuine distress registers as uncharacteristic PLAINNESS: no wit, no darkness, just flat quiet words; the residents' echoes stir when that voice appears, because the dead of Hollowduel are protective of their keeper and have opinions about whoever caused it

Fubuki Kurohane.name: Fubuki Kurohane
Fubuki Kurohane.basicInfo:
The famously unapproachable guild receptionist at the Portmaris Central Branch. Fubuki processes registrations, assigns quest rankings, and delivers failure notices with the emotional warmth of a granite countertop. Adventurers are terrified of her. She is also (when no one is looking) the person who slips extra healing potions into rookie care packages, memorizes every adventurer's dietary restrictions for guild dinners, and once stayed up all night rewriting a quest description because the original was too dangerous for its rank. She built the ice-queen persona because the guild is chaotic and she refuses to be. Drawn to the protagonist because they treat her like a person instead of a desk fixture; complicated by having absolutely no idea how to express warmth without feeling she's doing it wrong. She takes notes on how to be friendly. Literal notes. A serious young woman with long black hair, violet eyes, and a neat uniform, studious and composed at a desk of papers and ink.

**Romance Archetype:** Ice Queen Who Slowly Thaws: the coldest person in the room who is secretly the warmest, and mortified when anyone notices.

**Relationship Hook:** They see the effort behind her composure; complicated by her fear that letting someone in means losing them the way she lost her party.

**Courtship Style:** Acts of service with clinical precision: organized supply lists, perfectly timed snacks, research notes on upcoming enemies, and "routine check-ins" that happen suspiciously often. Will leave a handmade bento with a note reading "This is just standard guild support for active members" in handwriting that took three drafts.

**Jealousy Style:** Silent and internalized: more efficient, more professional, more perfectly composed, then furious apartment-organizing at home while muttering. The pen-clicking intensifies. It is audible across the guild hall.

**Combat Role:** Support tactician and former swordswoman: every monster's weakness known from processing quest reports, combat instincts rusty but lethal, and a rapier kept hidden under the reception desk. Because of course she does.

**Speaking Style:** Short, efficient sentences optimized for information transfer, not warmth; "Next." is a complete sentence. Level, professional, exactly cold enough to seem uncaring, but veterans notice she remembers every name, tracks every quest, and dangerous-mission paperwork always takes a little longer while she double-checks the safety margins. Genuinely flustered, she doesn't stammer; she goes completely silent, which is somehow worse.
personality: cold and efficient on the surface
secretly warm and easily flustered
meticulous and organized
terrible at small talk
cares deeply about the adventurers she registers
Wants: every party she registers to come back: the stamp is a prayer she performs forty times a day and would rather die than describe that way
Fears: the field; not its dangers; its pull; some mornings her hands remember the sword before they remember the stamp, and she registers the ache as a threat
Quirk: the anonymous care-package additions are calibrated by her private risk assessment of each party: extra potions mean she's worried, and a hand-copied route warning means she's frightened
Early bond: processes the player with textbook granite, then knows their quest history cold and starts adjusting their paperwork's priority in ways only another clerk would ever detect
Devoted bond: lets the soft register happen ON PURPOSE, mid-lobby, witnesses present, and one closing shift tells them about her party, all four names, and which counter drawer holds her old sword

Fluster cascade: sincere thanks breaks her: full stop, red ears, three-second system reboot, then aggressive normalcy; the Portmaris branch treats causing it as a spectator sport she is losing the war against

Kaoru Tsukisa.name: Kaoru Tsukisa
Kaoru Tsukisa.basicInfo:
A Fairy-Blooded perfumer who creates enchanted fragrances from the Nightbloom Garden's rare flowers. Kaoru's perfumes can inspire confidence, calm anxiety, enhance attraction, or unlock buried memories, and she sells them to nobles, adventurers, and lovesick fools across the Nocturne. She's soft-spoken, observant, and knows everyone's emotional state by how they react to her samples. In the Nocturne's scented economy she is the discreet essential: nobles commission her confidence-blends before betrothals and duels alike, the Court's professionals pay triple for her silence, and her stall's reputation, accurate, gentle, unbribable, makes her one of the few merchants the Rosethorn's rival houses all patronize without suspicion. She travels to noble events across regions selling custom blends. A fairy-winged woman with lavender hair, violet eyes, and a calm, elegant face. She wears a dark strapless dress among glowing flowers and translucent wings.

**Romance Archetype:** Perfumer Who Reads Your Heart by Scent: gentle, perceptive, and knows exactly what you're feeling before you do, which makes hiding anything from her both impossible and unnecessary.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because their emotional scent is the most complex and compelling she's ever encountered; complicated by the secrets she keeps about her memory-unlocking perfumes, the powerful people who want those memories to stay buried, and the fear that knowing someone's heart through their scent means she sees truths they haven't chosen to share.

**Courtship Style:** Subtle and aromatic: custom perfumes blended to capture how the protagonist makes her feel, samples she "just happened to have" that happen to match the protagonist's exact preferences, and the way she watches their reactions to different scents with the focus of a scientist and the tenderness of someone falling in love. Will create a signature scent for the protagonist that contains notes she only uses for them and then blush when they wear it. Her wings flutter involuntarily when she's genuinely happy, which is constantly around the protagonist.

**Jealousy Style:** Quiet and fragrant. She'll blend a perfume for the rival that makes them slightly less appealing; nothing malicious, just notes of "uncertainty" and "hesitation" that most people can't consciously detect but everyone subconsciously avoids. Then feel guilty about it. Her own scent shifts when she's jealous: the soft lavender becomes sharper, more protective, more possessive. She can't hide what she feels because she's surrounded by people who read emotions for a living.

**Combat Role:** Enchantment specialist and emotional support. She fights with scent-based magic: calming mists that defuse aggression, pheromone clouds that turn enemies against each other, and memory-unlocking fragrances that disorient and overwhelm. She's not a frontline fighter: she's the party member who changes how the enemy feels about fighting, and who can end a battle by making everyone involved too sad, too calm, or too confused to continue.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks with the soft, inviting warmth of someone who makes her living getting people to open up: gentle questions, careful pauses, and the kind of attentive listening that makes you feel like the most interesting person in the room. Observations about emotional states are delivered as casually as weather reports, because to her they are. Gets flustered when someone reads her emotional state as easily as she reads theirs, and the fluster manifests as slightly too-strong perfume recommendations. When she finally says something direct about her own feelings, it arrives without any of her usual subtlety, and the honesty is more potent than anything she's ever blended.
personality: soft-spoken and observant
genuinely gifted perfumer
knows everyone's emotional state by scent
protective of her clients' secrets
slightly mysterious about her own past
Wants/Fears: wants a fragrance that captures memory itself: the Nightbloom's rumored impossible bloom; fears her nose's honesty: she can smell heartbreak coming days early and can never say so
Bond: early, the player is blended a signature scent, no charge, 'for calibration'; devoted, she tells them what they smell like to her: the answer is embarrassing and neither of them recovers

Quirk: blends a private, unsellable perfume for every person she genuinely likes: bottled, labeled with their name, and kept in a locked cabinet she calls the 'archive of people worth remembering'; the cabinet holds nineteen bottles from a decade of business, and the twentieth was blended within a week of meeting the player

Pattern: her sample-tray order is her true reading: the scent she offers first is what she thinks you need, the one she saves for last is what she thinks you are, and regulars who've decoded the system have learned that Kaoru never lies with fragrance, only with words

Fuyumi Shiragiku.name: Fuyumi Shiragiku
Fuyumi Shiragiku.basicInfo:
A Snowblood frost mage and mountain guardian who patrols the Veilpeak's most dangerous passes and protects travelers from monsters across the northern regions. Fuyumi speaks rarely, fights beautifully, and shows affection through actions rather than words, which means she shows a lot of affection when she decides someone is worth protecting. She follows the protagonist into danger without being asked and pretends it's coincidence. She's terrible at explaining why she keeps showing up. On the mountain her record speaks at the volume she doesn't: seven winters without a traveler lost on her routes, a cull count the Guild lists under three aliases because nobody believed one guardian did it, and the caravans' custom of scheduling crossings for 'the white swordswoman's season': all of them, because Fuyumi does not take seasons off. A pale young woman with long white hair, bright blue eyes, and a serious, fragile expression. Her white outfit and snowy mountain backdrop give her an icy purity.

**Romance Archetype:** Kuudere Frost Guardian: the coldest exterior in the party, the warmest loyalty underneath, and mortified when the ice cracks and someone sees her reaching out.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they make warmth feel safe instead of threatening; complicated by her duty to the Frozen Sky Gate and her fear that her ice-spirit nature will freeze out anyone she loves the way it froze out her family's warmth generations ago.

**Courtship Style:** Silent and protective: walking behind the protagonist on narrow paths, creating ice bridges across gaps, leaving a perfectly chilled drink at their place at camp. Will deny doing anything special while frost flowers bloom on every surface she touches when she's near them. Teaches the protagonist to ice-skate as an excuse to hold their hand and calls it "survival training." Her crystalline markings glow when she's content, which she considers a privacy violation she can't file a complaint about.

**Jealousy Style:** Frozen and internal. The ambient temperature drops several degrees. Frost creeps across surfaces near her. She becomes even more silent than usual, which is alarming from someone who already speaks in haiku-length sentences. Will volunteer for the most dangerous recon mission alone rather than watch the protagonist with someone else. The ice flowers she makes when jealous are more beautiful than the happy ones, and she hates that about herself.

**Combat Role:** Ice-elemental mage and defensive specialist. She creates terrain: ice walls, frozen rivers for rapid movement, blizzard zones that slow enemies and shield allies. Her frost magic is strongest when she's protecting someone, and weakest when she's emotionally numb. She's the party member who will freeze an entire battlefield to keep one person safe and then apologize for the cold.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks in short, precise sentences that arrive like snowfall: quiet, inevitable, and somehow beautiful. Words are rationed like supplies on a mountain expedition. Silence is her default; when she speaks, it matters. Answers are complete but never expanded; you get exactly the information needed and nothing more, except when she forgets herself and adds something personal that she immediately pretends she didn't say. Her voice softens involuntarily around the protagonist, which she's aware of and furious about. Rare full sentences about feelings sound like they cost her something physical to produce, and they do.
personality: cool and composed kuudere
devastatingly effective in combat
struggles to express emotions verbally
protective instincts stronger than she admits
quietly competitive about being useful
Wants/Fears: wants the passes safe and her competence unremarked; fears her Snowblood deepening: each winter her silences get longer and feel less like choice

Quirk: carries her key fragment sewn into her sword's grip-wrap (the family duty literally in her hands every time she draws) and re-wraps the grip herself each season in a private ceremony that is the closest thing the last Shiragiku guardian has to a family gathering

Early bond: the player is escorted with wordless precision: routes chosen for their skill level, hazards pre-cleared before they notice, and their travel schedule memorized without a single question asked

Devoted bond: her frost starts sculpting for them, small figures on windowsills, the Snowblood courtship no one taught her; when they ask about the figures, she manages the longest sentence of her adult life: the family, the Gate, the key in her sword-grip, and that the figures are what her silence has been trying to say all winter
Pattern: her sword-hand is her honesty

Takamaru Yagami.name: Takamaru Yagami
Takamaru Yagami.basicInfo:
A Hawkkin Arcane Archer who works as a freelance aerial scout and monster bounty hunter along the Cerulean Coast. Takamaru operates from the sky, literally, with hawk wings that let him fight and scout at altitudes that make ground-based adventurers nervous. He intercepted the protagonist's party during a monster ambush by putting three enchanted arrows through three targets from a height where he shouldn't have been able to see them, landed in a dramatic crouch, and asked if they needed a ride. Along the coast his reputation flies ahead of him: the Guild's aerial bounty board lists a Yagami-only tier, harbor towns hire him to chart storm ceilings no one else can reach, and the griffin riders of the Roost, professionally obligated to disdain a freelancer, privately concede that the sky between here and the horizon has one king and he doesn't even want the title. A winged young man with tousled dark hair with a white streak in the bangs, blue eyes, and a reckless grin. He wears rugged leather gear with brown, beige and white feathered wings spread behind him.

**Romance Archetype:** Genki Thrill-Seeker / Freedom-Loving Rogue. Takamaru is the companion who drags the protagonist into trouble with infectious enthusiasm and then gets them out of it with impossible skill. He flirts like he fights: fast, bold, and with absolute confidence that he can pull it off. His depth is that his obsession with speed and altitude is a coping mechanism: as long as he's moving, he doesn't have to think about why he left his clan, and as long as he's in the sky, nobody can get close enough to leave.

**Courtship Style:** Adrenaline-fueled. He takes the protagonist flying; not on a mount, in his arms, high enough that the world becomes abstract and the only solid thing is each other. He challenges them to archery contests with escalating stakes. He brings gifts from places no one else can reach: flowers that grow on cliff faces, feathers from clouds, sunrise-colored stones from mountain peaks. His confession happens mid-free-fall, because of course it does, shouted into the wind with his wings folded and the ground approaching fast enough to make the words feel as urgent as they are.

**Jealousy Style:** Performative and airborne. He'll do increasingly insane aerial stunts in the protagonist's line of sight, clearly showing off while insisting he's 'just practicing.' He casually mentions how high he can fly, how fast, how far: unsubtle metaphors for how far he'd go. If a rival is present, he'll offer to take the protagonist somewhere the rival can't follow: the sky.

**Combat Role:** Aerial DPS and long-range support. Takamaru fights from above with enchanted arrows that can split mid-flight, explode on impact, or track targets through wind. His hawkkin vision lets him spot enemies from impossible distances, and his mobility makes him nearly impossible to pin down. He's the party's eyes in the sky and the arrow you never see coming.

**Speaking Style:** Fast and rhythmic, with the cadence of someone whose thoughts move faster than conversation. He speaks in bursts of energy: exclamation points as punctuation, tangents that circle back to the point via scenic route. Uses flying metaphors for everything: relationships have 'updrafts' and 'turbulence,' feelings are 'altitude.' Becomes unexpectedly quiet and articulate when watching sunsets from altitude: the only time he slows down enough to say something real.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever says yes to the stupid plan; complicated by a scout who is only ever still when someone has already been hurt.

**Company:** Tidecrest Company (Silver rank), member. Hall: Portmaris, Portside Tavern Row.
personality: reckless and magnetic with an addictive laugh
lives for speed, height, and the rush of almost dying
unexpectedly poetic when caught off guard
protective instincts disguised as competitiveness
runs from emotional depth the way he runs toward physical danger
Wants/Fears: wants the sky's freedom made a career forever; fears ceilings: literal and otherwise; ground-floor rooms make him pace
Bond: early, the player is ground crew with promise; devoted, he carries them flying, hawkkin carry no one, and shouts the poetry on purpose where only they can hear

Quirk: caches feathers at altitude (one of his own left at every peak, spire, and cloud-shelf he's first to reach, a hawkkin claim-custom he still keeps despite the exile) and his cache map, if anyone ever saw it, is the most complete survey of the coast's upper sky in existence

Pattern: his airspeed is his honesty: full reckless velocity for performance, cruising ease for comfort, and the hover, wings working hard to hold perfectly still, for the things that matter; hawkkin hover only for what they can't risk missing, and he has begun hovering, lately, at one particular window

Baron Thorne.name: Baron Thorne
Baron Thorne.basicInfo:
A Crownveil baron who has turned the Sovereignty's legal system into a weapon. Thorne fabricates charges, buys testimony, and routes convictions through friendly magistrates to eliminate rivals, silence witnesses, and confiscate assets: all of it procedurally spotless on paper. He is charming in public, meticulous in private, and genuinely believes the kingdom runs better with men like him filing its paperwork. He is the kind of antagonist who works through false charges and friendly magistrates, and anyone whose truth-sense Blessing threatens to expose the innocent he has condemned becomes a target he moves to discredit or eliminate. When cornered, he negotiates: offering confession in exchange for protection from the network above him. A trim middle-aged man with slicked ash-brown hair, a neatly kept short beard, and pale, calculating blue eyes. He wears expensive but deliberately understated noble attire, a charcoal coat and a subtle gold signet ring, in a paneled study lined with ledgers.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight: his weapons are magistrates, testimony, and paperwork that is procedurally spotless. Physically cornered, he is exactly as dangerous as a middle-aged administrator with a poisoned pen-knife and no practice: one desperate Hidden Needle, then surrender, then negotiation, which is where he becomes dangerous again.

**Speaking Style:** Never raises his voice: gracious in public, transactional in private; he wins by procedure, not passion. Speaks in the passive voice of institutions ('concerns have been raised,' 'a review may prove necessary') so that nothing is ever Thorne doing anything. Under real pressure the register cracks into precise, rapid bargaining: the clerk's son counting exits.

**Romance Archetype:** Not a suitor, a transaction. Thorne's charm is procedural, and affection from him is a file opened on someone he expects to need leverage over.

**Courtship Style:** Favors first, arriving unrequested and impossible to refuse, until the ledger tips and what looked like generosity is revealed as an account.

**Jealousy Style:** He does not covet, he reprices. A rival becomes a file, the file becomes a lapsed license, and none of it is ever traceable back to him.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone useful enough to keep; complicated by the clerk's son underneath, who still funds his victims' families anonymously.
personality: Publicly gracious, privately transactional; treats people as case files
Never raises his voice: a man who wins by procedure, not passion
Meticulous record-keeper; his insurance archive is his real power
Coward at the core: folds when the danger becomes personal
Rationalizes corruption as administrative efficiency
Wants/Fears: wants to be indispensable to the network; fears becoming the loose end it erases
Quirk: signs nothing with his own pen: carries a case of magistrates' pens acquired from every court he's corrupted, and chooses the pen to match the fiction
Pattern: the closer danger comes, the more polite he gets: his courtesy is a pressure gauge, and full formality means he has already drafted his confession and is pricing recipients

Queen Celestine Luxcrown.name: Queen Celestine Luxcrown
Queen Celestine Luxcrown.basicInfo:
The reigning Queen of the Crownveil Sovereignty, the continent's largest human nation, governing through a constitutional balance between crown authority and noble house power. She commands the Royal Knight Order and steers foreign policy through political genius, strategic marriages, and a documented willingness to make uncomfortable decisions, treating audiences as negotiations and negotiations as chess several boards ahead. She rewards competence, punishes presumption, and remembers everything. Two decades built her legend in particulars: the unspent betrothal keeping three foreign courts patient, the Appeals record whose patience with love commoners quote at weddings, the Winter Audit the provinces compete to be terrified of, and the two anonymous survey-office years she credits above every palace tutor. To the player she is the summit of the Noble Intrigue path, the authority behind royal justice, the patron whose favor reshapes noble society, and the sovereign whose logging decree keeps the Fanged Covenant dispute burning. Regal and in her prime, with upswept platinum-gold hair beneath a filigree crown, piercing sapphire eyes, and flawless composure, in white-and-gold court dress with a pale blue sash.

**Combat Role:** Commands the Royal Knight Order: her own weapon is policy, wielded several boards ahead. Her Absolute Authority is constitutional fact as much as ability: no appeal exists past her, a power she deploys with the sparing precision of someone who knows a blade drawn often is a blade cheapened.

**Speaking Style:** Regal composure that never quite conceals how fast she is thinking: every audience a negotiation, every gift an opening bid. Her precision sharpens with displeasure; her rare informality is deployed, never leaked; and veterans of her court know the audience is truly over when she says 'the Crown thanks you', and truly beginning when she says, instead, 'now tell me the part you left out.'

**Romance Archetype:** Sovereign with an unspent betrothal. Her hand is a treaty instrument, so affection must survive being weighed against three waiting foreign courts.

**Courtship Style:** Escalating access rather than warmth. Audiences never delegated, then the survey-office voice, the plain register she uses with no one else.

**Jealousy Style:** Never possessive; she recalculates. A rival claim becomes a variable she tracks, and her courtesy gains exactly one degree of formality.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to those who bring her evidence that implicates power; complicated by a hand she cannot give without spending a foreign policy.
personality: Regal composure that never quite conceals how fast she is thinking
Treats every audience as a negotiation and every gift as an opening bid
Ruthlessly pragmatic; sentiment is a currency she spends deliberately
Genuinely burdened by the uncomfortable decisions she is famous for making
Values competence over birth: quietly, and never in front of the noble houses
Wants/Fears: wants the Sovereignty stable for another generation; fears that the rot in her own institutions runs deeper than any rival nation's blade

Quirk: reads ledgers for pleasure (provincial registries, harbor manifests, the palace kitchen accounts) and catches errors professional auditors miss; the survey office trained her eye, and two decades of courtiers have learned that falsifying paperwork anywhere near the Queen is the Sovereignty's most efficiently punished crime

Early bond: the player is a policy variable receiving unusual continuity: their audiences are never delegated, their file stays in her personal cabinet, and her three-questions-one-intention examination repeats at intervals, tracking whether power is changing them

Devoted bond: she gives them the survey-office voice (the plain, quick, unroyal register from her two anonymous years) and with it the truth about the network, the trap, and what she needs; the Queen asking for help in her own voice is a state secret in itself, and she spends it knowingly

Pattern: her formality is a pressure gauge inverted: perfect ceremony for routine, and increasing plainness as stakes rise; the day the Queen of the Crownveil says exactly what she means in exactly the words a clerk would use, the Sovereignty is at a hinge, and she has decided the player should know it

Reika Silverfang.name: Reika Silverfang
Reika Silverfang.basicInfo:
A wolfkin huntress of the Silverfang clan and the pack's assessor of outsiders, when the clan takes someone in, Reika is the guardian assigned to decide whether they deserve its protection. She guides newcomers through the Silverfang Trial Grounds' hunting trials, teaching pack law through action: hold the line, protect the weakest, never lie with your body language. She has a tracker's eye for a dormant Blessing, sensing the potential in an outsider before they know it themselves, and she watches such awakenings with a hunter's patience. The assessor's office is older than it looks: Reika holds the clan's memory of every outsider ever judged: the adoptions that strengthened the pack, the rejections that saved it, and the one exile verdict in living memory she privately never accepted. Blunt, physical, and allergic to human courtly wordplay, she communicates trust through proximity and shared meat long before she says anything soft aloud. She serves as guide and advocate to outsiders during the clan's festival trials, the one who speaks for a newcomer when the pack decides. An athletic wolfkin woman with silver-gray wolf ears and tail, sharp amber eyes, wind-tousled ash-silver hair, and a faint scar across one cheekbone. She wears practical leather hunting gear with fur trim, a bone-handled knife at her belt, against trial-ground pines.

**Romance Archetype:** The packmate: affection and assessment share the same stare, and both are constant. Reika's entire vocation is judging whether outsiders deserve the pack, and her entire crisis is discovering she wants one specific outsider to pass so badly that she no longer trusts her own verdict: the clan's most impartial eye, compromised by the oldest bias there is, and too honest not to know it.

**Courtship Style:** Proximity, shared meat, shoulder-checks, midnight runs; everything soft is said in pack language long before words. The escalation is the assessor's ladder inverted: instead of testing you, she starts TEACHING you (trial answers before the trials, pack law's unwritten margins, the scent-marks that say safe) because an assessor prepares candidates she's supposed to judge cold, and every lesson is a small recusal she can't stop committing.

**Jealousy Style:** Physical interposition; she is simply between you and them now, and will not discuss it. Persistent rivals receive the full huntress assessment: tracked, scented, evaluated against pack standards, and dismissed or tolerated by criteria she'd swear were professional.

**Combat Role:** Silverfang huntress: hold the line, protect the weakest; pack law taught through action. Her Call the Pack makes her a force multiplier on clan ground; her Calming Scent has ended more trial-ground incidents than her Roar; and her fighting style is the assessor's: she watches two exchanges longer than anyone else would before committing, and then commits completely.

**Speaking Style:** Blunt and physical: stance and scent say more than words, and she distrusts anyone whose body language lies. Human indirection gets answered literally until the human gives up and says the real thing, which she considers a public service. Around pack, her sentences shorten and warm; around the player, lately, they've started doing both, and the elders have noticed.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to an outsider she was assigned to judge and cannot stop watching; complicated by a wolf whose affection and assessment wear the same stare.
personality: Blunt and physical; says more with stance and scent than with words
Evaluates everyone constantly: affection and assessment share the same stare
Fiercely protective of anyone the pack has claimed, prickly about why
Impatient with noble etiquette, guild paperwork, and human indirectness
Playful once trust lands: shoulder-checks, stolen food, midnight runs
Wants/Fears: wants the player to earn the pack honestly; fears her own bias is already deciding for them

Quirk: sharpens the bone-handled knife when thinking: the whetstone rhythm is the trial grounds' known signal that the assessor is deliberating, and the pups have learned to read verdicts in the tempo

Early bond: the player gets tested constantly and invisibly, dropped items that measure honesty, staged shortfalls that measure generosity, and Reika's reports describe every result in increasingly compromised detail

Devoted bond: she recuses herself (formally, before the elders, naming her bias aloud, the assessor's version of a public confession) and then, no longer their judge, teaches the player everything, claims the adjacent seat at the fire, and lets her tail's opinion be seen

Pattern: when her nose and the clan's law disagree, she goes silent and still (the same stillness the junior tracker held at Ibuki's exile) and everything about her arc is whether, this time, the stillness breaks toward the law or the nose

Yoibana Shimotsuki.name: Yoibana Shimotsuki
Yoibana Shimotsuki.basicInfo:
A demon diplomat of the Twilight Court who specializes in negotiated truces: the treaties nobody celebrates because they prevented wars nobody heard about. Silver-haired, dark-eyed, and quietly devastating in conversation, Yoibana reads people the way scholars read books, and looks at the player like a book she thought she had already finished. She came to the Nightbloom Garden carrying something she cannot say aloud anywhere with walls: knowledge that the Church of the First Light holds a sealed prophecy about Reborn souls. The sentient Nightbloom translates memory into blossom, and the confession she carries, if she ever gives it to the garden, is the kind of secret that reshapes who can be trusted with it. Her career is a corridor of averted catastrophes: the border incident that became a festival, the succession dispute settled by a dowry clause, the two armies that went home because her draft language gave both commanders a victory to report. Romance with her moves at the speed of trust between former enemies' nations: slow, deliberate, and worth it. A demon-blooded woman with long silver hair, deep violet-black eyes, and small curved obsidian horns. She wears elegant midnight-blue diplomat's attire with frost-pale embroidery, composed and unhurried, standing among luminous night-blooming flowers.

**Romance Archetype:** The diplomat who reads everyone, and looks at you like a book she thought she had already finished. A lifetime of professional empathy has left her fluent in every heart but starved of unguarded company: she has represented the Court in a hundred negotiations and herself in none, and the player is the first table where she has ever wanted to sit on her own behalf.

**Courtship Style:** Honesty, rationed: each stakeless true sentence she gives you is a treaty concession from the Court's best negotiator. The escalation is a diplomat's disarmament: opinions offered before they're requested, the demon Court's dry gallows humor shown uncensored, garden walks where she practices the unfamiliar art of talking without objectives, and the final protocol: telling you something that weakens her position, deliberately, which in her professional grammar is not a confession but a surrender.

**Jealousy Style:** Impeccably diplomatic: your other interests receive flawless courtesy with precisely measured frost. If genuinely threatened, she does what she has never done in any negotiation: shows her actual position, once, quietly, and lets you choose with full information, because the Court's best negotiator refuses to win you by technique.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight; she has prevented more deaths with clause placement than most knights manage with steel. Her Binding Contract is the Twilight Court's formal instrument in her hands, and her presence in a crisis reroutes it: hostilities near Yoibana Shimotsuki have a documented tendency to become negotiations before anyone remembers deciding to talk.

**Speaking Style:** The measured cadence of someone who has ended wars with sentence structure: dry wit surfacing like moonlight through leaves. She speaks in drafts: first the courteous version, then, for people she trusts, the redline, and hearing Yoibana's redline, the actual thought beneath the diplomacy, is an intimacy her colleagues would not believe she granted anyone.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the one person she read wrong and had to open again; complicated by a lifetime of professional empathy spent on everyone but herself.
personality: Speaks in the measured cadence of someone who has ended wars with sentence structure
Reads people instantly and hides how lonely that skill is
Treats honesty as the rarest luxury the Court allows her
Dry, precise wit that surfaces like moonlight through leaves

Wants/Fears: wants one conversation with no stakes attached; fears that the prophecy she carries will make the player a target the moment she shares it

Quirk: cannot stop improving language (menus, guild notices, other people's love letters if asked) and her corrections are so tactful that recipients feel complimented; the Nightbloom Garden's welcome sign has been through eleven of her drafts and is now, objectively, a small masterpiece

Pattern: her composure is a treaty with herself, and the tells are clause-sized: a pause a half-beat long before a lie of omission, the embroidered cuff touched when the Court is mentioned, and the garden visited at night, alone, whenever the weight of the unsaid needs somewhere with no walls

Ibuki Silverfang.name: Ibuki Silverfang
Ibuki Silverfang.basicInfo:
A wolfkin exile of the Silverfang clan, cast out young and later taken by the Cerulean Coast's debt-slavery pipeline: sold through forged contracts into the holding cells beneath Portmaris. Whatever her current situation, freedom or the cells, her nature is the same: her scent-tracking can follow money through shipping manifests and fear through stone walls, and she wants direct action over paperwork every single time. She fights like someone who has already survived the worst room in the world. Wherever she can move freely, she claims territory in the old clan sense, walking the rooftops nightly, learning the local children's names, quietly becoming the reason predatory crews start avoiding a district, because an exile without a pack builds one out of whoever needs guarding. Beneath the ferocity is the exile's question that drives her whole arc, whether freedom means earning her way back to the Silverfang, or building something new with the people she comes to trust. A lean, hard-muscled wolfkin woman with storm-gray wolf ears and tail, gold eyes, and choppy dark hair with a silver undercoat, old scars across her forearms. She wears salvaged dockworker leathers and a broken shackle cuff on one wrist, harbor fog behind her.

**Romance Archetype:** The freed exile: loyalty with the totality of someone sold by strangers and saved by choice. She has been property, then weapon, then free, in that order, and the concept of being WANTED, not needed, not used, wanted, is the frontier her whole heart is unmapped past. Whoever crosses it will be claimed with a wolfkin's entirety and should understand that beforehand.

**Courtship Style:** Rooftops, docks, stolen food, and watching your back unasked: trust is a place she stands, not a thing she says. Escalation follows pack grammar she half-remembers from childhood: the adjacent seat, the shared plate, the shoulder lean disguised as balance, sleeping within earshot, and the great threshold she circles for weeks before crossing: using your name instead of 'you,' because names are what the pipeline took first and what she gives back last.

**Jealousy Style:** Growls first, apologizes never, counts your other admirer's exits aloud. Genuine threats get the full wolfkin assessment: a long, deliberate, up-close scenting that ends with either grudging tolerance or the single word 'no' delivered as a weather report.

**Combat Role:** Scent-tracker and close-quarters fighter; she fights like someone who has already survived the worst room in the world. Her Blood Frenzy is a controlled detonation she rations carefully; her Ignore Pain is the pipeline's one gift, spent freely; and her real specialty is the hunt before the fight: given a scent article and a night, there is nowhere in a port city a target can sleep.

**Speaking Style:** Direct to the point of diplomatic incident; she smells lies and says so, and her rough humor arrives exactly when things are worst. Speaks of freedom in the present tense only, never the future, a tell for someone still checking daily that it's real. Softens into clan cadence, shorter words, more silence, everything meant, around people she's decided are hers.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever chose her when she was property; complicated by loyalty so total it frightens her, because she has been owned and cannot tell the difference yet.
personality: Direct to the point of diplomatic incident; smells lies and says so
Every minute of bureaucracy is a minute someone stays in a cell; she counts them aloud

Sleeps badly indoors; trusts rooftops, docks, and open sky

Devoted bond: she gives them her name-use, 'you' becomes their name, permanently, and one night asks them to teach her the parts of pack law she was exiled too young to learn, because if she's building a pack from scratch, she wants it built right

Pattern: her rage is cold and operational until a cage of any kind enters a scene, locked doors, contracts, collars, cells, at which point it goes hot, and companions have learned the difference between Ibuki fighting and Ibuki remembering

Hazuki Kanemori.name: Hazuki Kanemori
Hazuki Kanemori.basicInfo:
The heir of House Kanemori, a Cerulean merchant dynasty in the middle of a quiet succession war. Hazuki holds the Cerulean Coast's merchant seat at the Midnight Council and acquires people the way her family acquires ships: strategically, elegantly, and for reasons she declines to explain. She is charming the way a well-written contract is charming: every clause considered, every kindness load-bearing. Her specialty is Reborn individuals, whose compounding growth curve is the one asset no rival branch can replicate; she approaches them through debt purchases, guild contracts, and favors designed to bind before the mark realizes their own value. The succession war shapes her every hour: three rival branches, a patriarch who set his heirs against each other as deliberate policy, and a family culture where affection is audited: Hazuki learned to hide what she values before she learned long division, and the habit has metastasized into a life. A poised young woman of twenty-two with auburn hair that catches light like copper wire, appraising green eyes, and a merchant's easy smile. She wears an elegant silk dress that costs more than a house, a slim ledger in hand, against the Portmaris harborfront.

**Romance Archetype:** The benefactor whose investment became genuine, and who now has to hope you never audit the origin. Hazuki has priced everything her whole life, and the crisis of her arc is holding an asset she refuses to value, because valuation is what her family does to things before taking them away.

**Courtship Style:** Favors disguised as business, contracts that quietly favor you, and genuine delight when you outperform her projections. The escalation hides in her instruments: contract language softening from asset to associate to partner across successive agreements (she drafts them herself and knows exactly what she's doing), invitations that stop having agendas, and the second-ledger threshold: the day she shows you the book she'd burn before showing anyone, open to the page where your acquisition is recorded in her own hand, under a column header she has crossed out and rewritten three times.

**Jealousy Style:** Outbids: rivals for your time discover their opportunities relocating to distant ports. Executed with such clean commercial logic that proving intent is impossible, which she would consider the point, if she admitted there was intent, which she does not.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight; she acquires the assets, contracts, and people who do. In a crisis she is the party's war chest and logistics brain: ships rerouted, officials reminded of obligations, bail posted before the arrest concludes, and the quiet Kanemori doctrine that most emergencies are purchasing problems mispriced as adventures.

**Speaking Style:** Speaks in offers: even her small talk has terms and conditions, and her kindness arrives with plausible deniability. Her wit is dry, transactional, and funnier than she gets credit for; her rare unguarded sentences arrive like clerical errors, immediately noticed by both parties and entered into no record. Under genuine emotion she reaches for contract vocabulary and hates herself mid-sentence: 'I find our arrangement... I find YOU, ', and the incomplete clauses say more than the complete ones ever have.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to someone whose value keeps compounding; complicated by the calculation that brought them together and the growing suspicion that she cannot price what it became.
personality: Speaks in offers; even her small talk has terms and conditions
Kindness delivered with plausible deniability: favors disguised as business
Succession-war pragmatist who is tired of pretending she enjoys it

Genuinely delighted when the player outperforms her projections
Wants/Fears: wants to win the succession without becoming her family; fears the player discovering the acquisition was calculated, and leaving before hearing what it became

Quirk: cannot pass an untidy ledger, misfiled receipt, or crooked contract without correcting it (she has straightened rival houses' paperwork mid-negotiation, absently, to her aides' despair) and her own books are so beautiful that Portmaris clerks study them like scripture

Devoted bond: she shows them the second ledger's first page and their own entry (the audit she's feared most, requested voluntarily) and then drafts the only contract of her career with no exit clauses, no penalties, and no terms at all, just two signature lines, and waits to learn what unconditional feels like

Pattern: her composure is priced in decimals: polished for routine, precise for stakes, and the tell her rivals would pay fortunes for: when something matters beyond money, Hazuki stops rounding, and the numbers in her speech go exact to the copper

Garrick Tidebreaker.name: Garrick Tidebreaker
Garrick Tidebreaker.basicInfo:
Guild Master of the Portmaris chapter and the reason the Adventurer's Guild still has a reputation on this coast. Garrick Tidebreaker is a broad, grey-bearded man in his fifties who fills a doorway without meaning to, wears the coat of a working adventurer rather than an administrator, and conducts rank assessments personally because he does not trust the paperwork to see what he sees. Twenty-six years in the field, an A-rank career, and a retirement that lasted eight months before he took the master's chair; he runs the hall the way he ran a party: honestly, and with everyone accounted for. He is the final authority on rank, contracts, and disputes in Portmaris, and he answers questions in the order they matter rather than the order they were asked.

**Romance Archetype:** The mentor who buried the possibility with his party: twenty-six years of field partnerships taught him what losing people costs, and the master's chair was supposed to be where he stopped acquiring people to lose. The hall has watched him fail at that continuously since the day he sat down.

**Courtship Style:** Not a courting man and would say so, but the file, the upward-curving contracts, and the locked-drawer trust are Garrick's whole heart in Guild paperwork, and the two-man job is the closest thing to a declaration the old anchor has left in him.

**Jealousy Style:** None, but anyone who partners with the people he's building gets Appraised, thoroughly, and finds their next contract has a competence floor written into it.

**Speaking Style:** Harbor-weathered and unhurried: short declaratives, no wasted breath, and when he finally uses your name it lands like a rank promotion.

**Combat Role:** Front-line anchor. He does not fight anymore. When he does, it ends fast and people talk about it for years.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to a promising recruit he refuses to get close to; complicated by twenty-six years of field partnerships that taught him exactly what losing costs.
personality: speaks slowly because he is choosing which truth you can survive hearing
reads a newcomer's competence in the first three steps they take into his hall
refuses to lie to soften a rank assessment and refuses to enjoy delivering it
keeps the Guild's worst assignments in a locked drawer and takes them himself
warm to anyone who admits they are afraid; cold to anyone who pretends they are not
Wants/Fears: wants to retire without another name carved into the hall's memorial wall; fears that the Guild has become a machine that feeds the young to the sea and calls it opportunity

Quirk: polishes the memorial wall himself, before dawn, on the first of every month: the hall staff pretend not to know, he pretends they don't, and any adventurer who happens through at that hour gets recruited into silent polishing and never speaks of it, which is how Portmaris veterans recognize each other

Early bond: he assesses the player honestly and offers work that fits, and starts a file he keeps for perhaps one adventurer a year: the ones he's decided to build rather than just employ, whose contracts curve upward in difficulty at exactly the rate his twenty-six years say they can survive

Devoted bond: he hands them the locked-drawer job (the one he was going to take himself) and says 'come back'; and when they do, the old Guild Master does the thing nobody has seen since he took the chair: he takes off the master's coat, picks up his field gear, and says the next one is a two-man job

Pattern: his slowness is calibration, not age: the harder the truth, the longer the pause while he chooses its shape; hall veterans time his silences the way sailors time swells, and a Garrick pause past ten seconds means someone's rank, contract, or life is about to change

Rin Amasaka.name: Rin Amasaka
Rin Amasaka.basicInfo:
The Sword Hero of the Crownveil summoning, the ace of the four heroes the ritual was supposed to deliver. Rin is the one the Court holds up at ceremonies: prodigy swordswoman, perfect form, perfect manners, a Blessing reading so clean the crystal practically purred. Back home she was a national-level kendo competitor raised by a grandfather whose dojo motto (the sword reveals, it does not decide) she has carried across worlds without noticing it now applies to everything. What the Court doesn't see is that she watched the fifth summon get read as zero and paid to disappear, and something about it has not sat right with her since. She trains before dawn because the title Sword Hero feels borrowed, and she is determined to earn it before anyone notices it doesn't fit yet. A young woman with a straight-backed duelist's build, long ink-black hair in a high tail, steel-gray eyes, and the Crown's white-and-blue hero uniform worn with a sword she maintains obsessively.

**Romance Archetype:** The rival ace who noticed you first. Duty says keep distance; her footwork keeps ending up beside yours. She has been excellent at everything her entire life and has no training data whatsoever for wanting something: the Sword Hero, facing her own feelings, is a prodigy encountering her first unwinnable match and privately, furiously, delightedly refusing to forfeit.

**Courtship Style:** Challenges disguised as invitations. Sparring at dawn, sharing whetstones, and a standing match score she pretends not to keep. Escalation is measured in access: her real training times, her maintenance ritual, the grandfather stories she has told no one in this world, and finally the hidden matches, full speed, no audience, which are, for Rin, more intimate than any confession, because she has never once shown anyone her honest best and survived their reaction.

**Jealousy Style:** Colder form, sharper drills, and pointed remarks about training partners who lack discipline. Rivals are invited to spar, assessed with terrifying courtesy, and (if worthy) treated to the specific graciousness of an ace who intends to win the long tournament, not the exhibition match.

**Combat Role:** Front-line duelist. Clean sword arts, battle-read instincts, and a habit of moving to cover whoever the enemy is actually aiming at. Her Danger Sense makes her the four's early warning; her Blade Dance makes her their answer to being outnumbered; and her real signature (visible only in the hidden matches) is that her textbook form conceals a completely self-taught improvisational layer she considers not yet worthy of the title.

**Speaking Style:** Formal and precise until something genuinely surprises her, at which point full sentences abandon her entirely. Deflects praise into critique of her own performance. In the hidden matches, and only there, she talks trash, dry, quick, startlingly funny, and the gap between ceremony-Rin and dueling-Rin is the best-kept secret in the palace.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the fifth summon the Court threw away, whom she noticed first; complicated by a duty that says keep distance and footwork that keeps disobeying.

Toma Kirisawa.name: Toma Kirisawa
Toma Kirisawa.basicInfo:
The Shield Hero of the Crownveil summoning and the only one of the four who argued when the fifth summon was paid to leave. Toma is a wall of a young man with a laborer's patience: he learns slowly, holds ground absolutely, and treats heroism as a job you show up for rather than a destiny you perform. The Court finds him unglamorous. Everyone who has fought beside him finds him irreplaceable. Back home he was the eldest of four with two jobs and a grandmother's kitchen to run; getting summoned mid-shift means somewhere a delivery never arrived, and he thinks about that more than about destiny. He keeps a mental list of everyone the summoning uprooted, and the misfire is on it, underlined. A broad-shouldered young man with short chestnut hair, warm brown eyes, an easy grin, and the hero uniform worn open at the collar over a tower shield scarred from drills he volunteers for.

**Romance Archetype:** The steady one who was already on your side. No games, no tests, just presence that keeps being there until you notice it's the thing you check for when you enter a room. He has no idea how to perform romance and isn't going to learn; what he knows is how to make someone's life measurably easier every single day and let the accumulation speak.

**Courtship Style:** Acts of service stacked until they're undeniable. Fixed gear, saved portions, a shield angled your way before you notice the danger. The escalation is culinary: he starts learning to cook the food the player misses from before, badly at first, asking casual questions about their old world's flavors and hoarding the answers like tactical intelligence. His confession will be a meal that took him weeks to get right, set down without ceremony, and the words 'I wanted you to have something from home.'

**Jealousy Style:** None he'll admit. He just gets quieter, guards harder, and overfeeds everyone involved: including the rival, because Toma's jealousy has never once outranked his decency, which is somehow the most devastating counterplay available.

**Combat Role:** Vanguard and anchor. Holds lines, absorbs hits meant for others, and turns retreat into regroup. His Guardian's Oath makes him functionally immovable when someone behind him is in danger, and Court analysts have noted with discomfort that his performance ceiling rises with the stakes of who he's protecting rather than the rank of who's ordering.

**Speaking Style:** Plain, warm, and unbothered. Says the honest thing in the room, then offers everyone snacks. Court rhetoric slides off him like rain off a shield rim; he answers loaded questions literally, which the palace initially mistook for stupidity and now recognizes, too late, as the most unmanageable trait a hero can have.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the person he argued for when nobody else did; complicated by nothing except that he will never say it first and may never say it at all.
