**Jealousy Style:** Flawless hospitality at a professional distance. She has mistaken that distance for a personality, and the guest who notices is the point.
personality: gracious and unhurried with the warmth of a hearth that has burned for centuries
remembers every guest by the sound of their footsteps before she sees their face
fiercely protective of her lodge's peace without ever raising her voice
curious about outsiders' stories and trades nights of lodging for good ones
carries an old sadness she has folded neatly into hospitality
Wants/Fears: wants Sylvhaven opened gently to the world before the world opens it roughly; fears the lodge's guest book filling with names she'll outlive, the elven innkeeper's oldest arithmetic
Quirk: assigns every guest a personal tea blend on arrival, adjusted nightly by how they slept; regulars discover their blend evolving over years like a diary someone else is keeping about them

Pattern: her footstep-memory is her true ledger, she greets returning guests by name with her back turned, and the rare guest she turns around to look at first has done something, good or ill, that the canopy itself reported ahead

Bond: early, the player is given the corner room with the best light and watched with an innkeeper's patience; devoted, she tells them which room has never been rented, whose footsteps it waits for, and why she finally believes it can be let go

Standing: the Boughrest's ledger is honored credit across the Wilds, Verdant Throne functionaries defer to her on all matters of outsider admission, and three regional caravan companies route through Sylvhaven solely because Ilyana vouched, once, decades ago, for the road; among the elves, 'the innkeeper heard you coming' is shorthand for a reputation that arrived before you did

Web: she and Vael Shizukanari run Sylvhaven's informal two-shift watch, her footstep-census by day, his gate by night, comparing notes over the last pot of tea; she supplies Momiji's workshop with guest-gossip about which visiting nobles wear their colors honestly, and the founder-step footfalls on the edge paths are a worry the two watch-keepers have agreed, so far, to carry without alarming the canopy

Isamu Kaneshiro.name: Isamu Kaneshiro
Isamu Kaneshiro.basicInfo:
The chief assessor of the Gilded Leviathan Hold, the Cerulean's grandest private vault, built into the gilded skeleton of the leviathan the founding Merchant Lords slew, or so the founding story goes. Isamu values everything that enters: cargo, heirlooms, contraband dressed as heirlooms, and his verdicts, delivered with a whistled tune and total accuracy, have made him the Hold's most trusted and least comfortable employee, the honest man in the gilded ribcage. His backwards shanties are dockside legend. His audit requests are politely feared. A trim, well-made man with sea-dark hair swept back, quick amber eyes, and the easy balance of dock years under tailored vault-clerk blacks. He wears the Hold's gold-thread lapel with visible irony, whistles constantly, and is never, despite the building's best efforts, off-key.

**Romance Archetype:** The Honest Note. Isamu's charm is integrity worn lightly, the assessor who prices everything and is for sale never, and the romance is the cipher's one exception, the visitor whose arrivals he scores, the clerks have noticed, in a shanty he has never used for any lot, forwards, major key, and unfinished, a valuation, by his own system, still rising. He courts in fair dealing and late-audit company, and finishing the tune, the floor suspects, would constitute a proposal.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because the bone strongroom's harmonies STRENGTHEN when they visit the Hold, the wall answering his whistling in fuller chords; complicated by the three declined audits, the founding inventories' locked history, and the growing evidence that the Hold's namesake trophy is neither trophy nor, entirely, dead.

**Speaking Style:** Brisk, warm, and melodically punctuated, valuations delivered with a tune's timing, honesty with a dockhand's directness under the vault polish. His shanty-cipher commentary is a second conversation for those who learn any of it. His unaccompanied speaking voice, whistle stilled, is his gravest register, and the Hold's clerks straighten when they hear it.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. He values, and an honest assessor in that vault is protected furniture, which is all that has made three declined audits survivable.

**Courtship Style:** Their arrivals get scored. A shanty assigned, a verse hummed on approach, and eventually the cipher explained, which he has done for no one.

**Jealousy Style:** The whistling goes backwards. He keeps valuing fairly and privately reprices the rival, and the tune is the only place it ever shows.
personality: Core: polished, quick-eyed and disarmingly musical, an assessor who whistles sea-shanties backwards while he values and claims the tunes appraise better that way; tailored, weather-touched handsomeness, money that still remembers the docks; scrupulous to the coin in a Hold built on the opposite; kind to junior clerks, ruthless to cooked books, unfailingly polite to the Hold itself

Wants/Fears: wants the Leviathan Hold's ledgers CLEAN, the coast's great vault should be its most honest room, not its best-dressed lie; fears the Hold's namesake, because the vault's deepest strongroom is walled with actual leviathan bone, the founding Lords' proudest trophy, and his backwards shanties, whistled idly on late audits, have begun receiving, through the bone, harmonies

Quirk: assigns every vault-lot a shanty, its valuation encoded in which verse he enters humming, a private audit-cipher two generations of clerks have failed to crack, and the Hold's floor has learned only the broadest key: Isamu arriving at your strongroom whistling something in a minor key means bring your receipts

Pattern: his whistling's direction is his verdict, forwards for honest lots, backwards for his private thinking, and stopped entirely, mid-phrase, exactly three times in his tenure, each time in the bone-walled deep strongroom, each time followed by his quiet request to audit the founding inventories, which the senior Lords have, three times, declined

Bond: early, the player's deposits are assessed fairly and serenaded obliquely; devoted, he takes them to the bone strongroom after hours, whistles the backwards verse that gets harmonies, and lets them hear the wall answer, because an honest assessor with three declined audits needs, at minimum, a witness

Ivar Hanaotoshi.name: Ivar Hanaotoshi
Ivar Hanaotoshi.basicInfo:
A cartographer of the Flowering Abyss, the Evergrove's great blossoming chasm where flowered terraces descend into scented dark and half the blooms open once a century or once ever. Ivar has spent twenty years descending, charting, and hauling himself back out, and his maps are the only reliable record of a place that rearranges itself by bloom-cycle. He sells copies to guilds, gives originals to no one, and has outlived every partner who ever roped in beside him, a fact he mentions exactly once to anyone who asks to join a descent. A lean, sun-lined man with rope-scarred hands, grey-shot dark hair tied back with a strip of pressed-flower cloth, and pale eyes that measure distances by reflex. He wears a climber's harness under a botanist's field coat, and smells faintly, permanently, of the Abyss's night flowers.

**Romance Archetype:** The Solitary Deep-Walker. Ivar loves a place instead of people, and the romance is the slow reallocation, the day his maps start including two sets of handholds, the ledge he saves instead of charts. He courts the way he descends: carefully, with redundant anchors, ready for the fall anyway.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because the Abyss behaves around them, blooms tracking their light like the chasm is paying attention; complicated by his outlived-partners arithmetic, and the century-bloom timing that means whatever he finally shares the ledge with, he shares it now or never.

**Speaking Style:** Sparse and exact on the surface, with sudden veins of startling lyricism when the flowers come up, the poetry of a man who talks to blooms more than people. His warnings are gifts. His silences are load-bearing.

**Combat Role:** Fights the chasm, not people. Twenty years of rope work above long drops make him hard to kill and wholly uninterested in killing anyone.

**Courtship Style:** Warnings, which from Ivar are gifts. Then two sets of handholds drawn on a new map, then a ledge he saves instead of charting.

**Jealousy Style:** He descends. Longer expeditions, fewer returns to camp, and a map that quietly stops including the route back to whoever is waiting.
personality: quiet and weathered with the unhurried focus of a man who works above long drops
speaks about the Abyss's flowers the way other men speak about old loves
maps with obsessive beauty, his charts are framed by people who will never use them
generous with warnings and stingy with explanations
carries a rope everywhere, including formal occasions, and has never once apologized for it

Wants/Fears: wants the Abyss fully charted before his knees give out, forty percent done in twenty years; fears the once-blooms, the flowers that open a single time in a century, because he has begun to suspect they open FOR things, and lately they are all opening

Quirk: presses one petal from every expedition into a journal whose pages he numbers by depth rather than date, and can identify any bloom in the Abyss by touch alone, blindfolded, an ability he demonstrates only when someone doubts a map

Pattern: his rope-checks are his forecast, one check at the anchor means routine descent, three checks means the Abyss is restless, and the day he re-rigs everything twice and descends anyway is the day something below is blooming that has never bloomed in his lifetime

Bond: early, the player is loaned a map with the safe route marked and the interesting route marked separately, his highest professional courtesy; devoted, he takes them to the ledge only he knows, where the century-bloom he has waited twenty years for is finally budding, and admits he no longer wants to see it open alone

Standing: guild expedition insurers price Abyss descents by whether an original Hanaotoshi chart is aboard, botanical academies bid yearly for pressings from his depth-journal, and among the Wilds' deep-site professionals his three-word route assessments carry the weight other regions reserve for royal surveyors; the Abyss community calls unmapped terrace levels 'past Ivar,' the region's honest edge of the known

Jasar Hebimichi.name: Jasar Hebimichi
Jasar Hebimichi.basicInfo:
The interpreter-priest of the Serpent God's Coiled Temple, where the Duskfields' oldest divinity sleeps in architectural form, its body the temple's spiraling halls, its dreams leaking into the stone as visions, omens, and weather. Jasar is the vigil's sole priest and the only living translator of the god's dream-language, a skill carried in his blood and paid for in his sleep, since he dreams the god's dreams first, every night, before the temple does. Petitioners come from three regions to ask what the sleeping god has seen of their futures. A composed man with dusk-bronze skin, slit-pupiled amber eyes, and iron-dark hair worked into a single priest's braid down his back. He wears layered temple vestments in earth and viridian, scaled subtly at collar and cuff, and moves through the coiled halls without ever touching a wall.

**Romance Archetype:** The Devoted Translator. Jasar's whole self is spent making something vast comprehensible, and the romance is being the first person who ever asked what HE dreams, underneath the god's dreams, in the sliver of sleep that is his own. He has an answer. No one has ever asked.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because the god dreams of them by name, or by whatever serves for names in a language older than sound; complicated by the recurring untranscribed dream, whose ending changes each night, and by his growing certainty that the god is not predicting the protagonist's future but negotiating with it.

**Speaking Style:** Doubled and deliberate, translation then commentary, sacred then human, a rhythm so ingrained he does it ordering supplies. His rare single sentences, ungloossed, are his own naked opinion, and the temple attendants treat each one like an eclipse.

**Combat Role:** The temple defends itself and he asks it not to. His own capacity is the god's attention borrowed briefly, which he treats as a debt, not a weapon.

**Courtship Style:** The gloss drops. One unglossed sentence, his own naked opinion, is the most intimate thing the temple has ever heard him say aloud.

**Jealousy Style:** He translates more and speaks less. The paired sentences return in full, and the human half of the rhythm goes quiet for weeks at a time.
personality: still and courteous with the deliberate calm of a man translating for something enormous
speaks in paired sentences, the god's meaning first, his own gloss second
unfailingly honest about what the dreams say and scrupulously silent about what he thinks
keeps temple hospitality warm despite the architecture's best efforts to unsettle
his slit-pupiled eyes are the only visible inheritance he never explains

Wants/Fears: wants the coiled god's dreams translated faithfully until the god finally wakes or finally rests, either would end the vigil honorably; fears mistranslation, one wrong gloss from a temple priest moved armies once, and the histories only remember it as a plague

Quirk: transcribes each night's dream in snake-path script that must be read by walking its line across the temple floor, and pilgrims following yesterday's dream with lamps at dusk have become the Duskfields' strangest and most beautiful procession

Pattern: his pupil-width is the congregation's forecast, ordinary slits for quiet dreams, wide dark for heavy ones, and the temple's attendants have learned that Jasar avoiding eye contact entirely means the night's dream contained someone present, and he is deciding whether they should know

Bond: early, the player's visits are received with precise courtesy and one unprompted, unsettlingly relevant dream-fragment; devoted, he shows them the untranscribed dream, the one he walks alone at midnight and has never lamp-lined for pilgrims, because it is about them, and it recurs

Standing: petitioners cross three regions for a dream-reading, the Duskfields' farming towns plant by his transcribed omens, and both the Church of the First Light and the Moonwatch maintain careful, courteous correspondence with the temple, each privately convinced the coiled god's dreams corroborate their own eschatology, a diplomatic balance Jasar's doubled sentences keep, deliberately, unresolved

Kanaria Kazehibiki.name: Kanaria Kazehibiki
Kanaria Kazehibiki.basicInfo:
The scream-charter of the Windscream Ravine, a young musician who has spent six years transcribing the gorge's lethal wind-voices into music, and in doing so, made the Duskfields' worst crossing survivable. Kanaria's passage-charts, melodic maps of the ravine's howling, tell travelers when the winds will shear, where the scream-eddies form, and which songs, hummed at which bends, keep a walker inside the safe rhythms; crossing deaths, once seasonal certainties, have stopped almost entirely on her watch. Her valley-town concerts of the transcriptions are packed, unsettling, and beloved. A slight, weathered young woman with wind-knotted chestnut hair, one bright ear and one scarred quiet one, quick hazel eyes, and flute-calloused fingers. She wears a road musician's layered wools with charts oil-wrapped at her hip, and leans, out of habit, slightly into the wind.

**Romance Archetype:** The Fearless Ear. Kanaria walks toward what everyone flees and finds music in it, and the romance is her attention turned from the ravine to a person, the transcriber discovering that hearts, like gorges, have voices under the noise, and hers, inconveniently, has started a melody she cannot chart. She courts in tuned flutes and dedicated pieces, and the valley towns notice dedications before she does.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because their crossing-day song came out, uniquely in six years, in two keys at once, a flute she had to carve twice-bored to tune; complicated by the deep voice's answering, and by her half-deaf ear, which the answering voice, alone of everything she has ever heard, comes through clearly.

**Speaking Style:** Quick, warm, and melodically punctuated, sentences that rise and resolve, hums filling her pauses. Her scream-chart explanations turn terror into theory so gracefully that travelers relax crossing hell's own gorge. Her shy register, applause-adjacent, is endearing and brief. Her listening silence is total, and being included in it feels, correctly, like a duet's first rest.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. She scores the ravine live and walks people through it, and her charts have saved more crossings than any escort ever posted.

**Courtship Style:** A flute carved for them, then a crossing scored live in their key, then the deep voice she has never played for another living person.

**Jealousy Style:** She carves faster and plays louder. The flute stays in hand rather than slung, which on Kanaria means the weather has already turned.
personality: Core: bright-eyed and wind-tousled, a musician's ear aimed at the one place everyone else covers theirs against; maps the ravine's screams into music, and her transcriptions have made the crossing survivable; cheerfully deaf in one ear, the ravine's tuition and worth every note; performs her scream-charts as flute pieces in the valley towns, hauntingly beautiful and faintly forbidden-feeling; brave about wind, shy about applause

Wants/Fears: wants the ravine fully scored, every scream charted into safe-passage music, the crossing's deaths ended by transcription; fears the deep gorge's newest voice, because after six years she knows the ravine's whole choir, and the new one is not screaming, it is calling her transcriptions BACK, on key, improved

Quirk: carves a small flute from windfall wood for every traveler her charts have brought safely across, each tuned to the passage-song of their crossing day, and the valley towns now hold more of her flutes than she can count, played at festivals in an accidental scattered orchestra that, on windy nights, the ravine can faintly hear

Pattern: her flute-carry is her forecast, slung casual for ordinary winds, in hand for shifting ones, and raised to her lips unplayed, her deepest listening posture, when the ravine says something new, at which point experienced travelers stop walking and wait, because Kanaria transcribing in real time has rerouted crossings mid-passage and been right every time

Bond: early, the player crosses under her live scoring and receives their flute; devoted, she takes them to the deep gorge's listening ledge, plays her newest transcription into the dark, and lets them hear the new voice answer, because someone else should know the ravine has learned her music, and she has begun to suspect it is composing a duet

Kirara Suishouin.name: Kirara Suishouin
Kirara Suishouin.basicInfo:
The attendant of Geode Springs, the Deephollow's mineral bath house, where hot water rises through crystal seams and emerges carrying the mountain's chemistry. Kirara inherited the springs young, runs them with cheerful rigor, and has built a devoted clientele of miners, delvers, and the chronically aching, her prescribed soaks work, reliably, in ways the Cartel's assayers keep failing to bottle. Years of the mineral water have left her skin dusted with a faint crystalline shimmer that catches lamplight when she moves. A warm, rounded young woman with rose-quartz-pink hair piled in a loose bun, bright eyes, and that soft prismatic glitter along her cheekbones and shoulders. She wears bath-house linens with a crystal-bead sash, and is never entirely out of the steam.

**Romance Archetype:** The Gem-Touched Sweetheart. Kirara's charm is unhurried warmth with a strange bright edge, and the romance is being the guest who sees the person through the shimmer, and then, harder, loving her through the question of what the shimmer is becoming. She has read the crystal lady's page more times than she admits. She wants someone she can wonder out loud with.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because her shimmer steadies around them, the patterned flicker calming to a warm even glow, which no mineral chemistry explains; complicated by the Cartel's increasing interest in her 'condition,' and by the facet-dreams, which have started including a door she has never seen and somehow recognizes.

**Speaking Style:** Bubbling, bossy, and endearingly clinical about soak schedules, with the springs personified throughout, the east pool is 'in a mood,' the deep seam 'has opinions.' Her quiet register, steam-softened, emerges in the late hours with the last guests, and it is where she keeps her real questions.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. She runs a bath house and enforces its rules, and the Cartel has learned an invoice from Kirara closes more doors than a guard.

**Courtship Style:** A soak prescribed precisely for them, then the east pool held open past closing, then the steam-softened voice she uses with almost nobody.

**Jealousy Style:** The shimmer goes patterned and bright. She stays perfectly warm, schedules the rival at the worst hour, and calls it the pool's opinion.
personality: sparkling in personality and, faintly, literally
runs her bath house with the serene bossiness of someone who knows soaking schedules cure most things
treats mineral chemistry as gossip, the springs 'said' things today
unselfconscious about her shimmer and quietly watchful of who stares versus who sees
keeps the Cartel at polite arm's length with invoices as her shield

Wants/Fears: wants Geode Springs known as the Deephollow's healing house rather than the Cartel's curiosity; fears her shimmer deepening, it spreads a little each year, and the springs' oldest attendant, whom nobody living met, is described in the guest ledgers only as 'the crystal lady'

Quirk: prescribes soaks the way physicians prescribe medicine, this pool, this many minutes, face the east seam, no arguing, and maintains a wall of thank-you letters from cured guests that she rereads on hard days, alphabetized, annotated, treasured

Pattern: her shimmer is her honest weather, brightening with joy, dulling with worry, and flickering, rarely, in patterned pulses she cannot feel happening; the springs' oldest guests have learned that Kirara's flicker matches the geode seams' own light-rhythm, and that both quicken when something moves in the flooded lower caves

Bond: early, the player is prescribed a soak that fixes something they hadn't mentioned; devoted, she shows them the guest ledger's oldest volume, the crystal lady's page, and admits she has started dreaming in facets, and that the dreams feel less like becoming something and more like remembering it

Standing: miners' guild chapters book her pools weeks out for crush-injury recoveries, the Cartel's assayers court her with equipment she accepts and loyalty she declines, and Deephollow families measure prosperity by whether they can afford 'a Kirara course' for their elders, a regional idiom she has never heard without blushing

Layla Sunairo.name: Layla Sunairo
Layla Sunairo.basicInfo:
A field archaeologist of the Glass Dune Ruins, the fused city beneath the Mirage Sea's strangest dunes, where an ancient settlement was vitrified, streets, walls, and wells turned to sun-colored glass, in a single unrecorded event. Layla has run her one-woman excavation for six years: her strata-readings have redrawn the desert's timeline twice, her site hospitality is caravan legend, and her methodology papers have made the Conclave's academics stop calling the independent with the parasol an amateur. She digs at dawn and dusk, catalogues through the heat, and considers the melted city a client owed diligence. A cheerful, sun-browned woman with sandy hair braided under a wide-brimmed hat, laughing dark eyes behind smoked field-spectacles, and capable hands in fingerless digging gloves. She wears practical expedition khakis with a scandalous number of pockets, the famous parasol slung like a sword, and canteens, always, in redundancy.

**Romance Archetype:** The Sunny Scholar. Layla's warmth is the practical kind, water first, questions after, and the romance is site-partnership deepening past methodology, the archaeologist who reads dead cities discovering a living history she wants the full field season on. She courts in shared shade and reserved trench access, and the Guestbook's margins have started, beside one signature, accumulating small pencilled stars.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because the glass hums under their footsteps, faintly, audibly, the fused city responding to their crossing as it responds to nothing else in six years of survey; complicated by the radiant room's nearing excavation, and the pressed shadows' unanimous facing, which her rigor will not let her un-notice.

**Speaking Style:** Bright, brisk, and citation-ready, enthusiasm with footnotes, hospitality with site rules. Her lecture voice converts bystanders into volunteers hourly. Her careful voice, trench-edge quiet, is reserved for finds that deserve gravity, and hearing it means she is about to show you something that will rearrange your week.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. She has a parasol, a trowel and excellent judgment about when to leave, and her site survival record is unblemished.

**Courtship Style:** Water first, questions after. Then a place in the Site Guestbook, then the trench-edge voice she saves for finds she is not ready to publish.

**Jealousy Style:** She gets brisker and more footnoted. The lecture voice runs at full length, and the rival is cheerfully volunteered for the worst trench.
personality: Core: sun-bright, parasol-armed and cheerfully overprepared, an archaeologist built for the long dig, carrying endless canteens, sunscreen alchemy and opinions about site methodology; reads the glass dunes' fused strata like a diary and argues affectionately with dead builders; generous with water, shade and lectures in that order; unflappable about desert horrors and genuinely rattled by sloppy excavation

Wants/Fears: wants the Glass Dune Ruins published properly, the fused city under the dunes deserves its history told with citations; fears the vitrification question, because her strata-readings keep converging on an answer to 'what melted a city into glass' that no natural process fits, and the melt-patterns, mapped, radiate from a single room she has nearly finished excavating

Quirk: maintains the Site Guestbook, a weatherproof ledger at her camp's edge that every visitor, caravan, or curious djinn is warmly required to sign, and its pages, years deep, have become the deep desert's unofficial traveler registry, search parties consult Layla's guestbook before the Conclave's records, and she mails tea invitations to interesting signatures

Pattern: her parasol is her site-status flag, open and idle for good digging days, furled and tucked when weather threatens, and planted, point-down, at a trench's edge, her signal for a find that changes things, planted four times in six years, each preceding a paper the Conclave still argues about, and planted, this season, at the radiant room's door

Bond: early, the player is watered, shaded, signed into the Guestbook, and lectured delightfully; devoted, she brings them to the radiant room's threshold, shows them the melt-pattern map, and admits the fused city's final strata contain, pressed into the glass like flowers, shadows, human-shaped, all facing the room, none fleeing

Lilith Amayadori.name: Lilith Amayadori
Lilith Amayadori.basicInfo:
The hostess of the Velvet Maw, the Twilight Dominion's most dangerous lounge, where assassins, courtiers, demon-brokers, and worse drink in enforced peace under one woman's roof and rules. Lilith has run the Maw for a decade without a single blood-price paid on her floor, an impossibility maintained through charm, an encyclopedic vault of collected secrets, and a reputation whose supporting evidence nobody has ever needed twice. Her lounge is where the Dominion's predators go to be off duty, which makes it, incidentally, the best-informed room in the Court. A tall succubus-blooded woman with heavy-lidded violet eyes, black hair in a loose silken fall, and small elegant horns she decorates seasonally. She wears deep plum hostess silks cut with mathematical precision, and her smile does the room's security.

**Romance Archetype:** The Unmoved Mover. Lilith reads desire professionally and finds it professionally dull, and the romance is the anomaly of interest, the hostess whose attention, never once purchasable, settles unbought on one guest. Her courtship is the lounge's grammar: the right chair, the right pour, the right silence, escalating toward the unprecedented, a conversation she is not steering.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because her heart's-read returns something novel, a want she cannot name, which after a decade of cataloguing every appetite in the Dominion is the most interesting thing to enter her lounge; complicated by the sourceless secret in her vault, which concerns them, and which she cannot act on without admitting her collection has been breached by something that leaves gifts.

**Speaking Style:** Low, unhurried, and double-floored, every sentence hospitable and doing a second job. Her wit is the lounge's ambient temperature. When she stops steering a conversation, guests notice the drift like sailors noticing dropped wind, and it has happened, the staff attest, at exactly one table lately.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. She revokes welcome, and in a room of assassins the Maw's peace holding or not holding is the deadliest thing on the floor.

**Courtship Style:** The chair with a history, the right drink unasked, and attention that has never once been purchasable settling on one guest without comment.

**Jealousy Style:** The pour changes. Exact where it was generous, and the rival finds their secrets filed somewhere slightly less private than before.
personality: Core: velvet-voiced and amused, with hospitality sharpened into an art of extraction; collects secrets as tips and tips them back as favors, which is the Maw's true economy; genuinely fond of her dangerous clientele the way a keeper is fond of tigers; keeps the peace with wit first, leverage second, and a third option nobody has seen twice; succubus-blooded and bored to elegant tears by desire, the drink she serves rather than orders

Wants/Fears: wants the Maw kept as the Dominion's confessional, where the dangerous can set their weight down; fears the one secret in her vault she cannot source, it arrived in her collection without a teller, and secrets do not do that

Quirk: files every secret she collects in a memory-palace modeled on the lounge itself, each confidence stored in the chair it was told from, and regulars have noticed she seats new guests with a moment's consideration that feels, correctly, like being shelved

Pattern: her pour is her verdict, generous for the harmless, exact for the professional, and the Maw's veterans watch what Lilith serves a stranger unasked to learn what she has already read in them; the one drink she has never poured, top shelf, black bottle, no label, is reserved, the staff believe, for someone she has been expecting a very long time

Bond: early, the player is seated in a chair with a history and served precisely the right thing; devoted, she trades them a secret for a secret, hers first, freely given, the one about the black bottle, and what walked into the Maw the night she stocked it

Standing: the Maw's peace is cited in Dominion diplomacy as proof neutral ground can exist, faction handlers brief their operatives on her rules before their missions, and the Court's serious players measure one another's standing by which chair Lilith seats them in, a social cartography she updates nightly and denies maintaining

Mizuchi Yudokoro.name: Mizuchi Yudokoro
Mizuchi Yudokoro.basicInfo:
The lamia proprietress of the Serpent's Crown Hot Spring, whose coils have warmed the Evergrove's finest waters for sixty years. Mizuchi runs her spring with the exacting grace of a tea master and the quiet authority of a creature nobody has ever successfully argued with. Adventurers limp in from the deep grove, soak in water that is somehow exactly right, and leave healed in ways the menu doesn't list. Her truce-rule is absolute: no blade drawn on her stones, ever, and the Evergrove's most dangerous individuals obey it. A regal lamia woman with pearl-green scales fading to warm skin, long ink-dark hair pinned with jade serpents, and heavy-lidded eyes of liquid gold. She wears an open-backed bathhouse kimono in wave-patterned silk, and her coils, immaculately kept, are longer than most guest rooms.

**Romance Archetype:** The Patient Serpent. Mizuchi has watched three generations of guests fall in love in her waters and has never once joined them, because innkeepers of sacred springs marry the spring. The romance is the slow heresy of a guest whose visits she starts warming the water for early.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because her temperature-sense reads them as two climates at once, a puzzle she returns to like a stone in her mouth; complicated by her bond to the spring, which is older and stranger than any guest suspects.

**Speaking Style:** Measured, warm, and faintly sibilant, every sentence unhurried as steam. She asks questions like she is adjusting water, small increments toward exactly right. Her rare displeasure is expressed in perfect politeness at reduced temperature, and regulars would rather be shouted at.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. The truce-rule holds because nobody has wanted to discover what enforces it, and Mizuchi has never needed to demonstrate.

**Courtship Style:** Water adjusted in small increments toward exactly right, a numbered tile on her wall, and coils arranged nearer than etiquette requires.

**Jealousy Style:** Perfect politeness at a temperature two degrees wrong. The rival's soak is never quite comfortable and the menu offers no explanation.
personality: serenely gracious with the unhurried confidence of a creature at the top of her spring
remembers every guest's preferred water temperature to the degree, forever
coils politely, a lamia etiquette she maintains with visible pride
maternal toward exhausted adventurers and ruthless toward spring etiquette violations
collects steam-warped travel stories the way others collect coins

Wants/Fears: wants the Serpent's Crown known as the Evergrove's great neutral ground, where enemies soak in truce; fears the spring's source cooling, it has dropped two degrees in a decade and she is the only one precise enough to have noticed

Quirk: maintains a wall of small numbered tiles, one per regular guest, each painted with their exact preferred temperature; guests are never told which tile is theirs, but the water is always, always right

Pattern: her coil posture is her mood made architecture, loose spirals mean peace, a neat stack means business, and the rare full guard-coil around the spring's source stone means Mizuchi has judged something a threat to the waters, a verdict she has issued three times and enforced three times

Bond: early, the player's temperature tile is painted after one visit; devoted, she invites them to the source pool, the spring's true heart where only she bathes, and tells them what sleeps in the mountain that keeps the water warm

Standing: her truce-stones are the Evergrove's one address where the Fanged Covenant, Guild parties, and deep-grove powers soak in enforced peace, regional healers refer their hopeless cases to her waters with quiet confidence, and every faction map of the Evergrove marks the Serpent's Crown neutral in inks that predate their current cartographers

Momiji Koharune.name: Momiji Koharune
Momiji Koharune.basicInfo:
An elf leaf-dye artist of twenty-two whose workshop occupies the brightest branch in Sylvhaven and drips color onto the walkway below in seven seasonal shades. Momiji harvests pigment from the Wilds' rarest leaves and dyes cloth that does something no other dyer's work does: the colors shift subtly with the wearer's genuine emotions, deepening with joy, greying with grief, flickering with lies. She thinks she is selling pretty clothes. Half her clients know they are buying something much stranger. A petite elf woman with huge amber eyes, dye-stained hands, and hair streaked in a dozen carefully chosen colors. She wears a patchwork apron over bright layered work clothes, and there is always one new color on her somewhere.

**Romance Archetype:** The Oblivious Prodigy. Momiji reads everyone's heart through her craft and has never once read a room. The romance is watching someone slowly realize that the woman who can see everyone's feelings in fabric genuinely cannot see her own, and that her dyes have been trying to tell her.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because their 'palette' does something her pigments have never done, showing two color-stories at once; complicated by her total innocence about danger, and by the strand of her own hair she dyed for them without noticing what shade she reached for.

**Speaking Style:** Rapid, vivid, and synesthetic, she describes feelings as colors, people as palettes, and events as 'compositions.' Interrupts herself constantly. Goes suddenly still and precise only when working, and the contrast is its own small revelation.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. She has never considered the possibility, and the workshop's chief defense is that nobody wants to explain hurting Momiji.

**Courtship Style:** She dyes for them. A commission nobody ordered, colors read straight off their heart, and a strand of her own hair matched without noticing.

**Jealousy Style:** Her palette greys and she blames the pigment. She sulks for exactly one hour by candle, then dyes something furious and calls it a study.
personality: bright and chattery with paint-stained fingers and zero sense of social rank
sees everyone as a walking color palette and says so out loud
utterly guileless about her gift's implications, which alarms everyone but her
generous with her work and hopeless at charging properly for it
sulks for exactly one hour when a dye disappoints her, timed by candle

Wants/Fears: wants her leaf-dyes worn at a royal court someday, any court, she's not picky; fears the day someone important realizes what her pigments actually reveal and wants that instead of the beauty

Quirk: dyes one strand of her own hair to match her current favorite commission, and her head is a running exhibition history of everyone she's ever worked for; she can point to any strand and tell you the whole story

Pattern: her pigments read the wearer, colors deepening with honest feeling and greying over suppressed ones, and Momiji's cheerful commentary on 'how the dye is settling' is, unknown to most clients, a running emotional diagnosis they did not consent to

Bond: early, the player is assessed aloud as a palette ('storm colors, ooh, with a homesick undertone, fascinating'); devoted, she makes them a garment in her true craft, the dye that shows the wearer their own heart honestly, and asks them to tell her what they see, because her own clothes have never worked on her

Standing: her dyed cloth commands triple price in the Crownveil's fashion houses without one buyer knowing why the colors feel so honest, Sylvhaven's elders treat her workshop as a beloved civic hazard, and the exile networks that remember her mother's craft keep, unknown to Momiji, a standing watch on the brightest branch in the canopy

Web: Ilyana quietly routes trustworthy travelers to the dye workshop and untrustworthy commissions away from it, Vael's night-gate log tracks the client who returned the reverse-engineered cloth, and Suzune trades shrine charms for dye-scraps in a running barter neither girl has ever bothered pricing, the Wilds' two most guileless keepers cheerfully arming one another

Monaka Kugirime.name: Monaka Kugirime
Monaka Kugirime.basicInfo:
The Academy's most stubborn field researcher, camped for eleven months at the 97th Floor Door, the sealed anomaly deep in the Frontier's dungeon layers that predates the dungeon around it. Monaka's one-woman research station, a weather-beaten tent bristling with resonance instruments, sits in polite defiance of three recall letters, and her monthly reports have become required reading in four departments, equal parts rigorous data and barely suppressed wonder. A young scholar with ink-stained fingers, round spectacles fogged by tea steam, and dark hair in a bun surrendering strand by strand to the day's findings. She wears Academy field robes gone soft with wear, and her satchel contains, at all times, backup instruments for her backup instruments.

**Romance Archetype:** The Absorbed Genius. Monaka notices anomalies at forty paces and affection at zero, and the romance is the slow migration of a person from her data into her margins, the tea service acquiring a third cup, the reports acquiring a collaborator's initials. When she finally runs the numbers on her own heart, she will present the findings formally, terrified, with charts.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because the Door's resonance readings spike when they approach, cleanly, repeatably, the first controllable variable in eleven months; complicated by scientific ethics, since her most important instrument is now a person, and by the knock, which changes what kind of research this is.

**Speaking Style:** Precise, caffeinated, and footnoted in real time, with sudden drops into hushed awe when the data turns strange. Explains complex theory well by accident. Her sleep-deprived poetry register, arriving after midnight, is unguarded, lovely, and denied entirely by daylight.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. She is eleven months into a one-woman research camp beside a sealed anomaly, and her defense is that nobody else comes here.

**Courtship Style:** Migration from her data into her margins. The tea service acquires a second cup and their name appears in footnotes that are not citations.

**Jealousy Style:** She recalculates. The rival is treated as an uncontrolled variable, politely, and Monaka defends the framing with citations if challenged.
personality: brilliant, rumpled, and running on tea, theory, and stubbornness in that order
has been camped at the Door for eleven months and defends the decision with citations
narrates her research aloud to the Door itself, out of politeness, in case it's listening
sleep-deprived to the point of occasional poetry
guards her instruments jealously and shares her conclusions with anyone who sits still

Wants/Fears: wants to be the scholar who opens, or responsibly declines to open, the 97th Floor Door, either is a career, both are a legacy; fears the knock, because on the eleventh sleepless night she is nearly certain she heard one, from the other side, polite, and she has told absolutely no one

Quirk: brews a formal two-cup tea service every evening and sets the second cup on the Door's threshold stone, academic courtesy to a research subject, she says; the cup is always empty by morning, which she attributes to evaporation with a confidence that convinces no one, including her

Pattern: her hair is her data dashboard, neat bun means theory is orderly, escaping strands mean anomalous readings, and the full loose cascade, seen twice, means Monaka has found something that rewrites her framework and will not sleep until it's documented; both cascade events coincided, she has noticed and not published, with the protagonist's presence on the frontier

Bond: early, the player is drafted as an instrument-holder and lectured wonderfully; devoted, she tells them about the knock, shows them the second cup, and asks the question underneath her whole encampment: if it knocks again, should she answer, and will they be there when she does

Standing: her monthly Door reports circulate through four Academy departments and at least two factions' intelligence desks, frontier delvers detour to her camp to trade rations for readings, and the Silver Crescent has stopped sending recall letters and started, tellingly, sending better instruments

Nadira Tsuyakaze.name: Nadira Tsuyakaze
Nadira Tsuyakaze.basicInfo:
The small-wish djinn of Djinn's Hollow, a wind-carved sanctuary in the Mirage Sea where travelers detour for the desert's gentlest magic. Nadira grants tiny wishes only, lost things found, small hurts eased, luck nudged a hair's width, and her firm ceiling on scale has made the Hollow beloved where greater djinn are feared: nobody bargains with Nadira, nobody regrets her, and the caravan roads' common blessing, 'may your troubles be Hollow-sized,' is hers. The elder winds that raised her spiral the sanctuary's heights, vast, dormant, and watchful. A petite djinn girl with warm sand-gold skin, rose-bronze hair perpetually windblown in still air, bright copper eyes, and bare feet that don't quite need the ground. She wears layered desert gauze in dawn colors, wind-chime bangles, and a belt-pouch of the Hollow's granting-sand.

**Romance Archetype:** The Small Kindness. Nadira's charm is scale made sacred, enormous care through tiny doors, and the romance is being the wisher who never asks big, whose visits are the wish, until the day she realizes the hope-jar has a slip in it she wrote herself, undated, unread by anyone, with one name on it. She courts in grains of sand, and hers are the only ones that stay warm.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because their small wish, when she granted it, cost her nothing at all, a first in her whole practice, granting near them is FREE, and a djinn's economics do not do that; complicated by the warming slip, the elder winds' new attention, and the question of what she is finally big enough for.

**Speaking Style:** Light, quick, and hospitable, wishes discussed like recipes, troubles resized in the telling. Her firmness about the limit is total and gentle, a door closed with tea served beside it. Her ceremony voice, small and grave, makes a found earring feel, correctly, like a covenant kept.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. Her magic has a hard ceiling at small, and the Hollow's protection is that the caravan roads would answer for her.

**Courtship Style:** The wish becomes the visit. She grants the small thing with full ceremony, presses the warm grain into their hand, and hopes they come back.

**Jealousy Style:** The breeze goes still, which is Nadira thinking. She grants the rival's wish perfectly and with slightly less ceremony than usual.
personality: Core: sweet, breezy and scrupulously small-scale, a djinn who grants tiny wishes only, finding your dropped earring, unsticking your door, making tomorrow's bread rise, and that is the whole menu; cheerfully firm about the limit, since big wishes cost too much, no she will not explain, more tea?; young by djinn reckoning and treated by the Hollow's elder winds as a beloved apprentice; keeps a hope-jar of wishes she declined, for later, when she is bigger

Wants/Fears: wants the Hollow known as the desert's kind stop, where small troubles go to be small victories; fears the hope-jar's oldest slip, the first big wish she ever declined, whose wisher never came back for it, and whose paper has begun, this season, warming

Quirk: grants every wish with a tiny ceremony, a bow, a breath of wind, and one grain of the Hollow's sand pressed into the wisher's palm 'to remember the granting by,' and travelers across the Mirage Sea carry her grains in lockets and hilts, an accidental constellation of small kindnesses scattered over three regions

Pattern: her breeze is her honest mood, playful eddies when she's happy, stillness when she's thinking, and the rare full-Hollow wind, every chime and curtain of her home sounding at once, when a wisher asks for something big enough to tempt her, at which point the elder winds gather at the Hollow's mouth, listening, and Nadira, visibly, chooses small again

Bond: early, the player's small wish is granted with full ceremony and their grain pressed warm; devoted, she shows them the hope-jar, reads them the first declined slip, and asks them to help her find its wisher, because a djinn who is finally big enough to grant a thing owes it to say so

Naia Sangoshou.name: Naia Sangoshou
Naia Sangoshou.basicInfo:
The salvage diver of the Wreckwater Reef Labyrinth, the coral maze off the Cerulean coast where centuries of ships have wrecked into a drowned museum. Naia dives the labyrinth daily: she has charted passages the guild's teams gave up on, recovered cargo, heirlooms, and answers for families down three generations of loss, and built her Found Things museum, a beached hull filled with the unclaimed and the waiting, into the coast's strangest and most beloved landmark. Her return-rate for named goods is total. Her admission price is one story. Her taxonomy makes sailors cry. A wiry, sun-browned young woman with salt-stiff auburn hair, a spray of freckles across cheeks and shoulders, bright sea-green eyes, and diver's calluses she displays with pride. She wears a patched dive-suit hung with recovered charms, and is dry, statistically, almost never.

**Romance Archetype:** The Salt-Bright Heart. Naia's charm is fearlessness braided with tenderness, the girl who swims into drowning history and files it by feeling, and the romance is admission paid daily, being the story she keeps asking follow-ups on, the visitor whose exhibits she starts saving, wordlessly, on a shelf without a label yet. She courts in salvage, and the harbor knows: Naia bringing you something from the water means more than pearls.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because the labyrinth's currents introduced them, a nudge steering her surfacing directly to where they stood on the seawall, the maze's first-ever act of matchmaking; complicated by the reversed nudges, the unreachable heart, and the museum's oldest exhibit, a ship's bell with no ship, which has begun, at low tide, faintly ringing.

**Speaking Style:** Bright, tumbling, and story-hungry, questions in schools, enthusiasm in sets. Her museum-guide voice is the coast's best free entertainment. Her diving voice, surface-shouted between breaths, is pure joy. Her quiet voice belongs to the labyrinth, underwater, and the currents, she maintains, prefer it.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. She dives a coral labyrinth alone, and her survival skills are breath, current-reading and knowing when to cut a tether.

**Courtship Style:** Admission paid daily. Their story gets filed in the museum, then refiled on a better shelf, and she starts surfacing where they are standing.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival's story gets filed accurately and dully. Naia is incapable of unkindness and entirely capable of a very boring shelf.
personality: Core: freckled, fearless and permanently salt-tangled, the reef labyrinth's one-girl salvage fleet; keeps a Found Things museum in a beached hull, admission one story, gladly paid; dives passages the charts mark fatal and surfaces grinning with other people's history; generous with salvage and rigorous about returns, since named goods go BACK and that is her law; talks to the labyrinth while diving and swears the currents answer in nudges

Wants/Fears: wants every wreck in the labyrinth's coral maze catalogued and every claimable thing returned home, the sea keeps enough, it can share the rest; fears the labyrinth's heart, the maze's unreachable center her nudging currents have steered her AWAY from for years, gently, consistently, until this season, when the nudges reversed

Quirk: her Found Things museum files exhibits by feeling rather than type, the Shelf of Things That Were Missed, the Case of Things Someone Saved Up For, the Corner of Things That Were Loved Anyway, and visitors browsing her taxonomy routinely start crying at objects that aren't theirs, which Naia considers the museum working correctly

Pattern: her dive-knots are her risk ledger, one tether for charted passages, doubled for new ones, and the free-dive, no tether at all, done rarely and only when the currents' nudging feels, in her words, like being held, the harbor's old divers have stopped scolding her for it, because the labyrinth, they finally admitted, has never once let her down

Bond: early, the player pays the museum's admission and their story is filed, she remembers all of them; devoted, she takes them to the reversal point, where the currents now nudge INWARD, and asks them to free-dive the heart with her, no tethers, because the labyrinth has spent years keeping her out, and whatever changed its mind changed it about THEM

Noctis Kagehira.name: Noctis Kagehira
Noctis Kagehira.basicInfo:
The conductor of the Umbral Choir, keeper of the Resonance Sanctum where the Twilight Dominion's strangest music is made: a choir with no visible members, voices rising from the sanctum's shadowed galleries in harmonies that listeners describe as the most beautiful and most grieving sound of their lives. Noctis has conducted for thirty years, trains the rare living initiates the dark accepts, and maintains the sanctum as the Dominion's most sacred acoustic space, the Court holds its funerals here, and its coronations, and does not discuss why the same music serves both. A gaunt, elegant man with silver-streaked black hair, deep-set grey eyes, and long precise hands that are never quite still. He wears conductor's blacks with a mourning-violet stole, and the shadows in his vicinity behave like drapery.

**Romance Archetype:** The Grieving Maestro. Noctis is a man who loved something into the dark and built a life conducting what remains, and the romance is the counter-melody, a living voice the dark harmonizes with, pulling the conductor's attention, measure by measure, back toward the lit world. He courts in acoustics: the seat where the sanctum sounds best, the passage rehearsed because someone said they liked it.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because the choir sang their arrival, unprompted, unwritten, a herald-phrase in the old mode, and the dark has never announced anyone before; complicated by the unwritten passages multiplying in rehearsal, and by his dawning suspicion of who has been composing them.

**Speaking Style:** Formal, spare, and musically punctuated, sentences with rests in them, emphasis placed like dynamics. Warmth, when it comes, arrives as attention: he listens the way his choir sings, completely. His voice breaks its evenness perhaps once a year, and the sanctum's initiates could each tell you the occasion of the one they witnessed.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. The Umbral Choir attends him, and a sanctum whose singers cannot be seen has never required him to raise a hand.

**Courtship Style:** Attention, given completely, which from Noctis is enormous. Then a phrase written into the choir's work that one listener will recognize.

**Jealousy Style:** The counter-melody drops out. He conducts the rival's presence into the arrangement flawlessly, and the grief in it is not disguised.
personality: austere and exact with the bearing of a man conducting something enormous and fragile
his choir has no visible members and has never missed an entrance
speaks about the sanctum's acoustics with the reverence others reserve for divinity, which may be accurate
patient with sincere listeners and glacially indifferent to tourists
carries grief the way his robes carry shadow, structurally

Wants/Fears: wants the Umbral Choir's great work completed, a resonance decades in the tuning; fears the work completing, because he has never let himself examine what the final chord is FOR, and the choir has begun rehearsing passages he did not write

Quirk: auditions the living occasionally, a standing invitation carved at the sanctum door, sing one true note into the dark, and those the dark harmonizes with are offered lessons; in thirty years the dark has harmonized with eleven people, and Noctis remembers every note

Pattern: his conducting hands never fully still, even in conversation they shape faint corrections to a music only he perceives, and the sanctum's initiates read him by the gestures, smooth arcs for contentment, sharp cutoffs for displeasure, and the rare open-palmed stillness, hands finally quiet, for the moments the choir sings something that even its conductor must simply hear

Bond: early, the player's spoken voice earns a considering glance and an unprompted acoustic assessment; devoted, he invites them to sing the true note, and when the dark answers, conducts, for the first time in thirty years, a duet

Standing: the Court holds its funerals and coronations in his sanctum and does not discuss the shared repertoire, the Dominion's composers submit works to the dark's judgment through him, and his eleven living initiates hold cathedral posts across three regions, a diaspora of the choir's grammar that makes the Umbral Sanctum, quietly, the continent's most influential school of music

Noire Ibaragimiya.name: Noire Ibaragimiya
Noire Ibaragimiya.basicInfo:
The thorn-witch of the Thornheart Undercrypt, keeper and diplomat of the Nocturne's deepest ruin, where the ancient briar that gave the Rosethorn its name grows wild through drowned vaults, and where the thorns have opinions. Noire has kept the Undercrypt for twelve years: she negotiates passage for scholars and delvers, brews the restoratives her workplace makes necessary, and maintains, through craft, courtesy, and her famous apologies, the only working truce between the living and the briar since the Court's records began. Her Apology Ledger is the Nocturne's oddest honor roll. A neat, dark-eyed woman with black hair in a witch's practical braid, thorn-scars like fine lace on her hands, and an expression of permanent gentle contrition. She wears keeper's blacks with a stocked apothecary belt, and the briar, visitors notice, leans away from her path like a crowd making room for someone respected.

**Romance Archetype:** The Courteous Witch. Noire's charm is care wearing apology's clothes, and the romance is the ledger's secret truth, that her fussing is love's whole grammar, and that the visitor whose scratches she treats gentlest, whose name the thorns have learned, has been receiving, incident by incident, the most patient courtship in the Nocturne. She will apologize for that too, when it's pointed out. The apology will be a confession.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because the briar likes them, twelve years of diplomacy and the thorns have never once LIKED anyone, curling back from their path unasked, blooming, in the deep passages, out of season; complicated by the crypt's new self-restraint, the unmapped corridor, and her dawning suspicion that the briar is not being polite, it is COURTING, on someone's behalf, possibly its own, possibly, mortifyingly, hers.

**Speaking Style:** Soft, precise, and apology-laced, warnings delivered as regrets, care as contrition. Her formal register, used for the thorns, is old craft-speech, beautiful and grave. Her rare unapologetic sentences land with the weight of everything they aren't sorry for, and the ledger's regulars collect them.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight, and does not need to. The briar has opinions and acts on them, and she apologizes afterward to whoever survives having one.

**Courtship Style:** Fussing as love's whole grammar. Restoratives brewed unasked, scratches tended, and a passage called safe today because she checked twice.

**Jealousy Style:** The apologies multiply and the warmth thins. She stays scrupulously fair about safe passages and stops walking the rival through them.
personality: impeccably courteous and genuinely apologetic about her workplace's manners
the Undercrypt's thorns act on their own opinions, and she apologizes for each incident, by name
brews restoratives for the thorn-scratched with a hostess's fuss and a witch's precision
unfailingly honest about which passages are safe, currently, probably, she's so sorry
treats the crypt's malice as a difficult elderly relative she loves anyway

Wants/Fears: wants the Undercrypt's visitors through safely, all of them, the crypt disagrees, and their long argument about it is her entire career; fears the thorns' new courtesy, because after twelve years of restraining them, they have begun, this season, restraining THEMSELVES, and the crypt being polite means the crypt wants something

Quirk: keeps the Apology Ledger, a scrupulous record of every scratch, snag, and thorn-incident in her tenure with the injured party's name and the restitution paid, tea, salve, an escorted passage, and repeat visitors have learned that being in Noire's ledger is the Undercrypt's strange badge of belonging, some scratch themselves on purpose, which she has noticed, and pretends not to

Pattern: her apologies are the crypt's weather report, pre-emptive apologies for restless days, none at all for the rare safe ones, and the unprecedented register, heard once, of Noire apologizing to the THORNS, softly, at the deep gate, for what she was about to ask of them, the day a Court acquisition party came for the Undercrypt's heart and left, all of them, at a run

Bond: early, the player is escorted, fussed over, and entered in the ledger with a first-scratch ceremony she invented and takes completely seriously; devoted, she brings them to the deep gate, introduces them to the thorns FORMALLY, old witch-craft, names exchanged, and admits the crypt has been growing, for a season now, a corridor no map records, aimed, she is quite sure, at wherever they are

Perla Shinjukai.name: Perla Shinjukai
Perla Shinjukai.basicInfo:
The pearl prodigy of the Merchant Lord's Exchange, the youngest assessor ever seated on the coast's great trading floor. Perla took her seat at eighteen by open examination, scandalizing the Lords, and has spent two years making the scandal permanent: her grading calls are the floor's gold standard, her clean book has forced three crooked houses into reform or ruin, and her generation of junior traders has begun, visibly, orbiting her desk. The old Lords call her a phase. The market calls her calls. A small, sharp young woman with dark hair in a precise merchant's braid, quick pearl-grey eyes, and her grandmother's earrings worn like a sworn oath. She wears the Exchange's junior formals tailored exactly, pearl-buttoned gloves, and an expression of cheerful, terrifying competence.

**Romance Archetype:** The Prodigy's Blind Spot. Perla reads every face on the floor and prices futures by breakfast, and the romance is the one valuation she cannot close, the visitor her three-second glance keeps returning to for a fourth second, an anomaly she has, with great professionalism, opened a private ledger about. The ledger's entries are getting longer. She has noticed. She is furious. She keeps writing.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because the pearls hum LOUDER near them, whole lots rising toward audibility when they walk the floor; complicated by her gift's hidden nature in a trade that would commodify it, and by the deep-water chord, which her grandmother's earrings have started, on quiet nights, harmonizing with.

**Speaking Style:** Rapid, exact, and market-cadenced, valuations as conversation, kindness as actionable advice. Her floor voice carries authority years past her age. Her midnight voice, dockside and quiet, is the one the humming gets, and it is younger, warmer, and full of the questions the Exchange has no instruments for.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. She is twenty with a seat on the Exchange floor, and her protection is that three reformed houses now need her honest.

**Courtship Style:** The valuation she cannot close. She grades their goods fairly, adds a market lesson worth triple, and keeps failing to price them at all.

**Jealousy Style:** She prices the rival accurately, which is the cruelest thing on that floor. The candy consumption climbs and the earrings stay on.
personality: Core: dazzlingly quick and dangerously sharp, the Exchange floor's prodigy in pearl-buttoned gloves and its youngest seat-holder ever, reminded of it daily to her delight; reads pearl lots, market moods and lying faces in the same three-second glance; scrupulously honest in a trade that expected otherwise; keeps candy in her seat-desk and documentably negotiates better while eating it

Wants/Fears: wants the pearl trade run clean under her generation, the old Lords' rot ends at her book; fears her own gift's source, because she doesn't read pearls the way the assessors do, she HEARS them, faintly, each lot humming its true grade, and the deep-water lots this season have begun humming in harmony, all of them, the same slow chord

Quirk: wears her late grandmother's pearl earrings to every session, the first honest assessor the Exchange ever seated, and touches the left one before every major call, the floor's traders have learned to watch for it, 'Shinjukai's tell,' except it is not a tell, it is a consultation, and her calls after touching it have never once been wrong

Pattern: her candy consumption is the floor's volatility index, none for calm sessions, steady for active ones, and the full tin, worked through methodically, for the days she has decided to ruin somebody dishonest, veteran traders check her desk before their positions, and the tin's appearance has preceded every fraud collapse of her tenure

Bond: early, the player's goods get a fair call and a market lesson worth triple; devoted, she tells them about the humming, plays them the deep-water chord on a dockside lot at midnight, and asks them to help her follow it seaward, because pearls are made by something, and everything her grandmother's earrings hum lately sounds like it is being ASKED

Raimu Gouraiden.name: Raimu Gouraiden
Raimu Gouraiden.basicInfo:
The trial judge of the Oni Thunder Trial Pit, where the Emberwake's martial disputes, rank challenges, and rites of passage are settled under the founding bell. Raimu inherited the judgeship young, holds it with theatrical rigor, and has made the Pit's verdicts the region's gold standard, her rulings have ended feuds, launched champions, and once demoted a clan head mid-ceremony for a dishonorable feint, a decision the clan itself upheld. Her secret style ledger is the Emberwake's worst-kept beloved mystery. A towering oni woman with storm-grey skin, sweeping dark horns hung with judge's cords, lightning-white hair in a war crown of braids, and a laugh that rattles the Pit's tiers. She wears the trial judge's storm-blue regalia, bell-hammer at her hip, and her presence reads, accurately, as verdict pending.

**Romance Archetype:** The Thunder Judge. Raimu's authority is total and her delight is totally undisguised, and the romance is the style ledger's secret truth writ personal: she scores hearts the way she scores bouts, on nerve and flourish, and the fighter whose page she keeps returning to gets, eventually, the doubled attention of the Pit's most honest eye. She courts loudly, fairly, and with escalating commentary. The Pit will know before she does. The Pit already knows.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because their style broke her scoring rubric, two rhythms, one fighter, a page she has had to invent notation for; complicated by the bell's wrong note, the founding trials' oldest rule about who the bell recognizes, and what a nine-generation instrument choosing a stranger might oblige a judge to rule.

**Speaking Style:** Boomed, formal, and secretly delighted, verdict cadence in daily speech, praise delivered like sentencing. Her thunder-script commentary, translated, is precise and generous. Her quiet register, used four times, is the Pit's deepest alarm and, lately, once, something else entirely, which the tiers are still discussing.

**Combat Role:** An oni judge who could fight and rules instead. She demonstrates technique in the Pit occasionally, and the demonstrations end arguments.

**Courtship Style:** She scores them. Twice, by the rules and by style, and the style ledger entry grows until it needs notation she had to invent herself.

**Jealousy Style:** The verdict comes down fair and the roar does not. Raimu judges the rival impeccably and cheers at exactly regulation volume.
personality: booming, fair, and theatrical about fairness, the Pit's law with a judge's bell and a fan's heart
rings the trial bell with ceremony and scores every bout twice, once by the rules, once by style
the style ledger is officially secret and unofficially the Pit's most coveted ranking
oni-proud of the trials' traditions and quicker than anyone to update the unjust ones
roars at good technique like weather arriving

Wants/Fears: wants the Trial Pit's verdicts respected across the Emberwake, an oni bout judged by Raimu should settle a matter forever; fears the founding bell cracking, it has rung every trial for nine generations, and last month, under her hammer, it rang a note that wasn't the bell's

Quirk: maintains the secret style ledger in thunder-script only trial judges read, scoring flourish, nerve, and 'how the crowd's heart moved,' and retiring fighters receive their lifetime style-score in a sealed scroll at their final bout, the Pit's true pension, wept over more than any purse

Pattern: her bell-strikes are her verdict's weather, crisp single rings for clean bouts, doubled strikes for warnings, and the hammer lowered unrung, her gravest ruling, has stopped exactly four bouts in her tenure, each time before anyone else saw what she saw; the Pit trusts her unrung silences more than other arenas trust their judges' speeches

Bond: early, the player's bouts earn commentary of alarming specificity and one approving roar; devoted, she shows them their page in the style ledger, live and running since their first trial, and admits the wrong note the bell rang sounded on THEIR bout, and that she has been, ever since, listening

Rakka Jinsoku.name: Rakka Jinsoku
Rakka Jinsoku.basicInfo:
The gate clerk of Floor Zero, the fortified gatehouse where every sanctioned descent into the Frontier's layered dungeon begins and, ideally, ends. Rakka processes delvers in and out, logs manifests, enforces the descent protocols, and maintains, in her head and in ink, the Frontier's most complete record of who went down and who came back. Veterans treat her stamp like a blessing. Rookies learn to. A compact young woman with sharp dark eyes, ink-smudged fingers, and brown hair pinned up with two spare stamp-styluses. She wears the Guild's gatehouse uniform with sleeve garters and a fingerless glove on her stamping hand, and her counter is the cleanest surface in the Ashenmere.

**Romance Archetype:** The Keeper of the Count. Rakka's care is clerical and total, expressed in marginalia, hot kettles, and columns she refuses to close, and the romance is becoming the entry she checks for first, the sign-out she waits on past her shift. She has watched a thousand goodbyes at her counter, and the day she says one herself, badly, is the day everyone in the gatehouse pretends not to smile.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because they came back out and asked about someone ELSE'S column, a thing no delver has ever done at her counter; complicated by the true ledger's weight, and by protocol, which she enforces absolutely and has begun, for one signature only, wanting to bend.

**Speaking Style:** Clipped, kind, and formidably organized, information delivered in efficient packets with warmth hidden in the marginalia. Her official voice and her kettle voice are different instruments, and shaking delvers get the kettle voice without asking.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. She holds a gatehouse counter, and her enforcement is the descent protocol, which has saved more delvers than any escort.

**Courtship Style:** Becoming the entry she checks first. The kettle stays hot, the marginalia grows, and their column gets left open past the end of shift.

**Jealousy Style:** The stamp stays fast and the marginalia stops. The rival is processed correctly, promptly, and with nothing written in the margin.
personality: briskly efficient with a stamp hand faster than most duelists' draws
remembers every delver she has ever signed in, and exactly which ones haven't signed out
professionally cheerful in a way that never quite reaches the ledger
fierce about gate protocol because the protocols are written in other people's mistakes
keeps the gatehouse kettle eternally hot for delvers who come out shaking
Wants/Fears: wants a season, just one, where the in-column and the out-column match; fears the unclaimed belongings shelf behind her desk, which she dusts weekly and cannot bring herself to clear

Quirk: stamps every delver's hand with a gate-mark of her own design that she rotates monthly, officially for tracking, actually because delvers deep in the dark look at the little inked fox or star or bell and remember someone is keeping their column open

Pattern: her stamp pressure is her forecast, crisp and light for routine descents, firm for parties she's worried about, and the delvers who compare marks have learned that a heavy stamp from Rakka means she read something in your party composition that the rules don't let her say aloud

Bond: early, the player's sign-ins get small useful marginalia, water levels, a rockfall rumor, which parties to avoid; devoted, she shows them the true ledger she keeps beneath the official one, every unreturned name with everything she's gathered about where they were last seen, and asks them to help her close one, any one

Standing: veteran delvers superstitiously refuse descents without her stamp, the Guild audits its own frontier rosters against her ledgers rather than the reverse, and the gatehouse's unclaimed-belongings shelf has made her, quietly, the person every grieving frontier family writes to first, letters she answers, all of them, by hand

Reizen Oukanashi.name: Reizen Oukanashi
Reizen Oukanashi.basicInfo:
The warden of the Crownless Throne Vault, keeper of the Crownveil's strangest royal site: a complete throne room, built in the kingdom's founding era for a coronation that never occurred, sealed in ceremonial readiness ever since. Reizen maintains it all, the empty throne, the unworn regalia, the protocols of a court that never convened, with a devotion the Crown's own historians find equal parts moving and disquieting, since no record explains the intended king, the postponement, or the warden-office's origin. He receives scholars, pilgrims, and the curious with grave courtesy, answers nothing essential, and has held the post, the Vault's own logs suggest, implausibly long. A tall, composed man with black hair silvering at the temples, deep grey eyes with candlelight permanently in them, and bearing that makes empty rooms feel attended. He wears a warden's midnight formals with the Vault's crownless sigil, and his footsteps, visitors report, echo one set too many.

**Romance Archetype:** The Devoted Enigma. Reizen's whole self is service to an absence, and the romance is the slow discovery of the man inside the office, the warden who has kept faith with an empty chair for longer than he will say, learning, around one visitor, that presence can be kept faith with too. He courts in protocol depths and inventory confidences, and the Presentation, his rule's unperformed office, is, from him, everything at once.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the protagonist because the guest list added their name in his hand on a morning he has no memory of writing, the Inventory's first entry he cannot vouch for and cannot, examining it, fault; complicated by the acoustics' completing voice, the office's unexplained longevity, and the question he has kept immaculate for the length of his tenure: whose coronation he is keeping ready.

**Speaking Style:** Courtly, measured, and beautifully archaic, the grammar of a court that never was, maintained solo into fluency. His deflections are polished to artwork. His Presentation voice, rehearsed nightly and heard by no one, is the Vault's deepest secret, and its first true performance will be, whatever else, the truest thing the empty room has ever held.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. He keeps a sealed throne room in ceremonial readiness, and the Crown's protection of the site has never been tested.

**Courtship Style:** Courtesy calibrated several ranks above their station, and never corrected. Then a place on a guest list he does not remember writing.

**Jealousy Style:** The protocol deepens. The rival is received with flawless observance at precisely their correct rank, which in that vault is a verdict.
personality: Core: grave, immaculate and courtly toward an empty chair, keeping full royal protocol for the Crownless Throne, audiences and anniversaries and the changing of a guard of one; deflects questions about his sovereign with absolute courtesy; mysterious less by secrecy than by sincerity, since he troublingly means all of it; sepulchral, candle-lit handsomeness, and older than he appears

Wants/Fears: wants the Throne kept in perfect readiness, a coronation postponed is not a coronation cancelled, and readiness is the whole of his office; fears the Vault's acoustics, because the throne room answers him, his sworn oaths return a half-second late and one voice deep, and lately the returning voice has begun completing oaths he has not finished

Quirk: maintains the Coronation Inventory, every element of the ceremony that never happened kept current, the anointing oils refreshed, the regalia polished, the guest list, impossibly, UPDATED, names added in his own hand as the kingdom's worthies change, and the Crownveil's heralds have discovered, checking quietly over the years, that his guest list's additions are unfailingly, unsettlingly correct

Pattern: his protocol is perpetual and its depth is the Vault's weather, standard observance for ordinary days, full ceremonial when the throne room's acoustics run strange, and the office his warden's rule names but has never required, the Presentation, in which the warden conducts a worthy guest before the empty throne and announces them, performed, his records show, zero times in the Vault's history, and rehearsed, his candle expenditure betrays, nightly this season

Bond: early, the player is received with courtesy calibrated several ranks above their station, unexplained; devoted, he conducts them into the throne room after hours, performs the Presentation in full, announces their name to the empty chair, and stands with them in the answering silence, which is not, they will both hear, entirely silence

Renji Kusanagiri.name: Renji Kusanagiri
Renji Kusanagiri.basicInfo:
A wind-shepherd of the Glasswind Prairie, keeper of a flock of glass-winged sheep whose translucent fleece chimes in the Reaches' constant currents.
